body.text: paribhāṣā
body.translated_text: Definitions

children.text: prītim bhakta-janasya yas @janayate vighnam vinighnan smṛtas tam vṛndāraka-vṛnda-vandita-padam @natvā mataṅga-ānanam/
children.translated_text: Having bowed to the elephant-faced one (<s>Gaṇeśa</s>), whose feet are worshipped by hosts of gods, who when remembered destroys all obstacles and produces joy in his devotees,

children.text: pāṭīm sat-gaṇitasya @vacmi catura-prīti-pradām prasphuṭām saṃkṣipta-akṣara-komala-amala-padais lālitya-līlāvatīm//[śārdūlavikrīḍita]
children.translated_text: I speak this <s>pāṭī</s> (arithmetic) of good mathematics, clearly delightful, giving pleasure to the intelligent, the charming <s>Līlāvatī</s>, with concise, soft, and pure words.

children.text: varāṭakānām %daśaka-%dvayam 20 yad sā kākiṇī tās ca paṇas %catasras/
children.translated_text: Twenty <s>varāṭakas</s> (cowrie-shells) make one <s>kākiṇī</s>; four of those make a <s>paṇa</s>;

children.text: te %ṣoḍaśa drammas iha avagamyas drammais tathā %ṣoḍaśabhis ca niṣkas//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: sixteen of those are to be understood here as a <s>dramma</s>; and with sixteen <s>drammas</s>, a <s>niṣka</s>.

children.text: tulyā yavābhyām kathitā atra guñjā vallas %tri-guñjas dharaṇam ca te %aṣṭau/
children.translated_text: A <s>guñjā</s> is said here to be equal to two barley-grains; a <s>valla</s> is three <s>guñjās</s>; and eight of those make a <s>dharaṇa</s>.

children.text: gadyāṇakas tad-%dvayam #indra-14-tulyais vallais tathā %ekas ghaṭakas pradiṣṭas//[indravajrā]
children.translated_text: A <s>gadyāṇaka</s> is two of those; with <s>vallas</s> equal to fourteen, one <s>ghaṭaka</s> is prescribed.

children.text: %daśa-%ardha-guñjam @pravadanti māṣam māṣa-āhvayais %ṣoḍaśabhis ca karṣam/
children.translated_text: They call five and a half <s>guñjās</s> a <s>māṣa</s>; and with sixteen <s>māṣas</s>, a <s>karṣa</s>.

children.text: karṣais %caturbhis ca palam tulā-jñāḥ karṣam suvarṇasya suvarṇa-saṃjñam//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: Those who know weights [say] four <s>karṣas</s> make a <s>pala</s>; a <s>karṣa</s> of gold is called a <s>suvarṇa</s>.

children.text: yava-udarais aṅgulam %aṣṭa-saṃkhyais hastas aṅgulais %ṣaṣ-guṇitais %caturbhis/[āpaṭe: aguṅlam < aṅgulam]
children.translated_text: Eight barley-grains placed widthwise make a finger-breadth (<s>aṅgula</s>); a cubit (<s>hasta</s>) is twenty-four finger-breadths;

children.text: hastais %caturbhis @bhavati iha daṇḍas krośas %sahasra-%dvitayena teṣām//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: four cubits here make a staff (<s>daṇḍa</s>); and two thousand of those make a <s>krośa</s> (league).

children.text: @syāt yojanam krośa-%catuṣṭayena tathā karāṇām %daśakena vaṃśas/
children.translated_text: A <s>yojana</s> is four <s>krośas</s>; and ten cubits make a bamboo-length (<s>vaṃśa</s>);

children.text: nivartanam %viṃśati-vaṃśa-saṃkhyais kṣetram %caturbhis ca bhujais nibaddham//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: a <s>nivartana</s> (land measure) is twenty <s>vaṃśas</s> [squared]; and a field is bounded by four sides.

children.text: hasta-unmitais vistṛti-dairghya-piṇḍais yat %dvādaśa-asram ghana-hasta-saṃjñam/
children.translated_text: That which is twelve-edged, measured by cubit-dimensions in breadth, length, and volume, is called a cubic cubit (<s>ghana-hasta</s>);

children.text: dhānya-ādike yat ghana-hasta-mānam śāstra-uditā māgadha-khārikā sā//[indravajrā]
children.translated_text: that cubic cubit measure for grain and the like is the <s>Māgadha khārikā</s>, as stated in the treatise.

children.text: droṇas tu khāryās khalu %ṣoḍaśa-aṃśas @syāt āḍhakas droṇa-%caturtha-bhāgas/
children.translated_text: A <s>droṇa</s> is indeed one-sixteenth of a <s>khārī</s>; an <s>āḍhaka</s> is a quarter of a <s>droṇa</s>;

children.text: prasthas %caturtha-aṃśas iha āḍhakasya prastha-#aṅghris ādyais kuḍavas pradiṣṭas//[indravajrā]
children.translated_text: a <s>prastha</s> is a quarter of an <s>āḍhaka</s>; a quarter of a <s>prastha</s> is prescribed as a <s>kuḍava</s>.

children.text: #pāda-ūna-gadyāṇaka-tulya-ṭaṅkais %dvi-%sapta-tulyais kathitas atra seras/
children.translated_text: A <s>sera</s> is described here as equal to fourteen <s>ṭaṅkas</s>, [each being] a <s>gadyāṇaka</s> less a quarter;

children.text: maṇa-abhidhānam #kha-#yugais ca serais dhānya-ādi-taulyeṣu turuṣka-saṃjñā//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: and what is called a <s>maṇa</s> is ten <s>seras</s>, and the <s>Turuṣka</s> designation is for weighing grain and the like.

children.text: śeṣā kāla-ādi-paribhāṣā lokatas prasiddhā jñeyā/ iti paribhāṣā//
children.translated_text: The remaining definitions of time and so forth are to be known as well-established from common usage. Thus ends the Definitions.

body.text: parikarma-aṣṭaka
body.translated_text: The Eight Operations

body.text: atha saṃkhyā-sthāna-nirṇayas/
body.translated_text: Now, the determination of number-places.

children.text: līlā-gala-lulat-lola-kāla-vyāla-vilāsine/
children.translated_text: Homage to <s>Gaṇeśa</s>, who sports with the terrible serpent swinging playfully on the neck of <s>Līlā</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>),

children.text: gaṇeśāya namas nīla-kamala-amala-kāntaye//[śloka]
children.translated_text: who has the pure beauty of a blue lotus.

children.text: %eka-%daśa-%śata-%sahasra-%ayuta-%lakṣa-%prayuta-%koṭayas kramaśas/
children.translated_text: Units, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten-thousands (<s>ayuta</s>), hundred-thousands (<s>lakṣa</s>), millions (<s>prayuta</s>), ten-millions (<s>koṭi</s>), in order;

children.text: %arbudam %abjam %kharva-%nikharva-%mahāpadma-%śaṅkavas tasmāt//[gīti]
children.translated_text: then <s>arbuda</s>, <s>abja</s>, <s>kharva</s>, <s>nikharva</s>, <s>mahāpadma</s>, <s>śaṅku</s>,

children.text: %jaladhis ca %antyam %madhyam %parārdham iti %daśa-guṇa-uttarās saṃjñās/
children.translated_text: ocean (<s>jaladhi</s>), <s>antya</s>, <s>madhya</s>, and <s>parārdha</s> — these are the designations of the places of numbers, each ten times greater [than the preceding],

children.text: saṃkhyāyās sthānānām vyavahāra-artham kṛtās pūrvais//[āryā]
children.translated_text: made by the ancients for the purpose of practical use.

body.text: iti saṃkhyā-sthāna-nirṇayas// atha saṃkalita-vyavakalite/ atha saṃkalita-vyavakalitayos karaṇa-sūtram vṛtta-%ardham/
body.translated_text: Thus ends the determination of number-places. Now, addition and subtraction. The rule-verse for addition and subtraction, half a verse:

body.text: kāryas kramāt utkramatas atha vā aṅka-yogas yathā-sthānakam antaram vā/[indravajrā-ab; cd=14a]
body.translated_text: The sum of digits should be made in order or in reverse order, place by place; or [find] the difference.

body.text: atra uddeśakas/
body.translated_text: Here is the example:

children.text: aye bāle līlāvati mati-mati @brūhi sahitān %dvi-%pañca-%dvātriṃśat-%trinavati-%śata-%aṣṭādaśa %daśa/
children.translated_text: O girl <s>Līlāvatī</s>, of keen intellect, tell me the sum of two, five, thirty-two, one hundred and ninety-three, eighteen, and ten,

children.text: %śata-upetān etān %ayuta-viyutān ca api @vada me yadi vyakte yukti-vyavakalana-mārge @asi kuśalā//[śikhariṇī]
children.translated_text: together with one hundred; and tell me also these subtracted from ten thousand — if you are skilled in the method of addition and subtraction in arithmetic.

body.text: nyāsas/ 2/ 5/ 32/ 193/ 18/ 10/ 100/ saṃyojanāt jātam/ 360/ %ayutāt 10000 śodhite jātam 9640/ iti saṃkalita-vyavakalite// atha guṇana-prakāras/ guṇane karaṇa-sūtram sa-%ardha-vṛtta-%dvayam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: 2, 5, 32, 193, 18, 10, 100. By addition the result is 360. Subtracted from 10000, the result is 9640. Thus ends addition and subtraction. Now the method of multiplication. The rule-verse for multiplication, two and a half verses:

children.text: guṇya-antyam aṅkam guṇakena @hanyāt utsāritena evam upāntima-ādīn//[indravajrā-cd; ab=12]
children.translated_text: Multiply the last digit of the multiplicand by the multiplier shifted [to its position]; similarly [multiply] the penultimate and preceding digits.

children.text: guṇyas tu adhas adhas guṇa-khaṇḍa-tulyas tais khaṇḍakais saṃguṇitas yutas vā/
children.translated_text: Or the multiplicand [may be placed] successively below, equal to the parts of the multiplier; multiplied by those parts, [the results] are added.

children.text: bhaktas guṇas @śudhyati yena tena labdhyā ca guṇyas guṇitas phalam vā//[indravajrā]
children.translated_text: Or the multiplier is purified by that [number] by which the divisor and multiplicand are divided; and by the quotient, the multiplicand multiplied gives the result.

children.text: dvidhā @bhavet rūpa-vibhāgas evam sthānais pṛthak vā guṇitas sametas/
children.translated_text: Thus there is a twofold division of forms; or, multiplied separately by places and combined,

body.text: iṣṭa-ūna-yuktena guṇena nighnas abhīṣṭa-ghna-guṇya-anvita-varjitas vā//[upajāti]
body.translated_text: or multiplied by the multiplier increased or decreased by a chosen [number], with the product of the chosen number and the multiplicand added or subtracted.

body.text: atra uddeśakas/
body.translated_text: Here is the example:

children.text: bāle bāla-kuraṅga-lola-nayane līlāvati @procyatām %pañca-%tri-%eka-mitās #divākara-guṇās aṅkās kati @syus yadi/
children.translated_text: O girl with eyes like a young fawn's, <s>Līlāvatī</s>, tell me — if the digits measuring five, three, and one are multiplied by twelve, how many will there be?

children.text: rūpa-sthāna-vibhāga-khaṇḍa-guṇane kalpā @asi kalyāṇini chinnās tena guṇena te ca guṇitās jātās kati @syus @vada//[śārdūlavikrīḍita]
children.translated_text: If you are proficient, O auspicious one, in multiplication by form-division and part-multiplication, tell me how many result when divided and multiplied by that multiplier.

body.text: nyāsas/ guṇyas 135/ guṇakas 12/ guṇya-antyam aṅkam guṇakena @hanyāt iti kṛte jātam 1620// atha vā guṇa-rūpa-vibhāge kṛte khaṇḍe 4/ 8/ ābhyām pṛthak guṇye guṇite yute ca jātam tat eva 1620// atha vā guṇakas %tribhis bhaktas labdham 4/ ebhis %tribhis ca guṇye guṇite jātam tat eva 1620// atha vā sthāna-vibhāge kṛte khaṇḍe 1/ 2/ ābhyām pṛthak guṇye guṇite yathā-sthāna-yute ca jātam tat eva 1620// atha vā %dvi-ūnena guṇakena 10 %dvābhyām 2 ca pṛthak guṇye guṇite yute ca jātam tat eva 1620// atha vā %aṣṭa-yutena guṇakena 20 guṇye guṇite %aṣṭa-guṇita-guṇya-hīne ca jātam tat eva 1620// iti guṇana-prakāras// atha bhāga-hāras/ bhāga-hāre karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: multiplicand 135, multiplier 12. Applying 'multiply the last digit of the multiplicand by the multiplier,' the result is 1620. Or, dividing the multiplier into parts: 4 and 8. Multiplying the multiplicand separately by these and adding, the same result 1620. Or, the multiplier divided by 3 gives 4; multiplying the multiplicand by these three [and then by 4], the same result 1620. Or, dividing by places: 1 and 2. Multiplying the multiplicand separately by these and adding in their proper places, the same result 1620. Or, with the multiplier decreased by 2 (giving 10) and multiplied by 2 separately, adding, the same result 1620. Or, with the multiplier increased by 8 (giving 20), multiplying the multiplicand and subtracting 8 times the multiplicand, the same result 1620. Thus ends the method of multiplication. Now, division. The rule-verse for division, one verse:

children.text: bhājyāt haras @śudhyati yad-guṇas @syāt antyāt phalam tat khalu bhāga-hāre/
children.translated_text: In division, that multiple by which the divisor is subtracted from the last [digit] of the dividend — that indeed is the quotient.

children.text: samena kena api @apavartya hāra-bhājyau @bhajet vā sati saṃbhave tu//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: Or, having reduced the divisor and dividend by some common [factor], the wise person should divide.

body.text: atra pūrva-udāharaṇe guṇita-aṅkānām sva-guṇa-chedānām bhāga-hāra-artham nyāsas/ bhājyas 1620/ bhājakas 12/ bhajanāt labdhas guṇyas 135// atha vā bhājya-hārau %tribhis apavartitau 540_4/ %caturbhis vā 405_3/ sva-sva-hāreṇa hṛte phale tat eva 135// iti bhāga-hāras// atha vargas/ varge karaṇa-sūtram vṛtta-%dvayam/
body.translated_text: For the division of the previously multiplied numbers by their own multiplier-divisors, setting down: dividend 1620, divisor 12. By division, the multiplicand 135 is obtained. Or, the dividend and divisor reduced by 3 give 540 and 4; or by 4, 405 and 3. Dividing each by its divisor, the same result 135. Thus ends division. Now, squaring. The rule-verse for squaring, two verses:

children.text: sama-%dvi-ghātas kṛtis @ucyate atha sthāpyas antya-vargas %dvi-guṇa-antya-nighnas/
children.translated_text: The product of equals is called the square (<s>kṛti</s>); then place the square of the last [digit]; multiplied by twice the last,

children.text: sva-sva-upariṣṭāt ca tathā apare aṅkās @tyaktvā antyam @utsārya punar ca rāśim//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: the other digits [are placed] above their respective positions; removing the last [digit] and shifting the number, repeat.

children.text: khaṇḍa-%dvayasya abhihatis 5dvi-nighnī tad-khaṇḍa-varga-aikya-yutā kṛtis vā/
children.translated_text: Or, the product of two parts, doubled, combined with the sum of the squares of those parts, is the square.

children.text: iṣṭa-ūna-yuj-rāśi-vadhas kṛtis @syāt iṣṭasya vargeṇa samanvitas vā//[indravajrā]
children.translated_text: Or, the product of the number increased and decreased by a chosen [number] is the square, combined with the square of the chosen [number].

body.text: atra uddeśakas/
body.translated_text: Here is the example:

children.text: sakhe %navānām ca %caturdaśānām @brūhi %tri-hīnasya %śata-%trayasya/
children.translated_text: O friend, tell me the square of nine and of fourteen,

children.text: %pañca-uttarasya api %ayutasya vargam @jānāsi ced varga-vidhāna-mārgam//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: of three hundred minus three, and of ten thousand plus five — if you know the method of the squaring procedure.

body.text: nyāsas 9/ 14/ 297/ 10005/ eṣām yathā-ukta-karaṇena jātās vargās 81/ 196/ 88209/ 100100025// atha vā %navānām khaṇḍe 4/ 5/ anayos āhatis 20/ %dvi-ghnī 40/ tad-khaṇḍa-varga-aikyena 41 yutā jātā sā eva kṛtis 81// atha vā %caturdaśānām khaṇḍe 6/ 8/ anayos āhatis 48/ %dvi-ghnī 96/ tad-khaṇḍa-vargau 36/ 64/ anayos aikyena 100 yutā jātā sā eva kṛtis 196// atha vā khaṇḍe 4/ 10/ tathā api sā eva kṛtis 196// atha vā rāśis 297/ ayam %tribhis ūnas pṛthak yutas ca 294/ 300/ anayos ghātas 88200 %tri-varga-9-yutas jātas vargas sas eva 88209// evam sarvatra/ iti vargas// atha varga-mūlam/ varga-mūle karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: 9, 14, 297, 10005. By the stated procedure, the squares obtained are: 81, 196, 88209, 100100025. Or, for nine, parts 4 and 5; their product 20, doubled 40, combined with the sum of their squares 41, gives the same square 81. Or, for fourteen, parts 6 and 8; product 48, doubled 96, sum of squares 36 + 64 = 100, combined gives the same square 196. Or, parts 4 and 10; likewise the same square 196. Or, number 297; decreased by 3 gives 294, increased by 3 gives 300; their product 88200, plus the square of 3 (= 9), gives the same square 88209. Similarly everywhere. Thus ends squaring. Now, square root. The rule-verse for square root, one verse:

children.text: @tyaktvā antyāt viṣamāt kṛtim @%dvi-guṇayet mūlam same tad-hṛte @tyaktvā labdha-kṛtim tad-ādya-viṣamāt labdham %dvi-nighnam @nyaset/
children.translated_text: Removing the [nearest] square from the last odd-place [digit], double the root; in the even place, divide by it; removing the square of the quotient from the next odd place, place twice the quotient

children.text: paṅktyām paṅkti-hṛte same anya-viṣamāt @tyaktvā āpta-vargam phalam paṅktyām tat %dvi-guṇam @nyaset iti muhus paṅktes #dalam @syāt padam//[śārdūlavikrīḍita]
children.translated_text: in the row; divide the even place by the row; removing the obtained square from the other odd place, place the result doubled in the row; repeat — half the row is the root.

body.text: atra uddeśakas/
body.translated_text: Here is the example:

children.text: mūlam %caturṇām ca tathā %navānām pūrvam kṛtānām ca sakhe kṛtīnām/
children.translated_text: O friend, know separately the square roots of the squares previously obtained

children.text: pṛthak pṛthak varga-padāni @viddhi buddhes vivṛddhis yadi te atra jātā//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: of four, nine, and the rest — if your intellect has grown in this matter.

body.text: nyāsas 4/ 9/ 81/ 196/ 88209/ 100100025/ labdhāni krameṇa mūlāni 2/ 3/ 9/ 14/ 297/ 10005// iti varga-mūlam// atha ghanas/ ghane karaṇa-sūtram vṛtta-%trayam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: 4, 9, 81, 196, 88209, 100100025. The roots obtained in order are: 2, 3, 9, 14, 297, 10005. Thus ends square root. Now, cubing. The rule-verse for cubing, three verses:

children.text: sama-%tri-ghātas ca ghanas pradiṣṭas sthāpyas ghanas antyasya tatas antya-vargas/
children.translated_text: The product of three equals is prescribed as the cube. Place the cube of the last [digit]; then the square of the last

children.text: ādi-%tri-nighnas tatas ādi-vargas %tri-antya-āhatas atha ādi-ghanas ca sarve//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: multiplied by three times the first; then the square of the first multiplied by three times the last; then the cube of the first — all these

children.text: sthāna-antaratvena yutās ghanas @syāt @prakalpya tad-khaṇḍa-#yugam tatas antyam/
children.translated_text: are combined with appropriate place-shifts to give the cube. Having made two parts of that, [treat] the last;

children.text: evam muhus varga-ghana-prasiddhau ādya-aṅkatas vā vidhis eṣas kāryas//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: repeat the well-known procedure of squaring and cubing from the first digit onward.

children.text: khaṇḍābhyām vā āhatas rāśis %tri-ghnas khaṇḍa-ghana-aikya-yuk/
children.translated_text: Or, the number multiplied by the [two] parts, tripled, combined with the sum of the cubes of the parts [gives the cube].

children.text: varga-mūla-ghanas sva-ghnas varga-rāśes ghanas @bhavet//[śloka]
children.translated_text: The cube of the square root, cubed by itself, becomes the cube of the square-number.

body.text: atra uddeśakas/
body.translated_text: Here is the example:

children.text: nava-ghanam %tri-ghanasya ghanam tathā @kathaya %pañca-ghanasya ghanam ca me/
children.translated_text: Tell me the cube of nine, the cube of the cube of three, and the cube of five,

children.text: ghana-padam ca tatas api ghanāt sakhe yadi ghane @asti ghanā bhavatas matis//[drutavilambita]
children.translated_text: and also the cube root from those cubes, O friend — if your mind is solid in cubing.

body.text: nyāsas 9/ 27/ 125/ jātās krameṇa ghanās 729/ 19683/ 1953125// atha vā rāśis 9/ asya khaṇḍe 4/ 5/ ābhyām hatas rāśis 180/ %tri-ghnas 540/ khaṇḍa-ghana-aikyena 189 yutas jātas ghanas 729// atha vā rāśis 27/ asya khaṇḍe 20/ 7/ ābhyām hatas %tri-ghnas ca 11340/ khaṇḍa-ghana-aikyena 8343 yutas jātas ghanas 19683// atha vā rāśis 4/ asya mūlam 2/ asya ghanas 8/ ayam sva-ghnas jātas %carurṇām ghanas 64// atha vā rāśis 9/ asya mūlam 3/ asya ghanas 27/ asya vargas jātas %navānām ghanas 729/ yas eva varga-rāśi-ghanas sas eva varga-mūla-ghana-vargas// iti ghanas// atha ghana-mūle karaṇa-sūtram vṛtta-%dvayam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: 9, 27, 125. The cubes obtained in order are: 729, 19683, 1953125. Or, number 9; parts 4 and 5; multiplied by those parts and tripled: 180 × 3 = 540; combined with the sum of the cubes of the parts (64 + 125 = 189), the cube 729. Or, number 27; parts 20 and 7; multiplied by those parts and tripled: 11340; combined with the sum of the cubes of the parts (8000 + 343 = 8343), the cube 19683. Or, number 4; its root 2; cube of root 8; cubed by itself gives the cube of four: 64. Or, number 9; its root 3; cube of root 27; square of that gives the cube of nine: 729. The cube of a square-number equals the square of the cube of its root. Thus ends cubing. Now, the rule-verse for cube root, two verses:

children.text: ādyam ghana-sthānam atha aghane %dve punar tathā antyāt ghanatas @viśodhya/
children.translated_text: The first is a cube-place, then two non-cube [places]; repeat thus. Subtracting from the last [cube-place digit] the [nearest] cube,

children.text: ghanam pṛthak-stham padam asya @kṛtvā %tri-ghnyā tad-ādyam @vibhajet phalam tu//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: placing its root separately, divide the first [non-cube place] by thrice [the root]; the quotient

children.text: paṅktyām @nyaset tad-kṛtim antya-nighnīm %tri-ghnīm @tyajet tad-%prathamāt phalasya/
children.translated_text: is placed in the row; its square multiplied by thrice the last is subtracted from the first [non-cube place];

children.text: ghanam tad-ādyāt ghana-mūlam evam paṅktis @bhavet evam atas punar ca//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: then the cube [of the quotient is subtracted] from the first [cube-place]; the row becomes the cube root; and repeat.

children.text: atra pūrva-ghanānām mūla-artham nyāsas 729/ 19683/ 1953125/ krameṇa labdhāni mūlāni 9/ 27/ 125// iti ghana-mūlam// iti parikarma-%aṣṭakam//
children.translated_text: For finding the roots of the previous cubes, setting down: 729, 19683, 1953125. The roots obtained in order are: 9, 27, 125. Thus ends cube root. Thus ends the Eight Operations.

body.text: bhinna-parikarma-aṣṭaka
body.translated_text: The Eight Operations on Fractions

body.text: atha bhinna-parikarma-%aṣṭakam// atha aṃśa-savarṇanam/ tatra bhāga-jātau karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Now, the eight operations on fractions. Now, reducing fractions to a common denominator. The rule-verse for addition of fractions, one verse:

children.text: anyonya-hāra-abhihatau hara-aṃśau rāśyos sama-cheda-vidhānam evam/
children.translated_text: The numerators and denominators of the two quantities are cross-multiplied by each other's denominators — this is the method of making common denominators.

children.text: mithas harābhyām apavartitābhyām yat vā hara-aṃśau sudhiyā atra guṇyau//[upajāti]
children.translated_text: Or, the numerators and denominators should be multiplied by the intelligent person using the denominators mutually reduced [by their common factor].

body.text: atra uddeśakas/
body.translated_text: Here is the example:

children.text: rūpa-%trayam %pañca-lavas %tri-bhāgas yoga-artham etān @vada tulya-hārān/
children.translated_text: State these with common denominators for the purpose of addition: three units, one-fifth, and one-third.

children.text: %triṣaṣṭi-bhāgas ca %caturdaśa-aṃśas sama-chidau mitra viyojana-artham// [upajāti]
children.translated_text: And one sixty-third and one fourteenth — with common denominators, O friend, for the purpose of subtraction.

body.text: nyāsas/ 3_1/ 1_5/ 1_3/ jātās sama-chedās 45_15/ 3_15/ 5_15/ yoge jātam 53_15// atha %dvitīya-udāharaṇe nyāsas 1_63/ 1_14/ %sapta-apavartitābhyām hārābhyām 9/ 2 saṃguṇitau vā jātau sama-chedau 2_126/ 9_126/ viyoge jātam 7_126/ %sapta-apavartite ca jātam 1_18// iti bhāga-jātis// atha prabhāga-jātau karaṇa-sūtram vṛtta-%ardham/
body.translated_text: Setting down: 3/1, 1/5, 1/3. Made into common denominators: 45/15, 3/15, 5/15. By addition, the result is 53/15. In the second example, setting down: 1/63, 1/14. Reduced by 7, the denominators become 9 and 2; multiplied [accordingly], common denominators: 2/126, 9/126. By subtraction, the result is 7/126; reduced by 7, the result is 1/18. Thus ends addition of fractions. Now, the rule-verse for multiplication of fractions, half a verse:

body.text: lavās lava-ghnās ca harās hara-ghnās bhāga-prabhāgeṣu savarṇanam @syāt/ [upajāti-ab; cd=34a]
body.translated_text: In multiplication of fractions, the numerators are multiplied by numerators and the denominators by denominators; this constitutes reducing to common denominators.

body.text: atra uddeśakas/
body.translated_text: Here is the example:

children.text: dramma-%ardha-%tri-lava-%dvayasya sumate #pāda-%trayam yat @bhavet tat %pañca-aṃśaka-%ṣoḍaśa-aṃśa-#caraṇas saṃprārthitena arthine/
children.translated_text: O intelligent one, three-quarters of two-thirds of half a <s>dramma</s> — whatever that may be — of that, one-fifth of one-sixteenth of a quarter was requested by a beggar;

children.text: dattas yena varāṭakās kati kadaryeṇa arpitās tena me @brūhi tvam yadi @vetsi vatsa gaṇite jātim prabhāga-abhidhām// [śārdūlavikrīḍita]
children.translated_text: how many <s>varāṭakas</s> (cowrie-shells) were given by that miser? Tell me, child, if you know the fraction-operation called multiplication of fractions.

body.text: nyāsas/ 1_1/ 1_2/ 2_3/ 3_4/ 1_5/ 1_16/ 1_4/ savarṇite jātam 6_7680/ %ṣaḍbhis apavartite jātam/ 1_1280/ evam dattas varāṭakas// iti prabhāga-jātis// atha bhāga-anubandha-bhāga-apavāhayos karaṇa-sūtram sa-%ardham vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: 1/1, 1/2, 2/3, 3/4, 1/5, 1/16, 1/4. When reduced to a common denominator, the result is 6/7680. Simplified by six, the result is 1/1280. Thus the <s>varāṭaka</s> (cowrie shell) given. Thus ends <s>prabhāga-jāti</s> (sub-fraction type). Now the rule of operation for <s>bhāga-anubandha</s> (fraction-with-addition) and <s>bhāga-apavāha</s> (fraction-with-subtraction), a verse and a half:

children.text: cheda-ghna-rūpeṣu lavās dhana-ṛṇam %ekasya bhāgās adhika-ūnakās ced// [upajāti-cd; ab=32]
children.translated_text: When the fractions of one [quantity] are to be increased or decreased, [multiply] the numerators by the denominators [of the others] and add or subtract [respectively].

children.text: sva-aṃśa-adhika-ūnas khalu yatra tatra bhāga-anubandhe ca lava-apavāhe/
children.translated_text: Where [a fraction] is increased or decreased by its own parts, in <s>bhāga-anubandha</s> (fraction-addition) and <s>lava-apavāha</s> (fraction-subtraction),

children.text: tala-stha-hāreṇa haram @nihanyāt sva-aṃśa-adhika-ūnena tu tena bhāgān// [upajāti]
children.translated_text: one should multiply the denominator by the denominator placed below, and the numerators by that [denominator] increased or decreased by its own part.

body.text: atra uddeśakas/
body.translated_text: Here is an example:

children.text: sa-#aṅghri %dvayam %trayam vi-#aṅghri kīdṛś @brūhi savarṇitam/
children.translated_text: Two with a quarter, and three without a quarter — tell me, what are they when reduced to a common denominator?

children.text: @jānāsi aṃśa-anubandham ced tathā bhāga-apavāhanam//
children.translated_text: If you know <s>aṃśa-anubandha</s> (fraction-addition) and likewise <s>bhāga-apavāhana</s> (fraction-subtraction).

body.text: nyāsas 2_1_4/ 3_-1_4/ savarṇite jātam 9_4/ 11_4// atra uddeśakas/
body.translated_text: Setting down: 2 1/4, 3 −1/4. When reduced to a common denominator, the results are 9/4 and 11/4. Here is an example:

children.text: #aṅghris sva-%tri-aṃśa-yuktas sas nija-#dala-yutas kīdṛśas kīdṛśau %dvau %tri-aṃśau sva-%aṣṭa-aṃśa-hīnau tad-anu ca rahitau tau %tribhis %sapta-bhāgais/
children.translated_text: A quarter increased by its own third, that [quarter] increased by its own half — what is it? What are two-thirds decreased by their own eighth, and then those [two-thirds] diminished by three-sevenths?

children.text: %ardham sva-%aṣṭa-aṃśa-hīnam %navabhis atha yutam %saptama-aṃśais svakīyais kīdṛś @syāt @brūhi @vetsi tvam iha yadi sakhe aṃśa-anubandha-apavāhau// [sragdharā]
children.translated_text: A half decreased by its own eighth, then increased by its own nine-sevenths — what would it be? Tell me, if you know, dear friend, <s>aṃśa-anubandha</s> (fraction-addition) and <s>apavāha</s> (fraction-subtraction).

body.text: nyāsas/ {btabular} 1_4 & 2_3 & 1_2 \\ 1_3 & -1_8 & -1_8 \\ 1_2 & -3_7 & 9_7 {etabular} savarṇite jātam/ 1_2/ 1_3/ 1_1// iti jāti-%catuṣṭayam// atha bhinna-saṃkalita-vyavakalitayos karaṇa-sūtram vṛtta-%ardham/
body.translated_text: Setting down: {1/4, 2/3, 1/2 with sub-fractions 1/3, −1/8, −1/8 and 1/2, −3/7, 9/7}. When reduced to a common denominator, the results are: 1/2, 1/3, 1/1. Thus ends the four types of <s>jāti</s> (fraction operations). Now the rule of operation for addition and subtraction of fractions, half a verse:

body.text: yogas antaram tulya-hara-aṃśakānām kalpyas haras #rūpam ahāra-rāśes// [indravajrā-ab; cd=39]
body.translated_text: The sum or difference of [fractions] having equal denominators and numerators should be computed; the denominator of a quantity without a denominator is unity.

body.text: atra uddeśakas/
body.translated_text: Here is an example:

children.text: %pañca-aṃa-#pāda-%tri-lava-%ardha-%ṣaṣṭhān %ekī-kṛtān @brūhi sakhe mama etān/
children.translated_text: Tell me, dear friend, the sum of these: a fifth, a quarter, a third, a half, and a sixth.

children.text: ebhis ca bhāgais atha varjitānām kim @syāt %trayāṇām @kathaya āśu śeṣam// [indravajrā]
children.translated_text: And tell me quickly, what remainder would there be when three are diminished by these fractions?

body.text: nyāsas 1_5/ 1_4/ 1_3/ 1_2/ 1_6/ aikye jātam 29_20// atha etais varjitānām %trayāṇām śeṣam 31_20// iti bhinna-saṃkalita-vyavakalite// atha bhinna-guṇane karaṇa-sūtram vṛtta-%ardham/
body.translated_text: Setting down: 1/5, 1/4, 1/3, 1/2, 1/6. The sum is 29/20. Now the remainder when these are subtracted from three is 31/20. Thus ends addition and subtraction of fractions. Now the rule of operation for multiplication of fractions, half a verse:

body.text: aṃśa-āhatis cheda-vadhena bhaktā labdham vibhinne guṇane phalam @syāt//[indravajrā-cd; ab=37]
body.translated_text: The product of the numerators divided by the product of the denominators — that shall be the result in multiplication of fractions.

body.text: atra uddeśakas/
body.translated_text: Here is an example:

children.text: sa-%tri-aṃśa-rūpa-%dvitayena nighnam sa-%saptama-aṃśa-%dvitayam @bhavet kim/
children.translated_text: What would two-and-one-third multiplied by two-and-one-seventh be?

children.text: %ardham %tri-bhāgena hatam ca @viddhi dakṣas @asi bhinne guṇanā-vidhau ced// [upajāti]
children.translated_text: And know that a half multiplied by a third — [tell the result] if you are skilled in the method of multiplication of fractions.

body.text: nyāsas 2_1_3/ 2_1_7/ savarṇite jātam 7_3/ 15_7/ guṇite ca jātam 5_1// nyāsas 1_2/ 1_3/ guṇite jātam 1_6// iti bhinna-guṇanam// atha bhinna-bhāga-hāre karaṇa-sūtram vṛtta-%ardham/
body.translated_text: Setting down: 2 1/3, 2 1/7. When reduced to a common denominator, the results are 7/3 and 15/7. When multiplied, the result is 5/1. Setting down: 1/2, 1/3. When multiplied, the result is 1/6. Thus ends multiplication of fractions. Now the rule of operation for division of fractions, half a verse:

body.text: chedam lavam ca @parivartya harasya śeṣas kāryas atha bhāga-haraṇe guṇanā-vidhis ca// [vasantatilakā-ab; cd=43]
body.translated_text: Having inverted the denominator and numerator of the divisor, the remaining procedure for division of fractions is the same as the method of multiplication.

body.text: atra uddeśakas/
body.translated_text: Here is an example:

children.text: sa-%tri-aṃśa-rūpa-%dvitayena %pañca %tri-aṃśena %ṣaṣṭham @vada me @vibhajya/
children.translated_text: Tell me, having divided five by two-and-one-third, and one-sixth by one-third,

children.text: darbhīya-garbha-agra-su-tīkṣṇa-buddhis ced @asti te bhinna-hṛtau samarthā// [indravajrā]
children.translated_text: if you have an intellect as sharp as the tip of a <s>darbha</s> grass blade within, [and are] capable in division of fractions.

body.text: nyāsas 2_1_3/ 5_1/ 1_3/ 1_6/ yathā-ukta-karaṇena jātam 15_7/ 1_2// iti bhinna-bhāga-hāras// atha bhinna-varga-ādau karaṇa-sūtram vṛtta-%ardham/
body.translated_text: Setting down: 2 1/3, 5/1, 1/3, 1/6. By the stated procedure, the results are 15/7 and 1/2. Thus ends division of fractions. Now the rule of operation for squaring and other [operations] on fractions, half a verse:

body.text: varge kṛtī ghana-vidhau tu ghanau vidheyau hāra-aṃśayos atha pade ca pada-prasiddhyai// [vasantatilakā-cd; ab=41]
body.translated_text: For squaring, the square should be taken; for cubing, the cube should be taken — of both the denominator and numerator; and for the root, the root should be found [of each].

body.text: atra uddeśakas/
body.translated_text: Here is an example:

children.text: sa-%ardha-%trayāṇām @kathaya āśu vargam vargāt tatas varga-padam ca mitra/
children.translated_text: Tell me quickly the square of three-and-a-half, and then the square root from that square, O friend,

children.text: ghanam ca mūlam ca ghanāt tatas api @jānāsi ced varga-ghanau vibhinnau// [upajāti]
children.translated_text: and also the cube and the cube root from that — if you know squaring and cubing of fractions.

children.text: nyāsas 3_1_2/ cheda-ghna-rūpe kṛte jātam 7_2/ asya vargas 49_4/ atas mūlam 7_2/ ghanas 343_8/ asya mūlam 7_2// iti bhinna-parikarma-%aṣṭakam//
children.translated_text: Setting down: 3 1/2. When converted to a fraction with denominator, the result is 7/2. Its square is 49/4. From that, the root is 7/2. The cube is 343/8. Its [cube] root is 7/2. Thus ends the eight operations on fractions.

body.text: śūnya-parikarma-aṣṭaka
body.translated_text: Operations with zero — the eight operations

body.text: atha #śūnya-parikarmasu karaṇa-sūtram āryā-%dvayam/
body.translated_text: Now the rule of operation for operations with zero, two <s>āryā</s> verses:

children.text: yoge #kham kṣepa-samam varga-ādau #kham #kha-bhājitas rāśis/
children.translated_text: In addition, zero [added to a quantity] equals the addend; in squaring and other [operations], zero [results]. A quantity divided by zero [remains as is].

children.text: #kha-haras @syāt #kha-guṇas #kham #kha-guṇas cintyas ca śeṣa-vidhau// [āryā]
children.translated_text: A quantity multiplied by zero becomes zero; a quantity multiplied by zero is to be treated specially in subsequent operations.

children.text: #śūnye guṇake jāte #kham hāras ced punar tadā rāśis/
children.translated_text: When zero is the multiplier and the result becomes zero, if [zero is also] the divisor, then the quantity

children.text: avikṛtas eva jñeyas tathā eva #khena ūnitas ca yutas// [āryā]
children.translated_text: is to be understood as unchanged; and likewise [a quantity] diminished or increased by zero [remains unchanged].

body.text: atra uddeśakas/
body.translated_text: Here is an example:

children.text: #kham %pañca-yuk @bhavati kim @vada khasya vargam mūlam ghanam ghana-padam #kha-guṇās ca %pañca/
children.translated_text: Tell me, what is zero plus five? What is the square of zero, the root, the cube, the cube root? And what is five multiplied by zero?

children.text: #khena uddhṛtās %daśa ca kas %kha-guṇas nija-%ardha-yuktas %tribhis ca guṇitas sva-hatas %triṣaṣṭis// [vasantatilakā]
children.translated_text: And what is ten divided by zero? What quantity, multiplied by zero, added to its own half, then multiplied by three, and squared, gives sixty-three?

children.text: nyāsas 0/ etat %pañca-yutam jātam 5/ #khasya vargas 0/ mūlam 0/ ghanam 0/ ghana-mūlam 0// nyāsas 5/ ete #khena guṇitās jātās 0// nyāsas 10/ ete #kha-bhaktās 10_0// ajñātas rāśis tasya guṇas 0/ sva-%ardham kṣepas 1_2/ guṇas 3/ haras 0/ dṛśyam 63/ tatas vakṣyamāṇena viloma-vidhinā iṣṭa-karmaṇā vā labdhas rāśis 14// asya gaṇitasya graha-gaṇite
children.translated_text: Setting down: 0. This plus five gives 5. The square of zero is 0. The root is 0. The cube is 0. The cube root is 0. Setting down: 5. These multiplied by zero give 0. Setting down: 10. These divided by zero give 10/0. The unknown quantity: its multiplier is 0, its own half is the addend 1/2, multiplier 3, divisor 0, the visible result is 63. Then by the inverse method to be described, or by the desired operation, the quantity obtained is 14. The use of this computation is great

body.text: mahān upayogas// iti śūnya-parikarma-%aṣṭakam//
body.translated_text: in planetary computation. Thus ends the eight operations with zero.

body.text: prakīrṇaka
body.translated_text: Miscellaneous problems

body.text: atha vyasta-vidhau karaṇa-sūtram vṛtta-%dvayam/
body.translated_text: Now the rule of operation for the inverse method, two verses:

children.text: chedam guṇam guṇam chedam vargam mūlam padam kṛtim/
children.translated_text: Make the denominator the multiplier, the multiplier the denominator; the square becomes the root, the root becomes the square;

children.text: ṛṇam svam svam ṛṇam @kuryāt dṛśye rāśi-prasiddhaye// [śloka]
children.translated_text: subtraction becomes addition, addition becomes subtraction — [this is done] for finding the quantity from the visible [result].

children.text: atha sva-aṃśa-adhika-ūne tu lava-āḍhya-ūnas haras haras/
children.translated_text: Now when [a fraction] is increased or decreased by its own part, the denominator becomes the denominator decreased or increased by the numerator,

children.text: aṃśas tu avikṛtas tatra vilome śeṣam ukta-vat// [śloka]
children.translated_text: while the numerator remains unchanged — in the inverse [method]; the rest is as previously stated.

body.text: atra uddeśakas/
body.translated_text: Here is an example:

children.text: yas %tri-ghnas %tribhis anvitas sva-#caraṇais bhaktas tatas %saptabhis sva-%tri-aṃśena vivarjitas sva-guṇitas hīnas %dvipañcāśatā/
children.translated_text: That which is multiplied by three, increased by three-quarters of itself, divided by seven, diminished by its own third, squared, decreased by fifty-two,

children.text: tad-mūle %aṣṭa-yute hṛte ca %daśabhis jātam %dvayam @brūhi tam rāśim @vetsi hi cañcala-akṣi vimalām bāle viloma-kriyām// [śārdūlavikrīḍita]
children.translated_text: when its root is taken, eight is added, and divided by ten, the result is two — tell me that quantity. You know, O bright-eyed girl, the clear inverse method.

body.text: nyāsas guṇas 3/ kṣepas 3_4/ bhājakas 7/ ṛṇam 1_3/ vargas/ ṛṇam 52/ mūlam/ kṣepas 8/ haras 10/ dṛśyam 2/ yathā-ukta-karaṇena jātas rāśis 28// iti vyasta-vidhis// atha iṣṭa-karmasu dṛśya-jāti-śeṣa-jāti-viśleṣa-jāti-ādau karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: multiplier 3, addend 3/4, divisor 7, subtraction 1/3, squaring, subtraction 52, square root, addend 8, divisor 10, visible result 2. By the stated procedure, the quantity obtained is 28. Thus ends the inverse method. Now the rule of operation for desired operations — <s>dṛśya-jāti</s> (visible type), <s>śeṣa-jāti</s> (remainder type), <s>viśleṣa-jāti</s> (difference type), and others — a verse:

children.text: uddeśaka-ālāpa-vat iṣṭa-rāśis kṣuṇṇas hṛtas aṃśais rahitas yutas vā/
children.translated_text: An assumed quantity, multiplied, divided, diminished, or increased by [given] fractions, as stated in the example,

children.text: iṣṭa-āhatam dṛṣṭam anena bhaktam rāśis @bhavet proktam iti iṣṭa-karma// [indravajrā]
children.translated_text: the visible [result] multiplied by the assumed [quantity] and divided by this [computed result] gives the [true] quantity — this is called the method of assumed quantities.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: An illustration:

children.text: %pañca-ghnas sva-%tri-bhāga-ūnas %daśa-bhaktas samanvitas/
children.translated_text: A quantity multiplied by five, diminished by its own third, divided by ten, and then increased

children.text: rāśi-%tri-aṃśa-%ardha-pādais @syāt kas rāśis %dvi-ūna-%saptatis// [śloka]
children.translated_text: by a third, a half, and a quarter of the quantity — what is the quantity, if [the result] is sixty-eight minus two (i.e., sixty-eight)?

body.text: nyāsas/ guṇas 5/ sva-aṃśa-ṛṇam -1_3/ [āpaṭe: 0_1_3] ūnas 1_3/ bhāga-hāras 10/ rāśi-aṃśakās kṣepās 1_3/ 1_2/ 1_4/ dṛśyam 68/ atra kila iṣṭa-rāśis 3/ %pañca-ghnas 15/ sva-%tri-bhāga-ūnas 10/ %daśa-bhaktas 1/ atra kalpita-rāśes 3 %tri-aṃśa-%ardha-#pādais 3_3/ 3_2/ 3_4/ etais samanvitas jātas 17_4/ anena dṛṣṭam 68/ iṣṭa-āhatam bhaktam jātas rāśis 48// evam yatra udāharaṇe rāśis kena-cit guṇitas bhaktas vā rāśi-aṃśena rahitas yutas vā dṛṣṭas tatra iṣṭam rāśim @prakalpya tasmin uddeśaka-ālāpa-vat karmaṇi kṛte yat @niṣpadyate tena @bhajet dṛṣṭam iṣṭa-guṇam phalam rāśis @syāt// atha dṛśya-jāti-udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: multiplier 5, own-fraction subtracted −1/3, divisor 10, fractions of the quantity as addends 1/3, 1/2, 1/4, visible result 68. Here the assumed quantity is 3. Multiplied by five: 15. Diminished by its own third: 10. Divided by ten: 1. Now the assumed quantity 3, with its third, half, and quarter: 3/3, 3/2, 3/4 — added together gives 17/4. By this, the visible [result] 63 multiplied by the assumed quantity gives the quantity 48. Thus wherever in an example a quantity is multiplied or divided by something, diminished or increased by a fraction of the quantity, and the result is visible, there one should assume a quantity, perform the operations as stated in the example, and divide the visible result multiplied by the assumed quantity by the computed result — that gives the [true] quantity. Now an illustration of <s>dṛśya-jāti</s> (visible type):

children.text: amala-kamala-rāśes %tri-aṃśa-%pañca-aṃśa-%ṣaṣṭhais %tri-nayana-hari-sūryās yena %turyeṇa ca āryā/
children.translated_text: Of a collection of spotless lotuses, a third, a fifth, and a sixth [were offered] to <s>Trinayana</s> (three-eyed <s>Śiva</s>), <s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), and <s>Sūrya</s> (the Sun); and with a quarter, O noble lady,

children.text: guru-padam atha %ṣaḍbhis pūjitam śeṣa-padmais sakala-kamala-saṃkhyām kṣipram @ākhyāhi tasya// [mālinī]
children.translated_text: the feet of the Guru were worshipped; and with six remaining lotuses — tell me quickly the total number of lotuses.

body.text: nyāsas 1_3/ 1_5/ 1_6/ 1_4/ dṛśyam 6/ atra iṣṭam #rūpam 1 rāśim @prakalpya prāk-vat jātas rāśis 120// atha śeṣa-jāti-udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: 1/3, 1/5, 1/6, 1/4, visible result 6. Here, assuming unity (1) as the quantity, as before, the quantity obtained is 120. Now an illustration of <s>śeṣa-jāti</s> (remainder type):

children.text: sva-%ardham @prādāt prayāge %nava-lava-#yugalam yas avaśeṣāt ca kāśyām śeṣa-#aṅghrim śulka-hetos pathi %daśama-lavān %ṣaṭ ca śeṣāt gayāyām/
children.translated_text: A pilgrim traveling to sacred places gave half [of his wealth] at <s>Prayāga</s>, two-ninths of the remainder at <s>Kāśī</s>, a quarter of the remainder for toll on the road, and six-tenths of the remainder at <s>Gayā</s>,

children.text: śiṣṭās niṣka-%triṣaṣṭis nija-gṛham anayā tīrtha-pānthas prayātas tasya dravya-pramāṇam @vada yadi bhavatā śeṣa-jātis śrutā @asti// [sragdharā]
children.translated_text: The remainder was sixty-three <s>niṣkas</s> (gold coins) [which he brought] home. Tell me the measure of his wealth, if you have learned <s>śeṣa-jāti</s> (the remainder type).

body.text: nyāsas 1_1/ 1_2/ 2_9/ 1_4/ 6_10/ dṛśyam 63/ atra #rūpam 1 rāśim @prakalpya bhāgān śeṣān śeṣāt @apāsya atha vā bhāga-apavāha-vidhinā savarṇite jātam 7_60/ anena dṛṣṭe 63 iṣṭa-guṇite bhakte jātam dravya-pramāṇam 540// idam viloma-sūtreṇa api @sidhyati// atha viśleṣa-jāti-udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: 1/1, 1/2, 2/9, 1/4, 6/10, visible result 63. Here, assuming unity (1) as the quantity and subtracting the fractions from the remainders of the remainders — or by the method of <s>bhāga-apavāha</s> (fraction-subtraction), when reduced to a common denominator, the result is 7/60. By this, the visible [result] 63 multiplied by the assumed quantity and divided gives the measure of wealth: 540. This can also be solved by the inverse-method formula. Now an illustration of <s>viśleṣa-jāti</s> (difference type):

children.text: %pañca-aṃśas ali-kulāt kadambam @agamat %tri-aṃśas śilīndhram tayos viśleṣas %tri-guṇas mṛga-akṣi kuṭajam dolāyamānas aparas/
children.translated_text: One-fifth of a swarm of bees went to a <s>kadamba</s> flower, one-third alighted on a <s>śilīndhra</s> (mushroom plant); three times the difference of those two, O doe-eyed one, [went to] a <s>kuṭaja</s> tree, and another, swaying,

children.text: kānte ketaka-mālatī-parimala-prāpta-%eka-kāla-priyā-dūta-āhūtas itas tatas @bhramati khe bhṛṅgas ali-saṃkhyām @vada// [śārdūlavikrīḍita]
children.translated_text: a beloved messenger summoned by the simultaneous fragrance of <s>ketaka</s> and <s>mālatī</s> flowers, wanders here and there in the sky — tell me the number of bees in the swarm.

body.text: nyāsas 1_5/ 1_3/ 2_5/ dṛśyam 1/ jātam ali-kula-mānam 15// evam anyatra api// iti iṣṭa-karma// atha saṃkramaṇe karaṇa-sūtram vṛtta-ardham/
body.translated_text: Setting down: 1/5, 1/3, 2/5, visible result 1. The number of the bee-swarm obtained is 15. Similarly in other [problems]. Thus ends the method of assumed quantities. Now the rule of operation for <s>saṃkramaṇa</s> (transition/simultaneous equations), half a verse:

body.text: yogas antareṇa ūna-yutas ardhitas tau rāśī smṛtau saṃkramaṇa-ākhyam etat// [indravajrā-ab; cd=58]
body.translated_text: The sum increased and decreased by the difference, [each] halved — those are the two quantities. This is called <s>saṃkramaṇa</s> (transition).

body.text: atra uddeśakas/
body.translated_text: Here is an example:

children.text: yayos yogas %śatam sa-%ekam viyogas %pañcaviṃśatis/
children.translated_text: Of two quantities whose sum is one hundred and one, and whose difference is twenty-five,

children.text: tau rāśī @vada me vatsa @vetsi saṃkramaṇam yadi// [śloka]
children.translated_text: tell me those two quantities, dear child, if you know <s>saṃkramaṇa</s> (transition).

body.text: nyāsas/ yogas 101/ antaram 25/ jātau rāśī 38/ 63// varga-saṃkramaṇe karaṇa-sūtram vṛtta-%ardham/
body.translated_text: Setting down: sum 101, difference 25. The two quantities obtained are 38 and 63. The rule of operation for <s>varga-saṃkramaṇa</s> (square-transition), half a verse:

body.text: varga-antaram rāśi-viyoga-bhaktam yogas tatas prokta-vat eva rāśī// [indravajrā-cd; ab=56]
body.translated_text: The difference of the squares divided by the difference of the quantities gives the sum; then from that, as previously stated, [one obtains] the two quantities.

body.text: uddeśakas/
body.translated_text: An example:

children.text: rāśyos yayos viyogas %aṣṭau tad-kṛtyos ca %catuḥśatī/
children.translated_text: Of two quantities whose difference is eight, and the difference of whose squares is four hundred,

children.text: vivaram @brūhi tau rāśī śīghram gaṇita-kovida// [śloka]
children.translated_text: tell me that difference and those two quantities quickly, O one skilled in computation.

body.text: nyāsas/ rāśi-antaram 8/ kṛti-antaram 400/ jātau rāśī 21/ 29// iti viṣama-karma// atha kiṃcit varga-karma @procyate/
body.translated_text: Setting down: difference of quantities 8, difference of squares 400. The two quantities obtained are 21 and 29. Thus ends the <s>viṣama-karma</s> (unequal operations). Now some operations on squares are stated:

children.text: iṣṭa-kṛtis %aṣṭa-guṇitā vi-%ekā dalitā vibhājitā iṣṭena/
children.translated_text: The square of an assumed [number], multiplied by eight, minus one, halved, and divided by the assumed [number] —

children.text: %ekas @syāt asya kṛtis dalitā sa-%ekā aparas rāśis//
children.translated_text: plus one, its square halved, plus one — that is the other quantity.

children.text: #rūpam %dvi-guṇa-iṣṭa-hṛtam sa-iṣṭam %prathamas atha vā aparas #rūpam/
children.translated_text: Or: unity divided by twice the assumed [number], added to the assumed [number], is the first; the other is unity.

children.text: kṛti-yuti-viyutī vi-%eke vargau @syātām yayos rāśyos//
children.translated_text: The sum and difference of their squares, each minus one, shall be [perfect] squares — of which two quantities.

body.text: uddeśakas/
body.translated_text: An example:

children.text: rāśyos yayos kṛti-viyoga-yutī nis-%eke mūla-prade @pravada tau mama mitra yatra/
children.translated_text: Tell me, O friend, those two quantities for which the sum and difference of their squares, each minus one, yield square roots,

children.text: @kliśyanti bīja-gaṇite paṭavas api mūḍhās %ṣoḍhā-ukta-bīja-gaṇitam paribhāvayantas//
children.translated_text: where even the clever are confounded in <s>bīja-gaṇita</s> (algebra), bewildered though they contemplate the six-fold stated algebra.

body.text: atra %prathama-ānayane kalpitam iṣṭam 1_2/ asya kṛtis 1_4/ %aṣṭa-guṇitā 2/ iyam vi-%ekā 1/ dalitā 1_2/ iṣṭena 1_2 hṛtas jātas %prathamas rāśis 1// asya kṛtis 1/ dalitā 1_2/ sa-%ekā 3_2/ ayam aparas rāśis/ evam etau rāśī 1_1/ 3_2// evam %ekena iṣṭena jātau rāśī 7_2/ 57_8// %dvikena 31_4/ 993_32// atha %dvitīya-prakāreṇa iṣṭam 1/ anena %dvi-guṇena 2 %rūpam 1 bhaktam 1_2/ iṣṭena sahitam jātas %prathamas rāśis 3_2/ %dvitīyas #rūpam 1/ evam rāśī 3_2/ 1_1// evam %dvikena iṣṭena 9_4/ 1_1// %trikeṇa 19_6/ 1_1// %tri-aṃśena 11_6/ 1-1// atha vā sūtram/
body.translated_text: Here, for finding the first [quantity], the assumed number is 1/2. Its square is 1/4. Multiplied by eight: 2. This minus one: 1. Halved: 1/2. Divided by the assumed number 1/2, the first quantity obtained is 1. Its square is 1. Halved: 1/2. Plus one: 3/2. This is the other quantity. Thus the two quantities are 1/1 and 3/2. Similarly, with one as the assumed number, the two quantities are 7/2 and 57/8. With two: 31/4 and 993/32. Now by the second method: assumed number 1. Divided by twice this (2), unity (1) gives 1/2. Added to the assumed number, the first quantity is 3/2. The second is unity 1. Thus the quantities are 3/2 and 1/1. Similarly with two as the assumed number: 9/4 and 1/1. With three: 19/6 and 1/1. With one-third: 11/6 and 1/1. Or alternatively, [another] formula:

children.text: iṣṭasya varga-vargas ghanas ca tau %aṣṭa-saṃguṇau %prathamas/
children.translated_text: The fourth power of the assumed [number] and the cube, each multiplied by eight — the first

children.text: sa-%ekas rāśī @syātām evam vyakte atha vā avyakte//
children.translated_text: plus one — these shall be the two quantities, thus in determinate or indeterminate [analysis].

body.text: iṣṭam 1_2/ asya varga-vargas 1_16/ %aṣṭa-ghnas 1_2/ sa-%ekas jātas %prathamas rāśis 3-2/ punar iṣṭam 1_2/ asya ghanas 1_8/ %aṣṭa-guṇas jātas %dvitīyas rāśis 1_1/ evam jātau rāśī 3_2/ 1_1// atha %ekena iṣṭena 9/ 8// %dvikena 129/ 64// %trikeṇa 649/ 216// evam sarveṣu api prakāreṣu iṣṭa-vaśāt ānantyam//
body.translated_text: Assumed number 1/2. Its fourth power is 1/16. Multiplied by eight: 1/2. Plus one, the first quantity obtained is 3/2. Again, assumed number 1/2. Its cube is 1/8. Multiplied by eight, the second quantity obtained is 1/1. Thus the two quantities are 3/2 and 1/1. Now with one as the assumed number: 9 and 8. With two: 129 and 64. With three: 649 and 216. Thus in all methods, by choice of the assumed number, there is infinity [of solutions].

children.text: pāṭī-sūtra-upamam bījam gūḍham iti @avabhāsate/
children.translated_text: <s>Bīja</s> (algebra) appears to be hidden, like the formulas of <s>pāṭī</s> (arithmetic),

children.text: na @asti gūḍham amūḍhānām na eva %ṣoḍhā iti anekadhā//
children.translated_text: but nothing is hidden from the wise — nor is it merely sixfold, but manifold.

children.text: @asti trairāśikam pāṭī bījam ca vimalā matis/
children.translated_text: There is the Rule of Three (<s>trairāśika</s>), arithmetic (<s>pāṭī</s>), and algebra (<s>bīja</s>), and a clear intellect;

children.text: kim ajñātam su-buddhīnām atas manda-artham @ucyate//
children.translated_text: What is unknown to those of good intelligence? Therefore, this is stated for the sake of the dull-witted.

body.text: iti varga-karma// atha mūla-guṇake karṇa-sūtram vṛtta-%dvayam/
body.translated_text: Thus ends the operations on squares. Now, two verses as the operational rule for [finding a quantity when its] root is multiplied [by some number].

children.text: guṇa-ghna-mūla-ūna-yutasya rāśes dṛṣṭasya yuktasya guṇa-%ardha-kṛtyā/
children.translated_text: Of the quantity that is seen diminished or increased by its root multiplied by a factor, when augmented by the square of half the factor,

children.text: mūlam guṇa-%ardhena yutam vihīnam vargī-kṛtam praṣṭur abhīṣṭa-rāśis//
children.translated_text: The square root, increased or diminished by half the factor, when squared, is the desired quantity of the questioner.

children.text: yadā lavais ca ūna-yutas sas rāśis %ekena bhāga-ūna-yutena @bhaktvā/
children.translated_text: When that quantity is diminished or increased by fractions, then dividing by the [fraction] diminished or increased by one,

children.text: dṛśyam tathā mūla-guṇam ca tābhyām sādhyas tatas prokta-vat eva rāśis//
children.translated_text: The visible [result] and the root-multiplier [are found] from those; then the quantity is determined as previously stated.

body.text: yas rāśis sva-mūlena kena cit guṇitena ūnas dṛṣṭas tasya mūla-guṇa-%ardha-kṛtyā yuktasya yat padam tat guṇa-%ardhena yuktam kāryam/ yadi guṇa-ghna-mūla-yutas dṛṣṭas tarhi hīnam kāryam/ tasya vargas rāśis @syāt// mūla-ūne dṛṣṭe tāvat udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: For a quantity that is seen diminished by its root multiplied by some [number], when augmented by the square of half the root-multiplier, the square root of that, increased by half the multiplier, should be taken; if it is seen increased by the root multiplied by the factor, then it should be diminished. The square of that will be the quantity. Now, an example when the visible [result] is diminished by the root:

children.text: bāle marāla-kula-mūla-dalāni %sapta tīre vilāsa-bhara-manthara-gāṇi @apaśyam/
children.translated_text: O girl, I saw seven times the square root of a flock of geese as [separate] groups on the bank, moving slowly with the weight of their playfulness,

children.text: kurvat ca keli-kalaham kalahaṃsa-#yugmam śeṣam jale @vada marāla-kula-pramāṇam//
children.translated_text: And a pair of geese making a playful quarrel; tell me the total number of the flock of geese in the water.

body.text: nyāsas/ mūla-guṇakas 7_2/ dṛśyam 2/ dṛṣṭasya asya 2 guṇa-%ardha-kṛtyā 49_16 yuktasya 81_16 mūlam 9_4/ guṇa-%ardhena 7_4 yutam 4/ vargī-kṛtam jātam haṃsa-kula-mānam 16// atha mūla-yute dṛṣṭe tāvat udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: root-multiplier 7/2; visible [remainder] 2. Of this visible 2, augmented by the square of half the factor 49/16, [giving] 81/16, the root is 9/4; increased by half the factor 7/4, [we get] 4; squared, the total number of the flock of geese is 16. Now, an example when the visible [result] is increased by the root:

children.text: sva-padais %navabhis yuktas @syāt %catvāriṃśatā adhikam/
children.translated_text: Increased by nine times its own root, it should be

children.text: %śata-%dvādaśakam vidvan kas sas rāśis @nigadyatām//
children.translated_text: Twelve hundred and forty; O learned one, tell me what that quantity is.

body.text: nyāsas/ mūla-guṇakas 9/ dṛśyam 1240/ ukta-prakāreṇa jātas rāśis 961// udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: root-multiplier 9; visible [result] 1240. By the stated method, the quantity obtained is 961. Example:

children.text: yātam haṃsa-kulasya mūla-%daśakam megha-āgame mānasam @proḍḍīya sthala-padminī-vanam @agāt %aṣṭa-aṃśakas ambhas-taṭāt/
children.translated_text: Ten times the square root of a flock of geese went to Lake <s>Mānasa</s> at the approach of the monsoon; one-eighth flew from the water's edge to a grove of lotuses on land;

children.text: bāle bāla-mṛṇāla-śālini jale keli-kriyā-lālasam dṛṣṭam haṃsa-#yuga-%trayam ca sakalām yūthasya saṃkhyām @vada//
children.translated_text: O girl, three pairs of geese were seen playfully sporting in the water with tender lotus stalks; tell me the total number of the flock.

body.text: nyāsas/ mūla-guṇakas 10/ bhāgas 1_8/ dṛśyam 6/ yadā lavais ca ūna-yutas iti atra %ekena 1 bhāga-ūnena 7_8 dṛśya-mūla-guṇau @bhaktvā jātam dṛśyam 48_7/ mūla-guṇakas 80_7/ ābhyām abhīṣṭam guṇa-ghna-mūla-ūna-yutasya iti-ādi-vidhinā jātam haṃsa-kula-mānam 144// udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: root-multiplier 10; fraction 1/8; visible 6. 'When diminished or increased by fractions'—here, dividing the visible and the root-multiplier by one minus the fraction 7/8, the visible obtained is 48/7; root-multiplier 80/7. From these, by the rule 'of the quantity diminished or increased by its root multiplied by a factor' etc., the total number of the flock of geese obtained is 144. Example:

children.text: pārthas karṇa-vadhāya mārgaṇa-gaṇam kruddhas raṇe @saṃdadhe tasya ardhena @nivārya tad-śara-gaṇam mūlais %caturbhis hayān/
children.translated_text: <s>Arjuna</s>, enraged in battle, assembled a host of arrows for the slaying of <s>Karṇa</s>; with half of them he warded off <s>Karṇa's</s> arrows; with four times the square root [of the total] he [struck] the horses;

children.text: śalyam %ṣaḍbhis atha iṣubhis %tribhis api chatram dhvajam kārmukam @ciccheda asya śiras śareṇa kati te yān arjunas @saṃdadhe//
children.translated_text: With six he [struck] <s>Śalya</s>; with three more arrows he cut down the umbrella, banner, and bow; and with one arrow he severed his head. Tell me how many arrows <s>Arjuna</s> assembled.

body.text: nyāsas/ mūla-guṇakas 4/ bhāgas 1_2/ dṛśyam 10/ yadā lavais ca ūna-yutas iti-ādinā jātam bāṇa-mānam 100// api ca/
body.translated_text: Setting down: root-multiplier 4; fraction 1/2; visible 10. By the [rule] 'when diminished or increased by fractions' etc., the number of arrows obtained is 100. Moreover:

children.text: ali-kula-#dala-mūlam mālatīm yātam %aṣṭau nikhila-%navama-bhāgās cālinī bhṛṅgam %ekam/
children.translated_text: The square root of a swarm of bees, times half, went to a <s>mallikā</s> jasmine; eight-ninths of the whole [went] to a <s>cālinī</s> flower; one bee,

children.text: niśi parimala-lubdham padma-madhye niruddham @pratiraṇati raṇantam @brūhi kānte ali-saṃkhyām//
children.translated_text: Lured by the fragrance at night, was trapped inside a lotus, buzzing in response to the buzzing [of its mate]. O beloved, tell me the number of the swarm of bees.

body.text: atra kila rāśi-%nava-aṃśa-%aṣṭakam rāśi-ardha-mūlam ca rāśes ṛṇam rūpa-%dvayam dṛśyam/ etat ṛṇam dṛśyam ca ardhitam rāśi-%ardhasya @bhavati iti// tathā nyāsas/ mūla-guṇakas -1_2/ bhāgas -8_9/ atra prāk-vat labdham rāśi-dalam 36/ etat dvi-guṇitam ali-kula-mānam 72// bhāga-mūla-yute dṛṣṭe udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Here, eight-ninths of the quantity and the square root of half the quantity are subtracted from the quantity; two units are visible. This visible [result] halved becomes [the equation] for half the quantity. Thus, setting down: root-multiplier -1/2; fraction -8/9. Here, as before, half the quantity obtained is 36; doubled, the total number of the swarm of bees is 72. Example when the visible [result] involves fractional root:

children.text: yas rāśis %aṣṭādaśabhis sva-mūlais rāśi-%tri-bhāgena samanvitas ca/
children.translated_text: A quantity increased by eighteen times its own root and one-third of the quantity

children.text: jātam %śata-%dvādaśakam tam āśu @jānīhi pāṭyām paṭutā @asti te ced//
children.translated_text: Becomes twelve hundred; know it quickly, if you have skill in arithmetic!

body.text: nyāsas/ mūla-guṇakas 18/ bhāgas 1_3/ dṛśyam 1200/ atra %ekena bhāga-yutena 4_3 mūla-guṇam dṛśyam ca @bhaktvā prāk-vat jātas rāśis 576// iti guṇa-karma// atha trairāśike karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: root-multiplier 18; fraction 1/3; visible 1200. Here, dividing the root-multiplier and the visible by one plus the fraction 4/3, as before, the quantity obtained is 576. Thus ends the multiplication operations. Now, a verse as the operational rule for the Rule of Three (<s>trairāśika</s>):

children.text: pramāṇam icchā ca samāna-jātī ādi-antayos tad-phalam anya-jāti/
children.translated_text: The measure (<s>pramāṇa</s>) and the desire (<s>icchā</s>) are of the same kind, [placed] at the beginning and end; the fruit of that [measure] is of a different kind,

children.text: madhye tat icchā-hatam ādya-hṛt @syāt icchā-phalam vyasta-vidhis vilome//
children.translated_text: [Placed] in the middle. That [fruit], multiplied by the desire and divided by the first [measure], gives the desired result. In the inverse [case], the inverse method [is used].

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: kuṅkumasya sa-#dalam pala-%dvayam niṣka-%saptama-lavais %tribhis yadi/
children.translated_text: If two and a half <s>palas</s> (measures of weight) of saffron are obtained for three-sevenths of a <s>niṣka</s> (gold coin),

children.text: @prāpyate sapadi me vaṇij-vara @brūhi niṣka-%navakena tat kiyat//
children.translated_text: Tell me quickly, O best of merchants, how much is obtained for nine <s>niṣkas</s>?

body.text: nyāsas 3_7/ 5_2/ 9_1/ labdhāni kuṅkuma-palāni 52/ karṣau 2// api ca/
body.translated_text: Setting down: 3/7, 5/2, 9/1. The <s>palas</s> of saffron obtained are 52 and 2 <s>karṣas</s>. Moreover:

children.text: prakṛṣṭa-karpūra-pala-%triṣaṣṭyā ced @labhyate niṣka-%catuṣka-yuktam/
children.translated_text: If with sixty-three <s>palas</s> of fine camphor one obtains a hundred

children.text: %śatam tadā %dvādaśabhis sa-#pādais palais kim @ācakṣva sakhe @vicintya//
children.translated_text: Plus four <s>niṣkas</s>, then for twelve and a quarter <s>palas</s>, what [is the price]? Tell me, O friend, having considered.

body.text: nyāsas 63/ 104/ 49_4/ labdhās niṣkās 20/ drammās 3/ paṇās 8/ kākiṇyas 3/ varāṭakās 11/ varāṭaka-bhāgās ca 1_9// api ca/
body.translated_text: Setting down: 63, 104, 49/4. The <s>niṣkas</s> obtained are 20, <s>drammas</s> 3, <s>paṇas</s> 8, <s>kākiṇīs</s> 3, <s>varāṭakas</s> 11, and <s>varāṭaka</s> fractions 1/9. Moreover:

children.text: dramma-%dvayena sa-%aṣṭa-aṃśā śāli-taṇḍula-khārikā/
children.translated_text: If a <s>khārikā</s> (measure) of rice-grain with one-eighth [extra] is obtained

children.text: labhyā ced paṇa-%saptatyā tat kim sapadi @kathyatām//
children.translated_text: For two <s>drammas</s>, then for seventy <s>paṇas</s>, what [is obtained]? Let it be stated at once.

body.text: atra pramāṇasya sajātīya-karaṇa-artham dramma-%dvayasya paṇī-kṛtasya nyāsas 32/ 9_8/ 70/ labdhe khāryau 2/ droṇās 7/ āḍhakas 1/ prasthau 2// atha vyasta-trairāśike karaṇa-sūtram/
body.translated_text: Here, for the purpose of making the measure homogeneous, the two <s>drammas</s> converted to <s>paṇas</s>: setting down 32, 9/8, 70. The result obtained is 2 <s>khārīs</s>, 7 <s>droṇas</s>, 1 <s>āḍhaka</s>, 2 <s>prasthas</s>. Now, the operational rule for inverse Rule of Three:

children.text: icchā-vṛddhau phale hrāsas hrāse vṛddhis ca @jāyate/
children.translated_text: When the desire increases, the result decreases; when it decreases, the result increases—

children.text: vyastam trairāśikam tatra jñeyam gaṇita-kovidais//
children.translated_text: This should be known by those skilled in calculation as the inverse Rule of Three.

body.text: yatra icchā-vṛddhau phale hrāsas hrāse vā phala-vṛddhis tatra vyasta-trairāśikam/ tat yathā/
body.translated_text: Where an increase in the desire [causes] a decrease in the result, or a decrease [causes] an increase in the result—there the inverse Rule of Three [applies]. Namely:

children.text: jīvānām vayasas maulye taulye varṇasya haimane/
children.translated_text: In the pricing of living beings by age, in the assaying of gold by fineness,

children.text: bhāga-hāre ca rāśīnām vyastam trairāśikam @bhavet//
children.translated_text: And in the measuring of quantities by fractional division, the inverse Rule of Three applies.

body.text: jīva-vayas-mūlye udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example for pricing by age of living beings:

children.text: @prāpnoti ced %ṣoḍaśa-vatsarā strī %dvātriṃśatam %viṃśati-vatsarā kim/
children.translated_text: If a sixteen-year-old woman fetches thirty-two [niṣkas], what does a twenty-year-old [fetch]?

children.text: %dvi-dhūs-vahas niṣka-%catuṣkam ukṣā @prāpnoti dhūs-%ṣaṭka-vahas tadā kim//
children.translated_text: If a two-[bhāra]-load-bearing bull [fetches] four <s>niṣkas</s>, then what does a six-load-bearing one [fetch]?

body.text: nyāsas 16/ 32/ 20/ labdham niṣkās 25_3_5// %dvitīya-nyāsas 2/ 4/ 6/ labdham niṣkās 1_1_3// varṇīya-suvarṇa-taulye udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: 16, 32, 20. Result: <s>niṣkas</s> 25 3/5. Second setting down: 2, 4, 6. Result: <s>niṣkas</s> 1 1/3. Example for assaying gold by fineness:

children.text: %daśa-varṇam suvarṇam ced gadyāṇakam @avāpyate/
children.translated_text: If gold of ten <s>varṇas</s> (fineness) yields one <s>gadyāṇaka</s> (a weight)

children.text: niṣkeṇa #tithi-varṇam tu tadā @vada kiyad-mitam//
children.translated_text: Per <s>niṣka</s>, then for gold of fifteen <s>varṇas</s>, tell me how much [is yielded].

body.text: nyāsas 10/ 1/ 15/ labdham 2_3// rāśi-bhāga-haraṇe udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: 10, 1, 15. Result: 2/3. Example for measuring quantities by fractional division:

children.text: %sapta-āḍhakena mānena rāśau sasyasya māpite/
children.translated_text: When grain in a heap is measured with a seven-<s>āḍhaka</s> measure,

children.text: yadi māna-%śatam jātam tadā %pañca-āḍhakena kim//
children.translated_text: If a hundred [measures] are obtained, then with a five-<s>āḍhaka</s> [measure], how many?

body.text: nyāsas 7/ 100/ 5/ labdham 140// iti vyastam trairāśikam// atha %pañca-rāśika-ādau karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: 7, 100, 5. Result: 140. Thus ends the inverse Rule of Three. Now, a verse as the operational rule for the Rule of Five and beyond:

children.text: %pañca-%sapta-%nava-rāśika-ādike anyonya-pakṣa-nayanam phala-chidām/
children.translated_text: In the Rule of Five, Seven, Nine, and so forth, transferring the fruit and its divisors to the opposite side,

children.text: @saṃvidhāya bahu-rāśi-je vadhe su-alpa-rāśi-vadha-bhājite phalam//
children.translated_text: The product of the greater number of quantities, divided by the product of the fewer, gives the result.

body.text: atra uddeśakas/
body.translated_text: Here is the problem:

children.text: māse %śatasya yadi %pañca kalā-antaram @syāt varṣe gate @bhavati kim @vada %ṣoḍaśānām/
children.translated_text: If the interest on a hundred for one month is five, tell me what it would be for sixteen after a year has passed;

children.text: kālam tathā @kathaya mūla-kalā-antarābhyām mūlam dhanam gaṇaka kāla-phale @viditvā//
children.translated_text: Likewise, tell me the time from the principal and interest, and the principal, O calculator, knowing the time and the result.

body.text: nyāsas {btabular} 1 & 12 \\ 100 & 16 \\ 5 & * {etabular} labdham kalā-antaram 9_3_5// atha kāla-jñāna-artham nyāsas {btabular} 1 &* \\ 100 & 16\ \ 5 & 48_5 {etabular} labdhās māsās 12// mūla-dhana-artham nyāsas {btabular} 1 & 12 \\ 100 & * \\ 5 & 48_5 {etabular} labdham mūla-dhanam 16//
body.translated_text: Setting down: [table] 1, 12 / 100, 16 / 5, * [end table]. Result: interest 9 3/5. Now, for finding the time, setting down: [table] 1, * / 100, 16 / 5, 48/5 [end table]. Result: months 12. For finding the principal, setting down: [table] 1, 12 / 100, * / 5, 48/5 [end table]. Result: principal 16.

children.text: sa-%tri-aṃśa-māsena %śatasya ced @syāt kalā-antaram %pañca sa-%pañcama-aṃśās/
children.translated_text: If the interest on a hundred for one-and-a-third months is five and one-fifth,

children.text: māsais %tribhis %pañca-lava-adhikais tat sa-%ardha-%dviṣaṣṭes phalam @ucyatām kim//
children.translated_text: In three months and one-fifth, what is the result for sixty-two and a half?

body.text: nyāsas {btabular} 4_3 & 16_5 \\ 100 & 125_2 \\ 26_5 & * {etabular} labdham kalā-antaram 7_4_5// atha %sapta-rāśika-udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: [table] 4/3, 16/5 / 100, 125/2 / 26/5, * [end table]. Result: interest 7 4/5. Now, an example for the Rule of Seven:

children.text: vistāre %tri-karās kara-%aṣṭaka-mitās dairghye vicitrās ca ced rūpais utkaṭa-paṭṭa-sūtra-paṭikās %aṣṭau @labhante %śatam/
children.translated_text: If cloths of fine silk, three <s>hastas</s> (cubits) wide and eight <s>hastas</s> long, of various [patterns],

children.text: dairghye sa-%ardha-kara-%trayā apara-paṭī hasta-%ardha-vistāriṇī tādṛk kim @labhate drutam @vada vaṇik vāṇijyakam @vetsi ced//
children.translated_text: Eight [such] are obtained for a hundred <s>rūpas</s> (coins), then for another cloth three-and-a-half <s>hastas</s> long and half a <s>hasta</s> wide—of the same kind—what does it fetch? Tell me quickly, O merchant, if you know commerce!

body.text: nyāsas {btabular} 3 & 1_2 \\ 8 & 7_2 \\ 8 & 1 \\ 100 & * {etabular} labdham niṣkās 0/ drammās 14/ paṇās 9/ kākiṇī 1/ varāṭakās 6/ [āpaṭe: varaṭakās] varāṭaka-bhāgau 2_3// atha %nava-rāśika-udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: [table] 3, 1/2 / 8, 7/2 / 8, 1 / 100, * [end table]. Result: <s>niṣkas</s> 0, <s>drammas</s> 14, <s>paṇas</s> 9, <s>kākiṇī</s> 1, <s>varāṭakas</s> 6, <s>varāṭaka</s> fractions 2/3. Now, an example for the Rule of Nine:

children.text: piṇḍe ye #arka-mita-aṅgulās kila %catur-varga-aṅgulās vistṛtau paṭṭās dīrghatayā %caturdaśa-karās %triṃśat @labhante %śatam/
children.translated_text: If cloths of twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> (finger-widths) in roundness, sixteen <s>aṅgulas</s> in breadth, and fourteen <s>hastas</s> in length—thirty [such] are obtained for a hundred;

children.text: etās vistṛti-piṇḍa-dairghya-mitayas yeṣām %catur-varjitās paṭṭās te @vada me %caturdaśa sakhe maulyam @labhante kiyat//
children.translated_text: Those whose measures of breadth, roundness, and length are each diminished by four—tell me, my friend, for fourteen such cloths, what price is obtained?

body.text: nyāsas {btabular} 12 & 8 \\ 16 & 12 \\ 14 & 10 \\ 30 & 14 \\ 100 & * {etabular} labdham mūlyam niṣkās 16_2_3// atha %ekādaśa-rāśika-udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: [table] 12, 8 / 16, 12 / 14, 10 / 30, 14 / 100, * [end table]. Result: price <s>niṣkas</s> 16 2/3. Now, an example for the Rule of Eleven:

children.text: paṭṭās ye %prathama-udita-pramitayas gavyūti-mātre sthitās teṣām ānayanāya ced śakaṭinām dramma-%aṣṭakam bhāṭakam/
children.translated_text: If the freight for carters to carry the cloths of the first-stated dimensions, situated at a distance of one <s>gavyūti</s> (a unit of distance), is eight <s>drammas</s>,

children.text: anye ye tad-anantaram nigaditās mānais %catur-varjitās teṣām kā @bhavati iti bhāṭaka-mitis gavyūti-%ṣaṭke @vada//
children.translated_text: Then for the other [cloths] stated next, whose dimensions are each diminished by four, over a distance of six <s>gavyūtis</s>, tell me what the freight would be.

body.text: nyāsas {btabular} 12 & 8 \\ 16 & 12 \\ 14 & 10 \\ 30 & 14 \\ 1 & 6 \\ 8 & * {etabular} labdhās bhāṭaka-drammās 8// atha bhāṇḍa-pratibhāṇḍake karaṇa-sūtram vṛtta-%ardham/
body.translated_text: Setting down: [table] 12, 8 / 16, 12 / 14, 10 / 30, 14 / 1, 6 / 8, * [end table]. Result: freight <s>drammas</s> 8. Now, a half-verse as the operational rule for barter:

body.text: tathā eva bhāṇḍa-pratibhāṇḍake api viparyayas tatra sadā hi mūlye//
body.translated_text: In barter likewise, but there the inversion is always in the prices.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: drammeṇa @labhyate iha āmra-%śata-%trayam ced %triṃśat-paṇena vipaṇau vara-dāḍimāni/
children.translated_text: If three hundred mangoes are obtained for one <s>dramma</s>, and thirty choice pomegranates for one <s>paṇa</s>,

children.text: āmrais @vada āśu %daśabhis kati dāḍimāni labhyāni tad-vinimayena @bhavanti mitra//
children.translated_text: Tell me quickly, O friend, how many pomegranates are obtained for ten mangoes in exchange for them?

children.text: nyāsas {btabular} 16 & 1 \\ 300 & 30 \\ 10 & * {etabular} labdhāni dāḍimāni 16// iti gaṇita-pāṭyām līlāvatyām prakīrṇakāni//
children.translated_text: Setting down: [table] 16, 1 / 300, 30 / 10, * [end table]. Result: pomegranates 16. Thus ends miscellaneous [problems] in the Līlāvatī, a work on arithmetic.

body.text: miśraka-vyavahāra
body.translated_text: Mixture Problems (<s>Miśraka-vyavahāra</s>)

body.text: atha miśraka-vyavahāre karaṇa-sūtram sa-%ardha-vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Now, a verse-and-a-half as the operational rule for mixture problems:

children.text: pramāṇa-kālena hatam pramāṇam vimiśra-kālena hatam phalam ca/
children.translated_text: The measure (<s>pramāṇa</s>) multiplied by the measure-time, and the fruit multiplied by the mixed-time—

children.text: sva-yoga-bhakte ca pṛthak-sthite te miśra-āhate mūla-kalā-antare @stas/ [āpaṭe: prathak- < pṛthak-]
children.translated_text: Divided by their own sum and set down separately, when multiplied by the mixture, they become the principal and the interest respectively;

children.text: yat vā iṣṭa-karma-ākhya-vidhes tu mūlam miśrāt cyutam tat ca kalā-antaram @syāt//
children.translated_text: Or, the principal [found] by the procedure called the desired-operation, when subtracted from the mixture, gives the interest.

body.text: uddeśakas/
body.translated_text: Problem:

children.text: %pañcakena %śatena abde mūlam svam sakala-antaram/
children.translated_text: At the [rate of] five per hundred per year, the principal together with its total interest

children.text: sahasram ced pṛthak tatra @vada mūla-kalā-antare//
children.translated_text: Is a thousand; separately state the principal and the interest, O calculator.

body.text: nyāsas {btabular} 1 & 12 \\ 100 & 1000 \\ 5 & * {etabular} labdhe krameṇa mūla-kalā-antare 625/ 375// atha vā iṣṭa-karmaṇā kalpitam iṣṭam #rūpam 1/ uddeśaka-ālāpavat iṣṭa-rāśis iti-ādi-karaṇena #rūpasya varṣe kalā-antaram 3_5/ etad-yutena #rūpeṇa 8_5 dṛṣṭe 1000 #rūpa-guṇe bhakte labdham mūla-dhanam 625/ etat miśrāt cyutam kalā-antaram 375// miśra-antare karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: [table] 1, 12 / 100, 1000 / 5, * [end table]. The principal and interest obtained in order are 625 and 375. Or, by the desired-operation, the assumed desired [quantity] is 1. By the rule of the problem-statement 'the desired quantity' etc., the interest of one unit for one year is 3/5; dividing the visible 1000 by one plus this 8/5, the principal obtained is 625; this subtracted from the mixture gives the interest 375. The operational rule for mixed interest is a verse:

children.text: atha pramāṇais guṇitās sva-kālās vyatīta-kāla-ghna-phala-uddhṛtās te/
children.translated_text: Now, the [individual] times multiplied by the [respective] measures, those divided by the product of the elapsed time and the fruit,

children.text: sva-yoga-bhaktās ca vimiśra-nighnās prayukta-khaṇḍāni pṛthak @bhavanti//
children.translated_text: And divided by their own sum and multiplied by the mixed [total], give the individually invested portions separately.

body.text: uddeśakas/
body.translated_text: Problem:

children.text: yat %pañcaka-%trika-%catuṣka-%śatena dattam khaṇḍais %tribhis gaṇaka niṣka-%śatam %ṣaṣ-ūnam/
children.translated_text: What was given in three installments, O calculator, at [rates of] five, three, and four per hundred per [year]?—<s>niṣkas</s> one hundred less six,

children.text: māseṣu %sapta-%daśa-%pañcasu tulyam āptam khaṇḍa-%traye api hi phalam @vada khaṇḍa-saṃkhyām//
children.translated_text: In seven, ten, and five months [respectively]; equal interest being obtained in all three installments, tell me the amounts of the installments.

body.text: nyāsas {btabular} 1 & 7 & 1 & 10 & 1 & 5 \\ 100 & * & 100 & * & 100 * \\ 5 & * & 3 & * & 4 & * {etabular} miśra-dhanam 94/ sva-yogas 235_21/ [āpaṭe: sva-yogas 235_21/ miśra-dhanam 94/] labdhāni yathā-kramam khaṇḍāni 24/ 28/ 42/ %pañca-rāśi-vidhinā labdham sama-kalā-antaram 8_2_5// atha miśra-antare karaṇa-sūtram vṛtta-%ardham/
body.translated_text: Setting down: [table] 1, 7, 1, 10, 1, 5 / 100, *, 100, *, 100, * / 5, *, 3, *, 4, * [end table]. Mixed capital 94; own sum 235/21. The installments obtained in order are 24, 28, 42. By the Rule of Five, the equal interest obtained is 8 2/5. Now, a half-verse as the operational rule for mixed interest:

children.text: prakṣepakās miśra-hatās vibhaktās prakṣepa-yogeṇa pṛthak phalāni//
children.translated_text: The contributed amounts, multiplied by the mixture and divided by the sum of the contributions, give the individual results.

body.text: atra uddeśakas/
body.translated_text: Here is the problem:

children.text: %pañcāśat %eka-sahitā gaṇaka %aṣṭaṣaṣṭis %pañca-ūnitā %navatis ādi-dhanāni yeṣām/
children.translated_text: Fifty-one, sixty-eight minus five, and ninety, O calculator, are the initial capitals of those

children.text: prāptā vimiśrita-dhanais %triśatī %tribhis tais vāṇijyatas @vada @vibhajya dhanāni teṣām//
children.translated_text: Who obtained three hundred and three as mixed profit through commerce; tell me, having apportioned, their individual profits.

body.text: nyāsas 51/ 68/ 85/ miśra-dhanam 300/ jātāni dhanāni 75/ 100/ 125/ etāni ādi-dhanais ūnāni lābhās 24/ 32/ 40// atha vā miśra-dhanam 300/ ādi-dhana-aikyena 204 ūnam sarva-lābha-yogas 96/ asmin prakṣepa-guṇite prakṣepa-yoga-bhakte lābhās @bhavanti 24/ 32/ 40// vāpī-ādi-pūraṇe karaṇa-sūtram vṛtta-%ardham/
body.translated_text: Setting down: 51/ 68/ 85/ The mixed capital is 300/ The resulting capitals are 75/ 100/ 125/ These, diminished by the original capitals, give the profits 24/ 32/ 40// Alternatively: the mixed capital 300/ diminished by the sum of original capitals 204, gives the total profit 96/ When this is multiplied by the respective contributions and divided by the sum of contributions, the profits are 24/ 32/ 40// For filling a cistern and the like, the rule of operation in half a verse:

body.text: @bhajet chidas aṃśais atha tais vimiśrais #rūpam @bhajet @syāt paripūrti-kālas//
body.translated_text: Divide unity by the [respective] parts of the opening; then divide unity by those [parts] combined—that will be the time of complete filling.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: ye nirjharās dina-dina-%ardha-%tṛtīya-%ṣaṣṭhais @saṃpūrayanti hi pṛthak pṛthak eva muktās/
children.translated_text: The streams that, released separately, fill a cistern in one day, half a day, a third of a day, and a sixth of a day respectively,

children.text: vāpīm yadā yugapad eva sakhe vimuktās te kena vāsara-lavena tadā @vada āśu//
children.translated_text: when released simultaneously, O friend, in what fraction of a day do they [fill it]? Tell me quickly!

body.text: nyāsas 1_1/ 1_2/ 1_3/ 1_6/ labdhas vāpī-pūraṇa-kālas dina-aṃśas 1_12// kraya-vikraye karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: 1/1, 1/2, 1/3, 1/6/ The obtained time for filling the cistern is the fraction of a day: 1/12// For purchase and sale, the rule of operation in a verse:

children.text: paṇyais sva-mūlyāni @bhajet sva-bhāgais @hatvā tad-aikyena @bhajet ca tāni/
children.translated_text: Divide the respective prices by the commodities, and multiply by their respective shares; then divide those by the sum of those [results].

children.text: bhāgān ca miśreṇa dhanena @hatvā mūlyāni paṇyāni yathā-kramam @syus// [āpaṭe: krama < kramam]
children.translated_text: And having multiplied the shares by the mixed amount of money, the prices and commodities will be obtained in order.

body.text: uddeśakas/
body.translated_text: An example:

children.text: sa-%ardham taṇḍula-mānaka-%trayam aho drammeṇa māna-%aṣṭakam mudgānām ca yadi %trayodaśa-mitās etās vaṇik kākiṇīs/
