children.translated_text: If three and a half measures of rice [are obtained] for one <s>dramma</s>, and eight measures of <s>mudga</s> (green gram) for one [<s>dramma</s>], and these are thirteen <s>kākiṇī</s>s, O merchant,

children.text: @ādāya @arpaya taṇḍula-aṃśa-#yugalam mudga-%eka-bhāga-anvitam kṣipram kṣipra-bhujas @vrajema hi yatas sa-arthas agratas @yāsyati//
children.translated_text: taking [that money], give two parts of rice combined with one part of <s>mudga</s>—quickly, O swift-handed one, let us go, for he who has business will proceed ahead!

body.text: nyāsas/ mūlye 1/ 1/ paṇye 7_2/ 8_1/ sva-bhāgau 2_1/ 1_1/ miśra-dhanam 13_64/ atra mūlye sva-bhāga-guṇite paṇyābhyām bhakte jāte 4_7/ 1_8/ anayos yogena 39_56/ ete 4_7/ 1_8 bhāgau ca 1_2/ 1_1/ miśra-dhanena 13_64/ @saṃguṇya bhakte jāte taṇḍula-muḍga-mūlye 1_6/ 7_192/ tathā taṇḍula-mudga-māne bhāgau 7_12/ 7_24/ atra taṇḍula-mūlye paṇau 2 kākiṇyau < 2 varāṭakās 13/ varāṭaka-bhāgas ca 1_3/ mudga-mūlye [āpaṭe: mūdga- < mudga-] kākiṇyau 2/ varāṭakās 6/ varāṭaka-bhāgau ca 2_3// udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: prices 1/ 1/ commodities 7/2, 8/1/ respective shares 2/1, 1/1/ mixed amount 13/64/ Here, when the prices multiplied by respective shares are divided by the commodities, the results are 4/7, 1/8/ The sum of these is 39/56/ These 4/7, 1/8 and the shares 1/2, 1/1, multiplied by the mixed amount 13/64 and divided, give the prices of rice and <s>mudga</s>: 1/6, 7/192/ Likewise the measures of rice and <s>mudga</s> are the shares 7/12, 7/24/ Here the rice price is 2 <s>paṇa</s>s, 2 <s>kākiṇī</s>s, 13 <s>varāṭaka</s>s, and 1/3 of a <s>varāṭaka</s>/ The <s>mudga</s> price is 2 <s>kākiṇī</s>s, 6 <s>varāṭaka</s>s, and 2/3 of a <s>varāṭaka</s>// Example:

children.text: karpūrasya varasya niṣka-#yugalena %ekam palam @prāpyate vaiśyā-nandana candanasya ca palam dramma-%aṣṭa-bhāgena ced/
children.translated_text: If one <s>pala</s> of fine camphor is obtained for two <s>niṣka</s>s, O son of a merchant, and one <s>pala</s> of sandalwood for one-eighth of a <s>dramma</s>,

children.text: %aṣṭa-aṃśena tathā agaros pala-#dalam niṣkeṇa me @dehi tān bhāgais %ekaka-%ṣoḍaśa-%aṣṭaka-mitais dhūpam @cikīrṣāmi aham//
children.translated_text: and likewise half a <s>pala</s> of aloe-wood for one <s>niṣka</s>, give me those in portions measuring one, sixteen, and eight respectively—I wish to prepare incense!

body.text: nyāsas/ mūlyāni drammās 32_1/ 1_8/ 1_8/ paṇyāni 1_1/ 1_1/ 1_2/ bhāgās 1_1/ 16_1/ 8_1/ miśra-dhanam drammās 16/ labdhāni karpūra-ādīnām mūlyāni 2_9/ 8_9/ 8_9/ tathā teṣām paṇyāni 4_9/ 64_9/ 32_9// ratna-miśre karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: prices in <s>dramma</s>s 32/1, 1/8, 1/8/ commodities 1/1, 1/1, 1/2/ shares 1/1, 16/1, 8/1/ mixed amount in <s>dramma</s>s: 16/ The obtained prices of camphor and the rest are 2/9, 8/9, 8/9/ Likewise their quantities are 4/9, 64/9, 32/9// For the mixture of gems, the rule of operation in a verse:

children.text: nara-ghna-dāna-ūnita-ratna-śeṣais iṣṭe hṛte @syus khalu mūlya-saṃkhyās/
children.translated_text: When the remainder of gems, after subtracting the product of [the number of] persons and the gift, is divided by the desired [number], the price-values are obtained.

children.text: śeṣais hṛte śeṣa-vadhe pṛthak-sthais abhinna-mūlyāni atha vā @bhavanti//
children.translated_text: When divided by the remainders, with the products of the separately placed remainders, the non-fractional prices are obtained alternatively.

body.text: atra uddeśakas/
body.translated_text: Here an example:

children.text: māṇikya-%aṣṭakam indranīla-%daśakam muktāphalānām %śatam sad-vajrāṇi ca %pañca ratna-vaṇijām yeṣām %caturṇām dhanam/
children.translated_text: Eight rubies, ten sapphires, a hundred pearls, and five fine diamonds—these belong to four gem-merchants whose wealth,

children.text: saṅga-sneha-vaśena te nija-dhanāt @dattvā %ekam %ekam mithas jātās tulya-dhanās pṛthak @vada sakhe tad-ratna-mūlyāni me//
children.translated_text: out of affection and friendship, each having given one [gem] to each of the others from his own stock, they became equal in wealth. Tell me separately, O friend, the prices of those gems!

body.text: nyāsas mā 8/ nī 10/ mu 100/ va 5/ dānam 1/ narās 4/ nara-guṇita-dānena 4 ratna-saṃkhyāsu ūnitāsu śeṣāṇi mā 4/ nī 6/ mu 96/ va 1/ etais iṣṭa-rāśau bhakte ratna-mūlyāni @syus iti// tāni ca yathā-katham-cit iṣṭe kalpite abhinnāni/ atas atra iṣṭam tathā sudhiyā @kalpyate yathā abhinnāni iti/ tathā iṣṭam kalpitam 96/ atas jātāni mūlyāni 24/ 16/ 1/ 96/ sama-dhanam 233/ atha vā śeṣāṇām vadhe 2304 pṛthak śeṣais bhakte jātāni abhinnāni 596/ 384/ 24/ 2304/ janānām %caturṇām tulya-dhanam 5592/ teṣām ete drammās @saṃbhāvyante// atha suvarṇa-gaṇite karaṇa-sūtram/
body.translated_text: Setting down: rubies 8/ sapphires 10/ pearls 100/ diamonds 5/ gift 1/ persons 4/ When diminished from the gem-counts by the gift multiplied by the number of persons (4), the remainders are: rubies 4/ sapphires 6/ pearls 96/ diamonds 1/ When a chosen quantity is divided by these, the gem-prices result// And these should be non-fractional for some chosen value; therefore here the intelligent person should choose such a value that they are non-fractional// Thus the chosen value is 96/ Therefore the obtained prices are 24/ 16/ 1/ 96/ The equal wealth is 233// Alternatively, when the product of the remainders 2304 is divided separately by the remainders, the non-fractional results are 596/ 384/ 24/ 2304/ The equal wealth of the four persons is 5592/ These are considered as <s>dramma</s>s// Now for gold computation, the rule of operation:

children.text: suvarṇa-varṇa-āhati-yoga-rāśau svarṇa-aikya-bhakte kanaka-aikya-varṇas/
children.translated_text: When the sum of the products of the gold [quantities] and their purities is divided by the total of gold [quantities], the purity of the combined gold [is obtained].

children.text: varṇas @bhavet śodhita-hema-bhakte varṇa-uddhṛte śodhita-hema-saṃkhyā//
children.translated_text: The purity is obtained when divided by the refined gold; the quantity of refined gold is [obtained] when the purity is extracted.

body.text: udāharaṇāni/
body.translated_text: Examples:

children.text: #viśva-#arka-#rudra-%daśa-varṇa-suvarṇa-māṣās #diś-#veda-#locana-#yuga-pramitās krameṇa/
children.translated_text: Gold pieces of purities thirteen, twelve, eleven, and ten <s>varṇa</s>s, with quantities of ten, four, two, and four <s>māṣa</s>s respectively,

children.text: āvartiteṣu @vada teṣu suvarṇa-varṇas tūrṇam suvarṇa-gaṇita-jña vaṇik @bhavet kas//
children.translated_text: when they are melted together, tell quickly, O knower of gold computation, what will be the purity of the [combined] gold, O merchant?

children.text: te śodhane yadi ca %viṃśatis ukta-māṣās @syus %ṣoḍaśa āśu @vada varṇa-mitis tadā kā/
children.translated_text: And if those are refined and twenty <s>māṣa</s>s become sixteen, tell quickly what the purity is then.

children.text: ced śodhitam @bhavati %ṣoḍaśa-varṇa-hema te %viṃśatis kati @bhavanti tadā tu māṣās//
children.translated_text: If the refined [gold] becomes sixteen-<s>varṇa</s> gold, how many <s>māṣa</s>s will those twenty become?

body.text: nyāsas {btabular} 13 & 12 & 11 & 10 \\ 10 & 4 & 2 & 4 {etabular} jātā āvartite suvarṇa-varṇa-mitis 12/ ete eva yadi śodhitās santas %ṣoḍaśa māṣās @bhavanti tadā varṇās 15/ yadi te ca %ṣoḍaśa varṇās tadā %pañcadaśa māṣās @bhavanti 15// atha varṇa-jñānāya karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: {table: purities 13, 12, 11, 10; quantities 10, 4, 2, 4} The obtained purity of the combined gold is 12/ If these same [quantities], when refined, become sixteen <s>māṣa</s>s, then the purity is 15/ And if those are sixteen <s>varṇa</s>s, then fifteen <s>māṣa</s>s result: 15// Now for determining purity, the rule of operation in a verse:

children.text: svarṇa-aikya-nighnāt yuti-jāta-varṇāt suvarṇa-tad-varṇa-vadha-aikya-hīnāt/
children.translated_text: From the total gold multiplied by the purity obtained from combining, diminished by the sum of the products of [known] golds and their purities,

children.text: ajñāta-varṇa-agni-ja-saṃkhyayā āptam ajñāta-varṇasya @bhavet pramāṇam//
children.translated_text: divided by the quantity of gold whose purity is unknown, one obtains the measure of the unknown purity.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: %daśa-#īśa-varṇās #vasu-#netra-māṣās ajñāta-varṇasya ṣaṭ etad-aikye/
children.translated_text: [Golds] of purities ten and eleven, of quantities eight and two <s>māṣa</s>s, together with six [<s>māṣa</s>s] of unknown purity,

children.text: jātam sakhe %dvādaśakam suvarṇam ajñāta-varṇasya @vada pramāṇam//
children.translated_text: the combined gold, O friend, turns out to be twelve [<s>varṇa</s>]. Tell the measure of the unknown purity!

body.text: nyāsas/ {btabular} 10 & 11 & 0 \\ 8 & 2 & 6 {etabular} labdha-jñāta-varṇa-mānam 15// atha suvarṇa-jñānāya karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: {table: purities 10, 11, 0; quantities 8, 2, 6} The obtained measure of the unknown purity is 15// Now for determining the gold [quantity], the rule of operation in a verse:

children.text: svarṇa-aikya-nighnas yuti-jāta-varṇas svarṇa-ghna-varṇa-aikya-viyojitas ca/
children.translated_text: The purity obtained from combining, multiplied by the total gold, diminished by the sum of the products of [known] golds and purities,

children.text: ahema-varṇa-agni-ja-yoga-varṇa-viśleṣa-bhaktas avidita-agni-jam @syāt//
children.translated_text: divided by the difference between the combined purity and the purity of the unknown gold—that gives the unknown gold [quantity].

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: %daśa-#indra-varṇās #guṇa-#candra-māṣās kiṃcit tathā %ṣoḍaśakasya teṣām/
children.translated_text: [Golds] of purities ten and fourteen, of quantities three and one <s>māṣa</s>s, and some [amount] of sixteen [<s>varṇa</s>],

children.text: jātam yutau %dvādaśakam suvarṇam kati iha te %ṣoḍaśa-varṇa-māṣās//
children.translated_text: the combination yielding twelve [<s>varṇa</s>] gold—how many are those sixteen-<s>varṇa</s> <s>māṣa</s>s here?

body.text: nyāsas {btabular} 10 & 14 & 16 \\ 3 & 1 & 0 {etabular} labdham māṣa-mānam 1// atha suvarṇa-jñānāya anyat karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: {table: purities 10, 14, 16; quantities 3, 1, 0} The obtained measure in <s>māṣa</s>s is 1// Now another rule of operation for determining gold, in a verse:

children.text: sādhyena ūnas analpa-varṇas vidheyas sādhyas varṇas svalpa-varṇa-ūnitas ca/
children.translated_text: The higher purity diminished by the desired [purity] should be set down, and the desired purity diminished by the lower purity;

children.text: iṣṭa-kṣuṇṇe śeṣake svarṇa-māne @syātām svalpa-analpayos varṇayos te//
children.translated_text: when multiplied by a chosen [number], the remainders give the gold measures for the lower and higher purities respectively.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: hāṭaka-guṭike %ṣoḍaśa-%daśa-varṇe tad-yutau sakhe jātam/
children.translated_text: Two gold pellets of sixteen and ten <s>varṇa</s>s—when combined, O friend, the result is

children.text: %dvādaśa-varṇa-suvarṇam @brūhi tayos svarṇa-māne me//
children.translated_text: twelve-<s>varṇa</s> gold. Tell me the gold measures of the two!

body.text: nyāsas 16/ 10/ sādhyas varṇas 12/ kalpitam iṣṭam 1/ labdhe suvarṇa-māne {btabular} 16 & 10 \\ 2 & 4 {etabular} atha vā %dvikena iṣṭena {btabular} 16 & 10 \\ 4 & 8 {etabular} %ardha-guṇitena vā {btabular} 16 & 10 \\ 1 & 2 {etabular} evam bahudhā// atha chandas-citi-ādau karaṇa-sūtram śloka-%trayam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: 16/ 10/ desired purity 12/ chosen number 1/ The obtained gold measures: {table: 16, 10; quantities 2, 4}. Or with chosen number 2: {table: 16, 10; quantities 4, 8}. Or with half: {table: 16, 10; quantities 1, 2}. Thus in many ways// Now for prosodic enumeration and the like, the rule of operation in three verses:

children.text: %eka-ādi-eka-uttarās aṅkās vyastās bhājyās krama-sthitais/
children.translated_text: The numbers beginning with one, increasing by one, reversed, should be divided by those in direct order;

children.text: paras pūrveṇa saṃguṇyas tad-paras tena tena ca//
children.translated_text: each succeeding [quotient] is multiplied by the preceding, and the next by that, and so on.

children.text: %eka-%dvi-%tri-ādi-bhedās @syus idam sādhāraṇam smṛtam/
children.translated_text: The results will be the varieties having one, two, three, and so forth [of a given element]. This is stated to be the general [rule].

children.text: chandas-citi-uttare chandasi upayogas asya tad-vidām//
children.translated_text: Its application in prosodic enumeration and further [topics of] prosody is [known] to experts in that [field].

children.text: mūṣā-vahana-bheda-ādau khaṇḍa-merau ca śilpake/
children.translated_text: In [problems of] crucible-loads, varieties [of taste], and the like, in the truncated <s>Meru</s> (Pascal's triangle) in architecture,

children.text: vaidyake rasa-bhedīye tat na uktam vistṛtes bhayāt//
children.translated_text: and in medicine for the classification of <s>rasa</s>s (flavors)—that is not stated [here] for fear of prolixity.

body.text: tatra chandas-citi-uttare kiṃcit udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Here, some examples in prosodic enumeration and further [topics]:

children.text: prastāre mitra gāyatryās @syus pāde vyaktayas kati/
children.translated_text: O friend, in the expansion of <s>Gāyatrī</s>, how many varieties are there in a quarter-verse?

children.text: %eka-ādi-guravas ca āśu kati kati @ucyatām pṛthak//
children.translated_text: And how many having one and more heavy syllables respectively? Tell quickly, each separately!

body.text: iha hi %ṣaṣ-akṣaras gāyatrī-caraṇas/ atas %ṣaṣ-antānām %eka-ādi-%eka-uttara-aṅkānām vyastānām krama-sthānām ca nyāsas {btabular} 6 & 5 & 4 & 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 & 6 {etabular} yathā-ukta-karaṇena labdhās %eka-guru-vyaktayas 6/ %dvi-guravas 15/ %tri-guravas 20/ %catur-guravas 15/ %pañca-guravas 6/ %ṣaṣ-gurus 1/ atha %ekas sarva-laghus 1/ evam āsām aikyam pāda-vyakti-mitis 64// evam %catur-caraṇa-akṣara-saṃkhyakān yathā-uktam @vinyasya %eka-ādi-guru-bhedān @ānīya tān sa-%ekān @%ekī-kṛtya jātās gāyatrī-vṛtta-vyakti-saṃkhyās 16777216// evam ukthā-ādi-utkṛti-paryantam chandasām vyakti-mitis jñātavyā// udāharaṇam śilpe/
body.translated_text: Here, the <s>Gāyatrī</s> quarter-verse has six syllables. Therefore, the setting down of the numbers from one to six, reversed and in direct order: {table: 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1; 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}. By the stated operation, the obtained varieties with one heavy syllable are 6/ with two heavy: 15/ with three heavy: 20/ with four heavy: 15/ with five heavy: 6/ with six heavy: 1/ And one all-light: 1/ Thus the total of these, the number of quarter-verse varieties, is 64// Similarly, by setting down the syllable-counts of the four quarter-verses as stated and obtaining the varieties with one and more heavy [syllables], adding one to each and combining them, the obtained number of <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter varieties is 16777216// Thus the number of varieties of meters from <s>Ukthā</s> and others up to <s>Utkṛti</s> should be known// An example in architecture:

children.text: %eka-%dvi-%tri-ādi-mūṣā-vahana-mitim aho @brūhi me bhūmi-bhartus harmye ramye %aṣṭa-mūṣe catura-viracite ślakṣṇa-śālā-viśāle/
children.translated_text: Tell me the number of crucible-loads of one, two, three, and so forth, O [servant] of the king of the earth, in the beautiful palace with eight crucibles, skillfully constructed, in the smooth and spacious hall!

children.text: %eka-%dvi-%tri-ādi-yuktās madhura-kaṭu-kaṣāya-āmlaka-kṣāra-tiktais ekasmin %ṣaṣ-rasais @syus gaṇaka kati @vada vyañjane vyakti-bhedās//
children.translated_text: And with combinations of one, two, three, and more of the six <s>rasa</s>s (flavors)—sweet, pungent, astringent, sour, saline, and bitter—in a single dish, O calculator, tell how many distinct varieties of condiment there are!

body.text: mūṣā-nyāsas {btabular} 8 & 7 & 6 & 5 & 4 & 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 & 6 & 7 & 8 {etabular} labdhās %eka-%dvi-%tri-ādi-mūṣā-vahana-saṃkhyās {btabular} 8 & 28 & 56 & 70 & 56 & 28 & 8 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 & 6 & 7 & 8 {etabular} evam %aṣṭa-mūṣe rāja-gṛhe mūṣā-vahana-bhedās 255// atha %dvitīya-udāharaṇam/ nyāsas {btabular} 6 & 5 & 4 & 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 & 6 {etabular} labdhās %eka-ādi-rasa-saṃyogena pṛthak vyaktayas/ {btabular} 6 & 15 & 20 & 15 & 6 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 & 6 {etabular} etāsām aikyam sarva-bhedās 63// iti miśra-vyavahāras samāptas//
body.translated_text: Setting down for crucibles: {table: 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1; 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8}. The obtained numbers of crucible-loads of one, two, three, and so forth: {table: 8, 28, 56, 70, 56, 28, 8, 1; 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8}. Thus in the eight-crucible royal palace, the varieties of crucible-loads are 255// Now the second example: Setting down: {table: 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1; 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}. The obtained varieties separately by combination of one and more flavors: {table: 6, 15, 20, 15, 6, 1; 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}. The total of these, all varieties, is 63// Thus the section on mixture-problems (<s>miśra-vyavahāra</s>) is concluded//

body.text: śreḍhī-vyavahāra
body.translated_text: Section on Arithmetic Series

body.text: atha śreḍhī-vyavahāras// tatra saṃkalita-aikye karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Now the section on arithmetic series (<s>śreḍhī-vyavahāra</s>)// Therein, for the sum of summations, the rule of operation in a verse:

children.text: sa-%eka-pada-ghna-pada-%ardham atha %eka-ādi-aṅka-yutis kila saṃkalita-ākhyā/
children.translated_text: Half the product of the number of terms and the number of terms plus one—that is indeed the sum called <s>saṃkalita</s> (summation) of numbers beginning with one.

children.text: sā %dvi-yutena padena vinighnī @syāt %tri-hṛtā khalu saṃkalita-aikyam//
children.translated_text: That, multiplied by the number of terms plus two, and divided by three, will be the sum of summations (<s>saṃkalita-aikya</s>).

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: %eka-ādīnām %nava-antānām pṛthak saṃkalitāni me/
children.translated_text: The individual summations of [sequences] beginning with one and ending with [each of the numbers up to] nine,

children.text: teṣām saṃkalita-aikyāni @pracakṣva gaṇaka drutam//
children.translated_text: and the sums of those summations—declare them quickly, O calculator!

body.text: nyāsas {btabular} * & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 & 6 & 7 & 8 & 9 \\ saṃkalitāni & 1 & 3 & 6 & 10 & 15 & 21 & 28 & 36 & 45 \\ eṣām aikyāni & 1 & 4 & 10 & 20 & 35 & 56 & 84 & 120 & 165 {etabular} kṛti-ādi-yoge karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: {table: terms 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9; summations 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, 28, 36, 45; sums of summations 1, 4, 10, 20, 35, 56, 84, 120, 165}. For the sum of squares and so forth, the rule of operation in a verse:

children.text: %dvi-ghna-padam #ku-yutam %tri-vibhaktam saṃkalitena hatam kṛti-yogas/
children.translated_text: The number of terms multiplied by two, increased by one, divided by three, and multiplied by the summation—that is the sum of squares.

children.text: saṃkalitasya kṛtes samam %eka-ādi-aṅka-ghana-aikyam udāhṛtam ādyais//
children.translated_text: The sum of cubes of numbers beginning with one is declared by the ancients to be equal to the square of the summation.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: teṣām eva ca varga-aikyam ghana-aikyam ca @vada drutam/
children.translated_text: Tell quickly the sum of squares and the sum of cubes of those same [numbers],

children.text: kṛti-saṃkalanā-mārge kuśalā yadi te matis//
children.translated_text: if your mind is skilled in the method of summing squares!

body.text: nyāsas {btabular} * & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 & 6 & 7 & 8 & 9 \\ varga-aikyam & 1 & 5 & 14 & 30 & 55 & 91 & 140 & 204 & 285 \\ ghana-aikyam & 1 & 9 & 36 & 100 & 225 & 441 & 784 & 1296 & 2025 {etabular} yathā-uttara-caye antya-ādi-dhana-jñānāya karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: {table: terms 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9; sum of squares 1, 5, 14, 30, 55, 91, 140, 204, 285; sum of cubes 1, 9, 36, 100, 225, 441, 784, 1296, 2025}. For finding the last term and other quantities in an arithmetic progression with a given common difference, the rule of operation in a verse:

children.text: vi-%eka-pada-ghna-cayas mukha-yuk @syāt antya-dhanam mukha-yuk dalitam tat/
children.translated_text: The common difference multiplied by the number of terms less one, plus the first term, will be the last term. That, plus the first term, halved,

children.text: madhya-dhanam pada-saṃguṇitam tat sarva-dhanam gaṇitam ca tat uktam//
children.translated_text: is the middle term. That multiplied by the number of terms is the total sum, and that is called the <s>gaṇita</s> (computed total).

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: ādye dine dramma-%catuṣṭayam yas @dattvā dvijebhyas anu-dinam pravṛttas/
children.translated_text: One who, having given four <s>dramma</s>s to <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s on the first day, continued giving daily

children.text: dātum sakhe %pañca-cayena pakṣe drammās @vada drāk kati tena dattās//
children.translated_text: with an increment of five—O friend, tell quickly how many <s>dramma</s>s were given by him in a fortnight!

body.text: nyāsas/ ā 4/ ca 5/ ga 15/ madhya-dhanam 39/ antya-dhanam 74/ sarva-dhanam 575// udāharaṇa-antaram/
body.translated_text: Setting down: first term 4/ common difference 5/ number of terms 15/ middle term 39/ last term 74/ total sum 575// Another example:

children.text: ādis %sapta cayas %pañca gacchas %aṣṭau yatra tatra me/
children.translated_text: Where the first term is seven, the common difference is five, and the number of terms is eight,

children.text: madhya-antya-dhana-saṃkhye ke @vada sarva-dhanam ca kim//
children.translated_text: what are the middle term and last term values? Tell me, and what is the total sum?

body.text: nyāsas/ ā 7/ ca 5/ ga 8/ madhya-dhanam 49_2/ antya-dhanam 42/ sarva-dhanam 196// sama-dine gacche madhya-dina-abhāvāt madhyāt prāk-apara-dina-dhanayos yoga-%ardham madhya-dina-dhanam @bhavitum @arhati iti pratītis utpādyā// mukha-jñānāya karaṇa-sūtram vṛtta-%ardham/
body.translated_text: Setting down: first term 7/ common difference 5/ number of terms 8/ middle term 49/2/ last term 42/ total sum 196// When the number of terms is even, since there is no actual middle day, the understanding should be developed that the average of the values of the days before and after the midpoint serves as the middle-day value// For finding the first term, the rule of operation in half a verse:

body.text: gaccha-hṛte gaṇite vadanam @syāt vi-%eka-pada-ghna-caya-%ardha-vihīne//
body.translated_text: The computed total divided by the number of terms, diminished by half the common difference multiplied by the number of terms less one, gives the first term.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: %pañca-adhikam %śatam śreḍhī-phalam %sapta padam kila/
children.translated_text: The sum of the series is one hundred and five, the number of terms is seven,

children.text: cayam %trayam vayam @vidmas vadanam @vada nandana//
children.translated_text: the common difference is three — we know these; tell us the first term, O child!

body.text: nyāsas/ ā 0/ ca 3/ ga 7/ dha 105/ ādi-dhanam 6/ antya-dhanam 24/ madhya-dhanam 15// caya-jñānāya karaṇa-sūtram vṛtta-%ardham/
body.translated_text: Setting down: first term 0/ common difference 3/ number of terms 7/ total sum 105/ first term 6/ last term 24/ middle term 15// For finding the common difference, the rule of operation in half a verse:

body.text: gaccha-hṛtam dhanam ādi-vihīnam vi-%eka-pada-%ardha-hṛtam ca cayas @syāt//
body.translated_text: The total sum divided by the number of terms, diminished by the first term, divided by half the number of terms less one — that will be the common difference.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: %prathamam @agamat ahnā yojane yas jana-īśas tad-anu nanu kayā asau @brūhi yātas adhva-vṛddhyā/
children.translated_text: A king who on the first day marched one <s>yojana</s>, then with what daily increment of the march, tell me,

children.text: ari-kari-haraṇa-artham yojanānām %aśītyā ripu-nagaram avāptas %sapta-rātreṇa dhīman//
children.translated_text: did he, for the purpose of seizing the enemy's elephants, reach the enemy's city of eighty <s>yojanas</s> in seven nights, O wise one?

body.text: nyāsas/ ā 2/ ca 0/ ga 7/ dha 80/ labdham uttaram 22_7/ antya-dhanam 146_7/ madhya-dhanam 80_7// gaccha-jñānāya karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: first term 2/ common difference 0/ number of terms 7/ total sum 80/ obtained common difference 22/7/ last term 146/7/ middle term 80/7// For finding the number of terms, the rule of operation in a verse:

children.text: śreḍhī-phalāt uttara-#locana-ghnāt caya-%ardha-vaktra-antara-varga-yuktāt/
children.translated_text: From the total sum multiplied by eight times the common difference, plus the square of the difference between half the common difference and the first term,

children.text: mūlam mukha-ūnam caya-#khaṇḍa-yuktam caya-uddhṛtam gaccham @udāharanti//
children.translated_text: the root, diminished by the first term, increased by half the common difference, divided by the common difference — that, they declare, is the number of terms.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: dramma-%trayam yas %prathame ahni @dattvā @dātum pravṛttas %dvi-cayena tena/
children.translated_text: One who, having given three <s>drammas</s> on the first day, continued giving with an increment of two —

children.text: %śata-%trayam %ṣaṣṭi-adhikam dvijebhyas dattam kiyadbhis divasais @vada āśu//
children.translated_text: by him, three hundred and sixty was given to <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>; in how many days? Tell quickly!

body.text: nyāsas/ ā 3/ ca 2/ ga 0/ dha 360/ antya-dhanam 37/ madhya-dhanam 20/ labdhas gacchas 18// atha %dvi-guṇa-uttara-ādi-phala-ānayane karaṇa-sūtram sa-%ardhā āryā/
body.translated_text: Setting down: first term 3/ common difference 2/ number of terms 0/ total sum 360/ last term 37/ middle term 20/ obtained number of terms 18// Now, for finding the sum of a geometric progression, the rule of operation in one and a half <s>āryā</s> verses:

children.text: viṣame gacche vi-%eke guṇakas sthāpyas same ardhite vargas/
children.translated_text: When the number of terms is odd, minus one, the multiplier is to be set down; when even, halved, the square [is set down].

children.text: gaccha-kṣaya-antam antyāt vyastam guṇa-varga-jam phalam yat tat/
children.translated_text: This is done repeatedly until the number of terms is exhausted; starting from the last, in reverse order, the product of the multipliers and squares gives the result.

children.text: vi-%ekam vi-%eka-guṇa-uddhṛtam ādi-guṇam @syāt guṇa-uttare gaṇitam//
children.translated_text: Minus one, divided by the common ratio minus one, multiplied by the first term — that will be the total in a geometric progression.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: pūrvam varāṭaka-yugam yena %dvi-guṇa-uttaram pratijñātam/
children.translated_text: One who at first [gave] two <s>varāṭakas</s> [and] pledged to give with double the increment each day,

children.text: prati-aham arthi-janāya sas māse niṣkān @dadāti kati//
children.translated_text: how many <s>niṣkas</s> does he give in a month?

body.text: nyāsas/ ādis 2/ cayas guṇas 2/ gacchas 30/ labdhās varāṭakās 2147483646/ niṣka-varāṭakābhis bhaktās jātās niṣkās 104857/ drammās 9/ paṇās 9/ kākiṇyau 2/ varāṭakās 6// udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: first term 2/ common ratio 2/ number of terms 30/ obtained <s>varāṭakas</s> 2147483646/ divided by <s>niṣka</s>-<s>varāṭakas</s>, the result: <s>niṣkas</s> 104857/ <s>drammas</s> 9/ <s>paṇas</s> 9/ <s>kākiṇīs</s> 2/ <s>varāṭakas</s> 6// Example:

children.text: ādis %dvikam sakhe vṛddhis prati-aham %tri-guṇa-uttarā/
children.translated_text: The first term is two, O friend, the daily increment is triple,

children.text: gacchas %sapta-dinam yatra gaṇitam tatra kim @vada//
children.translated_text: the number of terms is seven days — what is the total there? Tell me!

body.text: nyāsas/ ādis 2/ cayas guṇas 3/ gacchas 7/ labdham gaṇitam 2186// sama-ādi-vṛtta-jñānāya karaṇa-sūtram sa-%ardhā āryā/
body.translated_text: Setting down: first term 2/ common ratio 3/ number of terms 7/ obtained total 2186// For knowing the number of equal-metrical-forms, the rule of operation in one and a half <s>āryā</s> verses:

children.text: pāda-akṣara-mita-gacche guṇa-varga-phalam caye %dvi-guṇe/
children.translated_text: When the number of terms is equal to the syllables of a quarter-verse, the square of the result of the common ratio — when the ratio is two —

children.text: sama-vṛttānām saṃkhyā tad-vargas varga-vargas ca/
children.translated_text: [gives] the number of equal meters (<s>sama-vṛtta</s>); its square [gives the number of] half-equal meters;

children.text: sva-sva-pada-ūnau @syātām %ardha-samānām ca viṣamāṇām//
children.translated_text: and the square of the square, diminished by each of its own quarter-verse [counts], gives the [number of] unequal meters.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: samānām %ardha-tulyānām viṣamāṇām pṛthak pṛthak/
children.translated_text: Tell me the numbers separately of equal, half-equal,

children.text: vṛttānām @vada me saṃkhyām anuṣṭubh-chandasi drutam//
children.translated_text: and unequal meters in the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> meter, quickly!

children.text: nyāsas/ uttaras %dvi-guṇas 2/ gacchas 8/ labdhās sama-vṛttānām saṃkhyās 256/ tathā %ardha-samānām ca 65280/ viṣamāṇām ca 4294901760// iti śreḍhī-vyavahāras samāptas//
children.translated_text: Setting down: common ratio, double, 2/ number of terms 8/ obtained number of equal meters: 256/ likewise of half-equal: 65280/ and of unequal: 4294901760// Thus the section on arithmetic series is concluded.

body.text: End of part one in āpaṭe
body.translated_text: End of Part One

body.text: kṣetra-vyavahāra
body.translated_text: Section on Geometry

body.text: atha kṣetra-vyavahāras/ tatra bhuja-koṭi-karṇānām anyatamābhyām anyatama-ānayanāya karaṇa-sūtram vṛtta-%dvayam/
body.translated_text: Now the section on geometry (<s>kṣetra-vyavahāra</s>). Therein, for finding any one from among the arm (<s>bhuja</s>), upright (<s>koṭi</s>), and hypotenuse (<s>karṇa</s>) from the other two, the rule of operation in two verses:

children.text: iṣṭas bāhus yas @syāt tad-spardhinyām diśi itaras bāhus/
children.translated_text: Whichever desired side there may be — the other side, in the perpendicular direction,

children.text: %tri-asre %catur-asre vā sā koṭis kīrtitā tad-jñais//
children.translated_text: in a triangle or quadrilateral — that is called the upright (<s>koṭi</s>) by those who know it.

children.text: tad-kṛtyos yoga-padam karṇas dos-karṇa-vargayos vivarāt/
children.translated_text: The square root of the sum of their squares is the hypotenuse; from the difference of the squares of the arm and hypotenuse,

children.text: mūlam koṭis koṭi-śruti-kṛtyos antarāt padam bāhus//
children.translated_text: the root is the upright; and from the difference of the squares of the upright and hypotenuse, the root is the arm.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: koṭis %catuṣṭayam yatra dos %trayam tatra kā śrutis/
children.translated_text: Where the upright is four and the arm is three, what is the hypotenuse?

children.text: koṭi-dos-karṇatas koṭi-śrutibhyām ca bhujam @vada//
children.translated_text: And from the upright, arm, and hypotenuse, tell the arm from the upright and hypotenuse.

body.text: nyāsas/ [fig.1] koṭis 4/ bhujas 3/ bhuja-vargas 9/ koṭi-vargas 16/ etayos yogāt 25/ mūlam 5/ karṇas jātas// atha karṇa-bhujābhyām koṭi-ānayanam/ nyāsas/ karṇas 5/ bhujas 3/ anayos varga-antaram 16/ etad-mūlam koṭis 4// atha koṭi-karṇābhyām bhuja-ānayanam/ nyāsas/ koṭis 4/ karṇas 5/ anayos varga-antaram 9/ etad-mūlam bhujas 3// atha prakāra-antareṇa tad-jñānāya karaṇa-sūtram sa-%ardha-vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: upright 4/ arm 3/ square of arm 9/ square of upright 16/ from their sum 25/ root 5/ the hypotenuse is obtained// Now finding the upright from the hypotenuse and arm: Setting down: hypotenuse 5/ arm 3/ difference of their squares 16/ root is the upright 4// Now finding the arm from the upright and hypotenuse: Setting down: upright 4/ hypotenuse 5/ difference of their squares 9/ root is the arm 3// Now, for knowing this by another method, the rule of operation in one and a half verses:

children.text: rāśyos antara-vargeṇa %dvi-ghne ghāte yute tayos/
children.translated_text: The product of two quantities, multiplied by two, combined with the square of their difference,

children.text: varga-yogas @bhavet evam tayos yoga-antara-āhatis/
children.translated_text: gives the sum of their squares; likewise, the product of their sum and difference

children.text: varga-antaram @bhavet evam jñeyam sarvatra dhīmatā//
children.translated_text: gives the difference of their squares — this should be known everywhere by the intelligent.

body.text: koṭis %catuṣṭayam iti pūrva-ukta-udāharaṇe nyāsas/ koṭis 4/ bhujas 3/ anayos ghāte 12/ %dvi-ghne 24/ antara-vargeṇa 1 yute varga-yogas 25/ asya mūlam karṇas 5// atha karṇa-bhujābhyām koṭi-ānayanam/ nyāsas/ karṇas 5/ bhujas 3/ anayos yogas 8/ punar etayos antareṇa 2 hatas varga-antaram 16/ asya mūlam koṭis 4// atha bhuja-jñānam/ nyāsas/ koṭis 4/ karṇas 5/ evam jātas bhujas 3// udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: In the previous example 'the upright is four,' setting down: upright 4/ arm 3/ their product 12/ doubled 24/ combined with the square of the difference (= 1), the sum of squares 25/ its root, the hypotenuse 5// Now finding the upright from the hypotenuse and arm: Setting down: hypotenuse 5/ arm 3/ their sum 8/ multiplied by their difference 2, the difference of squares 16/ its root, the upright 4// Now finding the arm: Setting down: upright 4/ hypotenuse 5/ similarly the arm 3 is obtained// Example:

children.text: sa-#aṅghri-%traya-mitas bāhus yatra koṭis ca tāvatī/
children.translated_text: Where the arm is three and a quarter and the upright is the same,

children.text: tatra karṇa-pramāṇam kim gaṇaka @brūhi me drutam//
children.translated_text: what is the measure of the hypotenuse? Tell me quickly, O calculator!

body.text: nyāsas/ [fig.2] bhujas 13_4/ koṭis 13_4/ anayos vargayos yogas 169_8/ asya mūla-abhāvāt karaṇī-gatas eva ayam karṇas/ asya āsanna-mūla-jñāna-artham upāyas/
body.translated_text: Setting down: arm 13/4/ upright 13/4/ sum of their squares 169/8/ since its root does not exist [as a rational number], this hypotenuse is expressed as a surd (<s>karaṇī</s>). For finding its approximate root, the method:

children.text: vargeṇa mahatā iṣṭena hatāt cheda-aṃśayos vadhāt/
children.translated_text: Multiply the product of the denominator and numerator by a large chosen square;

children.text: padam guṇa-pada-kṣuṇṇa-chid-bhaktam nikaṭam @bhavet//
children.translated_text: the root [of that product], divided by the denominator multiplied by the root of the chosen [square], will be the approximate [root].

body.text: iyam karṇa-karaṇī 169_8/ asyās cheda-aṃśa-ghātas 1352/ %ayuta-ghnas 13520000 asya āsanna-mūlam 3677/ idam guṇa-mūla-100-guṇita-chedena 800 bhaktam labdham āsanna-padam 4_477_800/ ayam karṇas/ evam sarvatra// atha %tri-asra-jātye karaṇa-sūtram vṛtta-%dvayam/
body.translated_text: This hypotenuse-surd is 169/8/ the product of its denominator and numerator is 1352/ multiplied by ten thousand: 13520000; its approximate root is 3677/ divided by the denominator multiplied by the square root of 100 (= 800), the obtained approximate root is 4 477/800/ this is the hypotenuse. Similarly everywhere// Now, the rule of operation for generating right triangles (<s>jātya trikoṇa</s>), in two verses:

children.text: iṣṭas bhujas asmāt %dvi-guṇa-iṣṭa-nighnāt iṣṭasya kṛtyā %eka-viyuktayā āptam/
children.translated_text: The chosen [number] is the arm; from this, multiplied by twice the chosen [number], divided by the square of the chosen minus one,

children.text: koṭis pṛthak sā iṣṭa-guṇā bhuja-ūnā karṇas @bhavet %tri-asram idam tu jātyam//
children.translated_text: the upright is obtained separately; that, multiplied by the chosen, minus the arm, is the hypotenuse. This triangle is rational (<s>jātya</s>).

children.text: iṣṭas bhujas tad-kṛtis iṣṭa-bhaktā %dvis sthāpitā iṣṭa-ūna-yutā ardhitā vā/
children.translated_text: The chosen [number] is the arm; its square divided by the chosen, placed twice — diminished and increased by the chosen, halved —

children.text: tau koṭi-karṇau iti koṭitas vā bāhu-śrutī vā akaraṇī-gate @stas//
children.translated_text: those are the upright and hypotenuse; or from the upright, the arm and hypotenuse — these will be surd-free.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: bhuje %dvādaśake yau yau koṭi-karṇau anekadhā/
children.translated_text: For the arm of twelve, tell quickly the many pairs of upright and hypotenuse

children.text: prakārābhyām @vada kṣipram tau tau akaraṇī-gatau//
children.translated_text: that are surd-free, by both methods!

body.text: nyāsas/ iṣṭas bhujas 12/ iṣṭam 2 anena %dvi-guṇena 4 guṇitas bhujas 48/ iṣṭa-2-kṛtyā 4 %eka-ūnayā 3 bhaktas labdhā koṭis 16/ iyam iṣṭa-guṇā 32 bhuja-ūnā 12 jātas karṇas 20// %trikeṇa iṣṭena vā koṭis 9/ karṇas 15// %pañcakena vā koṭis 5/ karṇas 13 iti-ādi// atha %dvitīya-prakāreṇa/ nyāsas/ iṣṭas bhujas 12/ asya kṛtis 144/ iṣṭena 2 bhaktā labdham 72/ iṣṭena 2 ūna-70-yutau 74 ardhitau jātau koṭi-karṇau 35/ 37// %catuṣṭayena vā koṭis 16/ karṇas 20// %ṣaṭkena vā koṭis 9/ karṇas 15// atha iṣṭa-karṇāt koṭi-bhuja-ānayane karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: chosen arm 12/ chosen number 2; multiplied by its double 4: 48/ divided by the square of 2 (= 4) minus one (= 3): upright 16/ this multiplied by chosen 2: 32, minus arm 12: hypotenuse 20// With chosen 3: upright 9/ hypotenuse 15// With chosen 5: upright 5/ hypotenuse 13, etc.// Now by the second method: Setting down: chosen arm 12/ its square 144/ divided by chosen 2: 72/ diminished by 2: 70, increased by 2: 74, halved: upright and hypotenuse 35, 37// With chosen 4: upright 16/ hypotenuse 20// With chosen 6: upright 9/ hypotenuse 15// Now, for finding the upright and arm from a chosen hypotenuse, the rule of operation in a verse:

children.text: iṣṭena nighnāt %dvi-guṇāt ca karṇāt iṣṭasya kṛtyā %eka-yujā yat āptam/
children.translated_text: From the chosen hypotenuse, doubled and multiplied by the chosen [number], divided by the square of the chosen plus one,

children.text: koṭis @bhavet sā pṛthak iṣṭa-nighnī tad-karṇayos antaram atra bāhus//
children.translated_text: the upright is obtained; that separately, multiplied by the chosen — its difference from the hypotenuse is the arm.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: %pañcāśīti-mite karṇe yau yau akaraṇī-gatau/
children.translated_text: For a hypotenuse measuring eighty-five, the pairs of upright and arm

children.text: @syātām koṭi-bhujau tau tau @vada kovida satvaram//
children.translated_text: that are surd-free — tell them quickly, O expert!

body.text: nyāsas/ karṇas 85/ ayam %dvi-guṇas 170/ %dvikena iṣṭena hatas 340/ iṣṭa-2-kṛtyā 4 sa-%ekayā 5 bhakte jātā koṭis 68/ iyam iṣṭa-guṇā 136/ karṇa-85-ūnitā jātas bhujas 51// %catuṣkeṇa iṣṭena vā/ koṭis 40 bhujas 75// punar prakāra-antareṇa tad-karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: hypotenuse 85/ this doubled 170/ multiplied by chosen 2: 340/ divided by square of 2 (= 4) plus one (= 5): upright 68/ this multiplied by chosen: 136/ minus hypotenuse 85: arm 51// With chosen 4: upright 40, arm 75// Again, by another method, the rule of operation in a verse:

children.text: iṣṭa-vargeṇa sa-%ekena %dvi-ghnas karṇas atha vā hatas/
children.translated_text: The hypotenuse, doubled or multiplied by the square of the chosen plus one,

children.text: phala-ūnas śravaṇas koṭis phalam iṣṭa-guṇam bhujas//
children.translated_text: minus the result, is the upright; the result multiplied by the chosen is the arm.

body.text: pūrva-udāharaṇe nyāsas/ karṇas 85/ atra %dvikena iṣṭena jātau kila koṭi-bhujau 51/ 68/ %catuṣkeṇa vā koṭis 75/ bhujas 40/ atra dos-koṭyos nāma-bhedas eva kevalam na sva-rūpa-bhedas// atha iṣṭābhyām bhuja-koṭi-karṇa-ānayane karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: In the previous example, setting down: hypotenuse 85/ here with chosen 2, the obtained upright and arm are 51, 68// With chosen 4: upright 75/ arm 40/ Here there is only a difference in the names of the arm and upright, not in their actual values// Now, for finding the arm, upright, and hypotenuse from two chosen [numbers], the rule of operation in a verse:

children.text: iṣṭayos āhatis %dvi-ghnī koṭis varga-antaram bhujas/
children.translated_text: The product of the two chosen [numbers], doubled, is the upright; the difference of their squares is the arm;

children.text: kṛti-yogas tayos eva karṇas ca akaraṇī-gatas//
children.translated_text: the sum of their squares is the hypotenuse — and these are surd-free.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: yais yais %tri-asram @bhavet jātyam koṭi-dos-śravaṇais sakhe/
children.translated_text: By what upright, arm, and hypotenuse does a rational right triangle arise, O friend?

children.text: %trīn api aviditān etān kṣipram @brūhi vicakṣaṇa//
children.translated_text: Tell quickly all three, though unknown, O discerning one!

body.text: nyāsas/ atra iṣṭe 2/ 1/ ābhyām koṭi-bhuja-karṇās 4/ 3/ 5// atha vā iṣṭe 2/ 3/ ābhyām koṭi-bhuja-karṇās 12/ 5/ 13// atha vā 2/ 4/ ābhyām koṭi-bhuja-karṇās 16/ 12/ 20// evam anyatra anekadhā// karṇa-koṭi-yutau bhuje ca jñāte pṛthak-karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: here, chosen numbers 2 and 1; from these, upright, arm, hypotenuse: 4, 3, 5// Or chosen 2 and 3: upright, arm, hypotenuse: 12, 5, 13// Or 2 and 4: upright, arm, hypotenuse: 16, 12, 20// Similarly elsewhere, in many ways// When the sum of the upright and hypotenuse is known, and the arm is known, the rule of operation for separating them, in a verse:

children.text: vaṃśa-agra-mūla-antara-bhūmi-vargas vaṃśa-uddhṛtas tena pṛthak yuta-ūnau/ [āpaṭe: -uddhṛtes < -uddhṛtas]
children.translated_text: The square of the ground-distance between the base and top of the bamboo, divided by the bamboo-[length], gives two values: the bamboo diminished and increased by this,

children.text: vaṃśau tad-ardhe @bhavatas krameṇa vaṃśasya khaṇḍe śruti-koṭi-rūpe//
children.translated_text: halved in order, become the two segments of the bamboo having the form of hypotenuse and upright.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: yadi sama-bhuvi veṇus %dvi-%tri-pāṇi-pramāṇas gaṇaka pavana-vegāt %eka-deśe sas bhagnas/
children.translated_text: If a bamboo of thirty-two cubits standing on level ground is broken at some point by the force of the wind,

children.text: bhuvi nṛpa-mita-hasteṣu aṅga lagnam tad-agram @kathaya katiṣu mūlāt eṣas bhagnas kareṣu//
children.translated_text: and its tip touches the ground at sixteen cubits [from the base] — tell me, at how many cubits from the root is it broken?

body.text: nyāsas/ vaṃśa-agra-mūla-antara-bhūmis 16/ vaṃśas 32/ koṭi-karṇa-yutis 32/ bhujas 16/ jāte ūrdhva-adhas-khaṇḍe 20/ 12// bāhu-karṇa-yoge dṛṣṭe koṭyām ca jñātāyām pṛthak-karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: ground distance between tip and base 16/ bamboo 32/ sum of upright and hypotenuse 32/ arm 16/ obtained upper and lower segments: 20, 12// When the sum of the arm and hypotenuse is observed, and the upright is known, the rule of operation for separating them, in a verse:

children.text: stambhasya vargas ahi-bila-antareṇa bhaktas phalam vyāla-bila-antarālāt/
children.translated_text: The square of the pillar, divided by the distance between the snake's hole [and the pillar base], the result subtracted from the hole-to-pillar distance,

children.text: śodhyam tad-%ardha-pramitais karais @syāt bila-agratas vyāla-kalāpi-yogas//
children.translated_text: halved — at that many cubits from the top of the hole is the meeting of the snake and the peacock.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: @asti stambha-tale bilam tad-upari krīḍā-śikhaṇḍī sthitas/
children.translated_text: At the base of a pillar there is a hole; atop it sits a playful peacock.

children.text: stambhe hasta-%nava-ucchrite %tri-guṇite stambha-pramāṇa-antare/
children.translated_text: The pillar is nine cubits high. At a distance of three times the pillar's measure,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ahim bilam āvrajantam @apatat tiryak sas tasya upari/
children.translated_text: seeing a snake approaching the hole, he swooped down diagonally upon it.

children.text: kṣipram @brūhi tayos bilāt kati-karais sāmyena gatyos yutis//
children.translated_text: Tell quickly — at how many cubits from the hole did they meet, with equal paths?

body.text: nyāsas/ stambhas 9/ ahi-bila-antaram 27/ jātās bila-yutyos madhye hastās 12// koṭi-karṇa-antare bhuje ca dṛṣṭe pṛthak-karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: pillar 9/ distance from hole to snake 27/ obtained cubits between hole and meeting point: 12// When the difference of the upright and hypotenuse is observed, and the arm is known, the rule of operation for separating them, in a verse:

children.text: bhujāt vargitāt koṭi-karṇa-antara-āptam dvidhā koṭi-karṇa-antareṇa ūna-yuktam/
children.translated_text: The square of the arm divided by the difference of the upright and hypotenuse, then severally diminished and increased by the difference of the upright and hypotenuse,

children.text: tad-%ardhe kramāt koṭi-karṇau bhavetām idam dhīmatā @āvedya sarvatra yojyam//
children.translated_text: halved in order, those become the upright and hypotenuse — this should be known and applied everywhere by the intelligent.

children.text: sakhe padma-tad-majjana-sthāna-madhyam bhujas koṭi-karṇa-antaram padma-dṛśyam/
children.translated_text: O friend, the [distance between] the lotus and its point of submersion is the arm; the difference of the upright and hypotenuse is the visible lotus [stem];

children.text: nalas koṭis etad-mitam @syāt yat ambhas @vada evam @samānīya pānīya-mānam//
children.translated_text: the stalk is the upright; as much as the water [depth] — thus, having brought it together, tell the measure of the water!

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: cakra-krauñca-ākulita-salile kva api dṛṣṭam taḍāge toyāt ūrdhvam kamala-kalikā-agram vitasti-pramāṇam/
children.translated_text: In a lake teeming with <s>cakravāka</s> birds and herons, a lotus-bud was seen rising a span above the water;

children.text: mandam mandam calitam anilena āhatam hasta-#yugme tasmin magnam gaṇaka @kathaya kṣipram ambhas-pramāṇam//
children.translated_text: gently moved by the wind, it submerged at [a distance of] two cubits — O calculator, tell quickly the depth of the water!

body.text: nyāsas/ koṭi-karṇa-antaram 1_2/ bhujas 2/ labdham jala-gāmbhīryam 15_4/ iyam koṭis 15_4/ iyam eva koṭis kalikā-māna-yutā jātas karṇas 17_4// koṭi-%eka-deśena yute karṇe bhuje ca dṛṣṭe koṭi-karṇa-jñānāya karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: difference of upright and hypotenuse 1/2/ arm 2/ obtained water depth 15/4/ this is the upright 15/4/ this upright plus the bud-measure gives the hypotenuse 17/4// When the upright is partially added to the hypotenuse and the arm is observed, the rule of operation for finding the upright and hypotenuse, in a verse:

children.text: %dvi-nighna-tāla-ucchriti-saṃyutam yat saras-antaram tena vibhājitāyās/
children.translated_text: The distance of the pond divided by the sum of twice the height of the palm tree and the pond-distance —

children.text: tāla-ucchrites tāla-saras-antara-ghnyās uḍḍīna-mānam khalu @labhyate tat// [āpaṭe: khala < khalu]
children.translated_text: multiplied by the height of the palm tree and the pond-distance — that gives the measure of the flight-distance.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: vṛkṣāt hasta-%śata-ucchrayāt %śata-#yuge vāpīm kapis kas api @agāt @uttīrya atha paras drutam śruti-pathena @uḍḍīya kimcit drumāt/
children.translated_text: A monkey descended from a tree one hundred cubits high and went to a pond at a distance of two hundred [cubits]; another [monkey] quickly leaping up and then flying diagonally from the tree

children.text: jātā evam samatā tayos yadi gatau uḍḍīna-mānam kiyat vidvan ced su-pariśramas @asti gaṇite kṣipram tat @ācakṣva me//
children.translated_text: reached [the pond] in equal distance — if the flight-measure is asked, O learned one, if there is good effort in mathematics, tell me quickly!

body.text: nyāsas/ vṛkṣa-vāpī-antaram 200/ vṛkṣa-ucchrāyas 100/ kabdham uḍḍīna-mānam 50/ koṭis 150/ karṇas 250/ bhujas 200// bhuja-koṭyos yoge karṇe ca jñāte pṛthak-karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: distance between tree and cistern 200/ height of tree 100/ the obtained flight-distance 50/ the base (<s>koṭi</s>) 150/ the hypotenuse (<s>karṇa</s>) 250/ the arm (<s>bhuja</s>) 200// When the sum of the arm and upright is known and the hypotenuse is known, the rule of operation for finding them separately, in a verse:

children.text: karṇasya vargāt %dvi-guṇāt viśodhyas dos-koṭi-yogas sva-guṇas asya mūlam/
children.translated_text: From twice the square of the hypotenuse, subtract the square of the sum of the arm and upright; the square root of this,

children.text: yogas dvidhā mūla-vihīna-yuktas @syātām tad-%ardhe bhuja-koṭi-māne//
children.translated_text: combined with and subtracted from the sum, [gives two quantities]; their halves will be the measures of the arm and the upright.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: %daśa %sapta-adhikas karṇas %tri-adhikā %viṃśatis sakhe/
children.translated_text: The hypotenuse is seventeen, and the sum of the arm and upright is twenty-three, O friend;

children.text: bhuja-koṭi-yutis yatra tatra te me pṛthak @vada//
children.translated_text: where this is so, tell me the arm and upright separately!

body.text: nyāsas/ karṇas 17/ dos-koṭi-yogas 23/ jāte bhuja-koṭī 8/ 15// udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: hypotenuse 17/ sum of arm and upright 23/ the obtained arm and upright: 8/ 15// Example:

children.text: dos-koṭyos antaram #śailās karṇas yatra %trayodaśa/
children.translated_text: The difference of the arm and upright is seven, and the hypotenuse is thirteen;

children.text: bhuja-koṭī pṛthak tatra @vada āśu gaṇaka-uttama//
children.translated_text: tell the arm and upright separately there, quickly, O best of calculators!

body.text: nyāsas/ karṇas 13/ bhuja-koṭi-antaram 7/ labdhe bhuja-koṭī 5/ 12// lamba-avabādhā-jñānāya karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: hypotenuse 13/ difference of arm and upright 7/ the obtained arm and upright: 5/ 12// For finding the perpendicular and the segments of the base, the rule of operation in a verse:

children.text: anyonya-mūla-agra-ga-sūtra-yogāt veṇvos vadhe yoga-hṛte avalambas/
children.translated_text: From the sum of the strings going from the root of each [pole] to the top of the other, the product of the two poles divided by their sum is the perpendicular.

children.text: vaṃśau sva-yogena hṛtau abhīṣṭa-bhū-ghnau ca lamba-ubhayatas ku-khaṇḍe//
children.translated_text: The two poles, each divided by their sum and multiplied by the desired ground-distance, give the two ground-segments on either side of the perpendicular.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: %pañcadaśa-%daśa-kara-ucchraya-veṇvos ajñāta-madhya-bhūmikayos/
children.translated_text: For two bamboo poles of heights fifteen and ten hands, with the ground between them unknown,

children.text: itaretara-mūla-agra-ga-sūtra-yutes lamba-mānam @ācakṣva//
children.translated_text: when the strings from the root of each to the top of the other meet, tell the measure of the perpendicular!

body.text: nyāsas/ vaṃśau 15/ 10 jātas lambas 6/ vaṃśa-antara-bhūs 5/ atas jāte bhū-khaṇḍe 3/2/ atha vā bhūs 10 khaṇḍe 6/4 vā bhūs 15/ khaṇḍe 9/6 vā bhūs 20 khaṇḍe 12/8// evam sarvatra lambas sas eva/ yadi atra bhūmi-tulye bhuje vaṃśas koṭis tadā bhū-khaṇḍena kim iti trairāśikena sarvatra pratītis// atha akṣetra-lakṣaṇa-sūtram/
body.translated_text: Setting down: the two poles 15/ 10. The obtained perpendicular is 6/ The ground between the poles is 5/ Therefore the obtained ground-segments are 3/ 2// Or if the ground is 10, the segments are 6/ 4; or if the ground is 15, the segments are 9/ 6; or if the ground is 20, the segments are 12/ 8// Thus everywhere the perpendicular is one and the same. If here the arm equal to the ground is the pole, and the upright is the base-segment, then [the result follows] by the rule of three in every case, giving certainty// Now the rule for an impossible figure:

children.text: dhṛṣṭa-uddiṣṭam ṛju-bhuja-kṣetram yatra %eka-bāhutas su-alpā/
children.translated_text: A rectilinear figure boldly proposed, in which the sum of [all] sides except one is less than that one side,

children.text: tad-itara-bhuja-yutis atha vā tulyā jñeyam tat akṣetram// [āpaṭe: -yatis < -yutis]
children.translated_text: or equal [to it]—that should be known as an impossible figure.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: %catur-asre %tri-%ṣaṣ-%dvi-#arkās bhujās %tri-asre %tri-%ṣaṣ-%navās/
children.translated_text: In a quadrilateral where the sides are three, six, two, and twelve, and in a triangle where [they are] three, six, and nine,

children.text: uddiṣṭās yatra dhṛṣṭena tat akṣetram @vinirdiśet// [āpaṭe: dhaṣṭena < dhṛṣṭena]
children.translated_text: boldly proposed—one should point out that these are impossible figures.

body.text: ete anupapanne kṣetre/ bhuja-pramāṇās ṛju-śalākās bhuja-sthāneṣu @vinyasya anupapattis darśanīyā// [āpaṭe: anapapattis < anupapattis] ābādhā-ādi-jñānāya karaṇa-sūtram āryā-%dvayam/
body.translated_text: These are infeasible figures. By arranging straight rods of the given side-measures at the positions of the sides, the impossibility should be demonstrated// For finding the segments and other [quantities] of the base, the rule of operation in two <s>āryā</s> verses:

children.text: %tri-bhuje bhujayos yogas tad-antara-guṇas bhuvā hṛtas labdhyā/
children.translated_text: In a triangle, the sum of the two sides multiplied by their difference, divided by the base, gives a quotient;

children.text: %dvis-sthā bhūs ūna-yutā dalitā ābādhe tayos @syātām//
children.translated_text: the base, placed twice, diminished and increased [by that quotient], and halved, gives the two base-segments.

children.text: sva-ābādhā-bhuja-kṛtyos antara-mūlam @prajāyate lambas/
children.translated_text: The square root of the difference of the squares of a side and its corresponding base-segment is the perpendicular.

children.text: lamba-guṇam bhūmi-%ardham spaṣṭam %tri-bhuje phalam @bhavati//
children.translated_text: Half the base multiplied by the perpendicular is clearly the area of the triangle.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: kṣetre mahī manu-mitā %tri-bhuje bhujau tu yatra %trayodaśa-#tithi-pramitau ca yasya/
children.translated_text: In a triangular field where the base measures fourteen, and the two sides measure thirteen and fifteen respectively,

children.text: tatra avalambakam atho @kathaya avabādhe kṣipram tathā ca sama-koṣṭha-mitim phala-ākhyam//
children.translated_text: tell the perpendicular and the base-segments, and quickly also the area, measured in equal compartments!

body.text: nyāsas/ bhūs 14/ bhujau 13/15/ labdhe ābādhe 5/9/ lambaś ca 12/ kṣetra-phalam ca 84// ṛṇa-ābādhā-udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: base 14/ sides 13/ 15/ the obtained base-segments: 5/ 9/ and the perpendicular 12/ and the area of the field 84// Example with a negative base-segment:

children.text: %daśa-%saptadaśa-pramau hbujau %tri-bhuje yatra %nava-pramā mahī/
children.translated_text: In a triangle where the sides measure ten and seventeen, and the base measures nine,

children.text: abadhe @vada lambakam tathā gaṇitam gāṇitika āśu tatra me//
children.translated_text: tell me the base-segments and the perpendicular, and also the area, O mathematician, quickly!

body.text: nyāsas/ bhujau 10/17/ bhūmis 9/ atra %tri-bhuje bhujayos yogas iti-ādinā labdham 21/ anena bhūs ūnā na @syāt/ asmāt eva bhūs apanītā śeṣa-%ardham ṛṇa-gatā ābādhā diś-vaiparītyena iti arthas/ tathā jāte ābādhe 6/15/ atra ubhayatra api jātas lambas 8/ phalam 36// %catur-bhuja-%tri-bhujayos aspaṣṭa-phala-ānayane karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: sides 10/ 17/ base 9/ Here in the triangle, by [the rule] 'the sum of the two sides' and so on, the result is 21/ The base cannot be less than this; from this very [quantity] the base is subtracted, and the half of the remainder is the negative base-segment—meaning it extends in the opposite direction. Thus the obtained base-segments are 6/ 15/ Here in both cases the obtained perpendicular is 8/ The area is 36// For finding the approximate area of a quadrilateral and triangle, the rule of operation in a verse:

children.text: sarva-dos-yuti-#dalam %catur-sthitam bāhubhis virahitam ca tad-vadhāt/
children.translated_text: Half the sum of all sides, placed fourfold, diminished [successively] by the [four] sides, and the product of those [four results]—

children.text: mūlam asphuṭa-phalam %catur-bhuje spaṣṭam evam uditam %tri-bāhuke//
children.translated_text: its square root is the approximate area of a quadrilateral; and it is stated to be exact for a triangle.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: bhūmis %caturdaśa-mitā mukham #aṅka-saṃkhyam bāhū %trayodaśa-#divākara-saṃmitau ca/
children.translated_text: A field whose base measures fourteen, whose face (top side) numbers nine, and whose two flanks measure thirteen and twelve,

children.text: lambas api yatra #ravi-saṃkhyakas eva tatra kṣetre phalam @kathaya tat kathitam yat ādyais//
children.translated_text: and where the perpendicular is twelve—tell the area of that field, as declared by the ancients!

body.text: nyāsas/ bhūmis 14/ mukham 9/ bāhū 13/ 12/ lambas 12/ ukta-vat karaṇena jātam kṣetra-phalam karaṇī 19800/ asyās padam kiṃcid-nyūnam %ekacatvāriṃśacchatam 141/ idam atra kṣetre na vāstavam phalam kiṃtu lambena nighnam ku-mukha-aikya-#khaṇḍam iti vakṣyamāṇa-karaṇena vāstavam phalam 138// atra %tri-bhujasya pūrva-udāhṛtasya nyāsas/ bhūmis 14/ bhujau 13/ 15/ anena api prakāreṇa %tri-bāhuke tat eva vāstavam phalam 84/ atra %catur-bhujasya aspaṣṭam uditam// atha sthūlatva-nirūpaṇa-artham sūtram sa-%ardha-vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: base 14/ face 9/ flanks 13/ 12/ perpendicular 12/ By the stated rule, the obtained field-area is the surd 19800/ Its root is slightly less than one hundred forty-one: 141/ This is not the true area of this field; rather, by the rule to be stated—'the perpendicular multiplied by half the sum of the base and face'—the true area is 138// Here for the previously given triangle, setting down: base 14/ sides 13/ 15/ By this method also, for the triangle, the true area is the same: 84/ Here for the quadrilateral it is stated to be approximate// Now a rule for demonstrating the approximation, in one and a half verses:

children.text: %catur-bhujasya aniyatau hi karṇau katham tatas asmin niyatam phalam @syāt/
children.translated_text: For a quadrilateral, the two diagonals are indeed indeterminate—how then can there be a determinate area?

children.text: prasādhitau tad-śravaṇau yat ādyais sva-kalpitau tau itaratra na @stas/
children.translated_text: The diagonals computed by the ancients were assumed by them [for specific cases]; in other [cases] they would not hold.

children.text: teṣu eva bāhuṣu aparau ca karṇau anekadhā kṣetra-phalam tatas ca//
children.translated_text: With those very sides, other diagonals [are possible], and hence the area [varies] in many ways.

children.text: %catur-bhuje hi %eka-antara-koṇau @ākramya antar-praveśyamānau bhujau tad-saṃsaktam sva-karṇam @saṃkocayatas/ itarau tu bahis-prasarantau sva-karṇam @vardhayatas/ atas uktam teṣu eva bāhuṣu aparau ca karṇau iti//
children.translated_text: For in a quadrilateral, when two opposite corners are pressed inward, the sides adjacent to them contract their diagonal; while the other two, extending outward, lengthen their diagonal. Hence it is said, 'with those very sides, other diagonals [are possible].'

children.text: lambayos karṇayos vā %ekam @anirdiśya aparam katham/
children.translated_text: Without specifying one of the two—either a perpendicular or a diagonal—how can the other be asked?

children.text: @pṛcchati aniyatatve api niyatam ca api tad-phalam//
children.translated_text: And how can the area be determinate when [the figure] is indeterminate?

children.text: sas pṛcchakas piśācas vā vaktā vā nitarām tatas/
children.translated_text: That questioner is either a demon or, even more so, the one who [claims to] answer—

children.text: yas na @vetti %catur-bāhu-kṣetrasya aniyatām sthitim// [no numbers are given to these two śloka stanśas in āpaṭe.]
children.translated_text: he who does not know the indeterminate nature of the quadrilateral field!

children.text: sama-catur-bhuja-āyatayos phala-ānayane karaṇa-sūtram sa-ardha-śloka-dvayam/
children.translated_text: For finding the area of a rhombus and a rectangle, the rule of operation in two and a half verses:

children.text: iṣṭā śrutis tulya-%catur-bhujasya kalpyā atha tad-varga-vivarjitā yā/
children.translated_text: For a rhombus, one diagonal should be assumed at will; then the square of the side diminished by [a quarter of] its square,

children.text: %catur-guṇā bāhu-kṛtis tadīyam mūlam %dvitīya-śravaṇa-pramāṇam//
children.translated_text: multiplied by four—the square root of that is the measure of the second diagonal.

children.text: atulya-karṇa-abhihatis %dvi-bhaktā phalam sphuṭam tulya-%catur-bhuje @syāt/
children.translated_text: Half the product of the unequal diagonals will be the exact area of the rhombus.

children.text: sama-śrutau tulya-%catur-bhuje ca tathā āyate tad-bhuja-koṭi-ghātas/
children.translated_text: In a rhombus with equal diagonals, and likewise in a rectangle, [the area is] the product of the side and upright.

children.text: %catur-bhuje anyatra samāna-lambe lambena nighnam ku-mukha-aikya-#khaṇḍam//
children.translated_text: In other quadrilaterals having equal perpendiculars, [the area is] the perpendicular multiplied by half the sum of the base and face.

body.text: atra uddeśakas/
body.translated_text: Here an example:

children.text: kṣetrasya %pañca-kṛti-tulya-%catur-bhujasya karṇau tatas ca gaṇitam gaṇaka @pracakṣva/
children.translated_text: Tell the diagonals and then the area of a rhombus whose side equals twenty-five, O calculator!

children.text: tulya-śrutes ca khalu tasya tathā āyatasya yad-vistṛtis #rasa-mitā %aṣṭa-mitam ca dairghyam//
children.translated_text: And [tell the same] for one with equal diagonals, as well as for a rectangle whose breadth measures six and whose length is eight.

body.text: %prathama-udāharaṇe nyāsas [fig.3]/ bhujās 25/ 25/ 25/ 25/ atra %triṃśat-30-mitām %ekām śrutim @prakalpya yathā-ukta-prakāreṇa jātā anyā śrutis 40/ phalam ca 600// atha vā/ nyāsas [fig.4]/ %caturdaśa-14-mitām %ekām śrutim @prakalpya ukta-vat-karaṇena jātā anyā śrutis 48/ phalam ca 336// %dvitīya-udāharaṇe nyāsas [fig.5]/ tad-kṛtyos yoga-padam karṇa iti jātā karaṇī-gatā śrutis ubhayatra tulyā eva 1250/ gaṇitam ca 625// atha āyatasya nyāsas/ vistṛtis 6/ dairghyam 8/ [fig.6] asya gaṇitam 48// udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: In the first example, setting down [fig. 3]: sides 25/ 25/ 25/ 25/ Here, assuming one diagonal to be thirty (30), by the stated method the other diagonal obtained is 40/ and the area 600// Or alternatively, setting down [fig. 4]: assuming one diagonal to be fourteen (14), by the stated method the other diagonal obtained is 48/ and the area 336// In the second example, setting down [fig. 5]: the square root of the sum of their squares is the diagonal; the obtained surd-diagonal is the same in both cases: root of 1250/ and the area 625// Now for the rectangle, setting down: breadth 6/ length 8/ [fig. 6] its area is 48// Example:

children.text: kṣetrasya yasya vadanam #madanāri-tulyam viśvaṃbharā %dvi-guṇitena mukhena tulyā/
children.translated_text: A field whose face equals eleven, whose base equals twice the face,

children.text: bāhū %trayodaśa-#nakha-pramitau ca lambas #sūrya-unmitas ca gaṇitam @vada tatra kim @syāt//
children.translated_text: whose two flanks measure thirteen and twenty, and whose perpendicular measures twelve—tell, what would be the area there?

body.text: nyāsas/ vadanam 11/ viśvaṃbharā 22/ bāhū 13/ 20/ lambas 12/ [fig.7] atra sarva-dos-yuti-#dalam iti-ādinā sthūla-phalam 250/ vāstavam tu lambena nighnam ku-mukha-aikya-#khaṇḍam iti jātam phalam 198/ kṣetrasya khaṇḍa-%trayam @kṛtvā phalāni pṛthak @ānīya aikyam @kṛtvā asya phala-upapattis darśanīyā/ khaṇḍa-%traya-darśanam/ [fig.8a][fig.8b][fig.8c] nyāsas/ %prathamasya bhuja-koṭi-karṇās 5/ 12/ 13/ %dvitīyasya āyatasya vistṛtis 6/ dairghyam 12/ %tṛtīyasya bhuja-koṭi-karṇās 16/ 12/ 20/ atra %tri-bhujayos kṣetrayos bhuja-koṭi-ghāta-%ardham phalam/ āyate %catur-asre kṣetre tad-bhuja-koṭi-ghātas phalam / yathā %prathama-kṣetre phalam 30/ %dvitīye 72/ %tṛtīye 96/ eṣām aikyam sarva-kṣetre phalam 198// atha anyat udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: face 11/ base 22/ flanks 13/ 20/ perpendicular 12/ [fig. 7] Here by 'half the sum of all sides' and so on, the approximate area is 250/ But the true [area], by 'the perpendicular multiplied by half the sum of the base and face,' is 198/ By dividing the field into three parts, finding the areas separately, and summing them, the verification of this area should be demonstrated. The three parts shown: [fig. 8a][fig. 8b][fig. 8c] Setting down: the first [triangle's] arm, upright, and hypotenuse: 5/ 12/ 13/ the second [rectangle's] breadth 6/ length 12/ the third [triangle's] arm, upright, and hypotenuse: 16/ 12/ 20/ Here, for the two triangular fields, half the product of arm and upright is the area; for the rectangular field, the product of its sides is the area. Thus the first field's area is 30/ the second 72/ the third 96/ Their sum, the total field area, is 198// Now another example:

children.text: %pañcāśat %eka-sahitā vadanam yadīyam bhūs %pañcasaptati-mitā pramitas %aṣṭaṣaṣṭyā/
children.translated_text: A [field] whose face is fifty-one, whose base measures seventy-five, whose left side measures sixty-eight,

children.text: savyas bhujas %dvi-guṇa-%viṃśati-saṃmitas anyas tasmin phalam śravaṇa-lamba-mitī @pracakṣva//
children.translated_text: and whose other side measures forty—in that [field], tell the area, the diagonal, and the perpendicular measures!

body.text: nyāsas/ vadanam 51/ bhūmis 75/ bhujau 68/ 40// [fig.9] atra phala-avalamba-śrutīnām sūtram vṛtta-%ardham/
body.translated_text: Setting down: face 51/ base 75/ sides 68/ 40// [fig. 9] Here, the rule for the area, perpendicular, and diagonal, in half a verse:

body.text: jñāte avalambe śravaṇas śrutau tu lambas phalam @syāt niyatam tu tatra//
body.translated_text: When the perpendicular is known, the diagonal [can be found]; and when the diagonal is known, the perpendicular; and the area is then determinate.

body.text: karṇasya aniyatatvāt lambas api aniyatas iti arthas// lamba-jñānāya karaṇa-sūtram vṛtta-%ardham/
body.translated_text: The meaning is: since the diagonal is indeterminate, the perpendicular is also indeterminate// For finding the perpendicular, the rule of operation in half a verse:

body.text: %catur-bhuja-antar-%tri-bhuje avalambas prāk-vat bhujau karṇa-bhujau mahī bhūs//
body.translated_text: In the triangle interior to the quadrilateral, the perpendicular [is found] as before, where the sides are the diagonal and [one] side, and the base is the ground.

body.text: atra lamba-jñāna-artham savya-bhuja-agrāt dakṣiṇa-bhuja-mūla-gāmī iṣṭa-karṇas %saptasaptati-mitas kalpitas tena %catur-bhuja-antar-%tri-bhujam kalpitam tatra asau karṇa %ekas bhujas 77/ %dvitīyas tu savya-bhujas 68/ bhūs sā eva 75/ atra prāk-vat labdhas lambas 308_5// lambe jñāte karṇa-jñāna-artham sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Here, for finding the perpendicular, a chosen diagonal of seventy-seven is assumed, going from the top of the left side to the base of the right side. By this, an interior triangle within the quadrilateral is formed, where that diagonal is one side (77), the second is the left side (68), and the base is the same (75). Here, as before, the obtained perpendicular is 308/5// When the perpendicular is known, the rule for finding the diagonal, in a verse:

children.text: yat lamba-lamba-āśrita-bāhu-varga-viśleṣa-mūlam kathitā avabādhā/
children.translated_text: The square root of the difference of the squares of the perpendicular and the side resting on it is called the base-segment.

children.text: tad-ūna-bhū-varga-samanvitasya yat lamba-vargasya padam sas karṇas//
children.translated_text: The square root of the sum of the square of the perpendicular and the square of the base diminished by that [segment] is the diagonal.

body.text: fig.10
body.translated_text: fig. 10

body.text: atra savya-bhuja-agrāt lambas kila kalpitas 308_5/ atas jātā ābādhā 144_5 tad-ūna-bhū-varga-samanvitasya iti-ādinā jātas karṇas 77// %dvitīya-karṇa-jñāna-artham sūtram vṛtta-%dvayam/
body.translated_text: Here the perpendicular is assumed from the top of the left side: 308/5/ Therefore the obtained base-segment is 144/5. By [the rule] 'the square of the base diminished by that, together with the square of the perpendicular' and so on, the obtained diagonal is 77// For finding the second diagonal, the rule in two verses:

children.text: iṣṭas atra karṇas %prathamam prakalpyas %tri-asre tu karṇa-ubhayatas sthite ye/
children.translated_text: Here a first diagonal should be assumed; in the two triangles situated on either side of the diagonal,

children.text: karṇam tayos kṣmām itarau ca bāhū @prakalpya lamba-avabadhe ca sādhye//
children.translated_text: taking the diagonal as the base and the other [sides] as the arms, the perpendicular and base-segments should be determined.

children.text: ābādhayos %eka-kakubh-sthayos yat @syāt antaram tat kṛti-saṃyutasya/
children.translated_text: The square of the difference of the two base-segments that lie on the same side,

children.text: lamba-aikya-vargasya padam %dvitīyas karṇas @bhavet sarva-%catur-bhujeṣu//
children.translated_text: added to the square of the sum of the perpendiculars—the square root of that will be the second diagonal, in all quadrilaterals.

body.text: nyāsas/ tatra %catur-bhuje savya-bhuja-agrāt dakṣiṇa-bhuja-mūla-gāminas karṇasya mānam kalpitam 77/ tad-karṇa-rekhā-avacchinnasya kṣetrasya madhye karṇa-rekhā-ubhayatas ye %tri-asre utpanne tayos karṇam bhūmim tad-itarau ca bhujau @prakalpya prāk-vat lambas ābādhā ca sādhitā/ tad-darśanam [fig.11] lambas 60/ %dvitīya-lambas 24/ ābādhayos 45/ 32/ %eka-kakubh-sthayos antarasya 13/ kṛtes 169 lamba-aikya-84-kṛtes 7056 ca yogas 7225/ tasya padam %dvitīya-karṇa-pramāṇam 85// [fig.12] atra iṣṭa-karṇa-kalpane viśeṣa-ukti-sūtram sa-%ardha-vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: In the quadrilateral, the measure of the diagonal going from the top of the left side to the base of the right side is assumed as 77/ In the field cut by that diagonal line, the two triangles produced on either side of the diagonal line—taking the diagonal as the base and the other [sides] as the arms—the perpendicular and base-segments are determined as before. Their display: [fig. 11] perpendicular 60/ second perpendicular 24/ base-segments 45/ 32/ the difference of those on the same side: 13/ its square 169, the square of the sum of the perpendiculars (84): 7056, and their sum 7225/ its square root, the measure of the second diagonal: 85// [fig. 12] Here, a special instruction-rule for assuming the diagonal, in one and a half verses:

children.text: karṇa-āśrita-su-alpa-bhuja-aikyam urvīm @prakalpya tad-śeṣa-bhujau ca bāhū/
children.translated_text: Taking as the base the sum of the smaller sides adjacent to the diagonal, and the remaining sides as the arms,

children.text: sādhyas avalambas atha tathā anya-karṇas sva-urvyās katham-cit śravaṇas na dīrghas/
children.translated_text: the perpendicular should be determined; and then similarly the other diagonal. The diagonal should not be longer than its own base,

children.text: tad-anya-lambāt na laghus tathā idam @jñātvā iṣṭa-karṇas sudhiyā prakalpyas//
children.translated_text: nor shorter than the other perpendicular. Knowing this, the intelligent person should assume the desired diagonal.

body.text: %catur-bhuje hi %eka-antara-koṇau @ākramya saṃkocyamānam %tri-bhujatvam @yāti/ tatra %eka-koṇe lagna-laghu-bhujayos aikyam bhūmim itarau bhujau ca @prakalpya tad-lambāt ūnas saṃkocyamānas karṇas katham-cit api na @syāt tad-itaras bhūmes adhikas na @syāt evam ubhayathā api etat anuktam api buddhi-matā @jñāyate// viṣama-%catur-bhuja-phala-ānayanāya karaṇa-sūtram vṛtta-%ardham/
body.translated_text: For when opposite corners of a quadrilateral are pressed together, it contracts toward a triangle. There, taking the sum of the two small sides meeting at one corner as the base and the other two as the arms, the contracting diagonal should never be less than the perpendicular [so obtained]; and the other [diagonal] should never exceed the base. Thus, in both cases, even though not [explicitly] stated, the intelligent person understands [these constraints]// For finding the area of a scalene quadrilateral, the rule of operation in half a verse:

body.text: %tri-asre tu karṇa-ubhayatas sthite ye tayos phala-aikyam phalam atra nūnam//
body.translated_text: In [a quadrilateral], those [triangles] standing on both sides of the diagonal—the sum of their areas is certainly the area here.

body.text: anantara-ukta-kṣetra-antar-%tri-asrayos phale 924/ 2310 [/] anayos aikyam 3234 tasya phalam// samāna-lambasya ābādhā-ādi-jñānāya karaṇa-sūtram vṛtta-%dvayam/
body.translated_text: The areas of the two triangles within the previously-mentioned figure are 924 and 2310; the sum of these, 3234, is the area. For finding the perpendicular segments (<s>ābādhā</s>) and other quantities of a [trapezoid] with equal altitudes, the rule of operation in two verses:

children.text: samāna-lambasya %catur-bhujasya mukha-ūna-bhūmim @parikalpya bhūmim/
children.translated_text: For a quadrilateral with equal altitudes, treating the base diminished by the face as the [new] base,

children.text: bhujau bhujau %tri-asra-vat eva sādhye tasya abadhe lamba-mitis tatas ca//
children.translated_text: the two sides should be determined just as for a triangle; its perpendicular segments and the measure of the altitude [follow] from that.

children.text: ābādhayā ūnā %catur-asra-bhūmis tad-lamba-varga-aikya-padam śrutis @syāt/
children.translated_text: The base of the quadrilateral diminished by the perpendicular segment—the square root of the sum of the squares of that and the altitude gives the diagonal.

children.text: samāna-lambe laghu-dos-ku-yogāt mukha-anya-dos-saṃyutis alpikā @syāt//
children.translated_text: In an equal-altitude [trapezoid], from the sum of the smaller side and the base, the sum of the face and the other side would be the smaller [quantity].

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: %dvipañcāśat-mita-vi-%eka-%catvāriṃśat-mitau bhujau/
children.translated_text: The two sides measure fifty-two and forty-one;

children.text: mukham tu %pañcaviṃśatyā tulyam %ṣaṣṭyā mahī kila//
children.translated_text: the face equals twenty-five, and the base is sixty, indeed.

children.text: atulya-lambakam kṣetram idam pūrvais udāhṛtam/
children.translated_text: This figure with unequal altitudes was stated by earlier [authorities];

children.text: %ṣaṭpañcāśat %triṣaṣṭis ca niyate karṇayos mitī/
children.translated_text: fifty-six and sixty-three are the stated measures of the diagonals.

children.text: karṇau tatra aparau @brūhi sama-lambam ca tad-śrutī//
children.translated_text: State the other two diagonals there, and [for] the equal-altitude [version], its diagonals!

body.text: nyāsas/ [fig.13] atra bṛhat-karṇam %triṣaṣṭi-mitam @prakalpya jñātas [ed.jātas] prāk-vat anya-karṇas 56// atha %ṣaṭpañcāśat-sthāne %dvātriṃśat-mitam karṇam 32 @prakalpya prāk-vat sādhyamāne karṇe nyāsas/ [fig.14] jātam karaṇī-khaṇḍa-%dvayam 621/ 2700/ anayos mūlayos 24_23_25/ 51_24_25/ aikyam %dvitīyas karṇas 76_22_25// atha tat eva kṣetram ced sama-lambam[/] [fig.15] mukha-ūna-bhūmim @prakalpya bhūmim iti jñāna-artham %tri-asram kalpitam/ nyāsas/ [fig.16] atra ābādhe jāte 3_5/ 172_5/ lambas ca karaṇī-gatas jātas 38016_25[/] āsanna-mūla-karaṇena jātas 38_622_625/ ayam tatra %catur-bhuje sama-lambas[/] laghu-ābādhā-ūnita-bhūmes sama-lambasya ca varga-yogas 5049[/] ayam karṇa-vargas/ evam bṛhat-ābādhātas %dvitīya-karṇa-vargas 2176/ anayos āsanna-mūla-karaṇena jātau karṇau 71_1_20[/] 46_13_20[/] evam %catur-asre teṣu eva bāhuṣu anyau karṇau bahudhā @bhavatas// evam aniyatatve api niyatau eva karṇau ānītau brahmagupta-ādyais tad-ānayanam yathā/
body.translated_text: Setting down: [Fig. 13] Here, taking the larger diagonal as sixty-three, the other diagonal obtained as before is 56. Now, taking a diagonal of measure thirty-two in place of fifty-six, when determining the diagonal as before, setting down: [Fig. 14] The two surd-segments obtained are 621 and 2700; the roots of these are 24 23/25 and 51 24/25; their sum, the second diagonal, is 76 22/25. Now, if that same figure has equal altitudes: [Fig. 15] Treating the base minus the face as the base—for the purpose of determining [this], a triangle is constructed. Setting down: [Fig. 16] Here, the perpendicular segments obtained are 3/5 and 172/5; and the altitude obtained as a surd is √(38016/25); by the approximate square root method, [it is] 38 622/625. This is the equal altitude in that quadrilateral. The sum of squares of the base minus the smaller perpendicular segment and the equal altitude is 5049; this is the square of the diagonal. Similarly, from the larger perpendicular segment, the square of the second diagonal is 2176. By the approximate square root method, the two diagonals obtained are 71 1/20 and 46 13/20. Thus in a quadrilateral, with those same sides, other diagonals can exist in many ways. Even though [the diagonals are] thus indeterminate, specific diagonals were derived by <s>Brahmagupta</s> and others; that derivation is as follows:

children.text: karṇa-āśrita-bhuja-ghāta-aikyam ubhayathā anyonya-bhājitam @guṇayet/
children.translated_text: The sums of products of sides sharing a diagonal, [found] both ways, divided by each other, should be multiplied

children.text: yogena bhuja-pratibhuja-vadhayos karṇau pade viṣame//
