children.translated_text: by the sum of the products of opposite sides—the square roots of the two unequal [results] are the diagonals.

body.text: nyāsas/ karṇa-āśrita-bhuja-ghāta-ity %eka-vāram anayos 25/ 39 ghātas 975/ tathā 52/ 60 anayos ghātas 3120/ ghātayos %dvayos aikyam 4095/ tathā %dvtīya-vāram 25/ 52/ anayos ghāte jātam 1300/ tathā %dvitīya-vāram 39/ 60/ anayos ghāte jātam 2340/ [tathā 25/ 52 anayos ghāte jātam 1300/] ghātayos %dvayos aikyam 3640/ bhuja-pratibhujayos 52/ 39 ghātas 2028/ paścāt 25/ 60 anayos vadhas 1500/ tayos aikyam 3528/ anena aikyena 3640 guṇitam jātam pūrva-aikyam 12841920/ %prathama-karṇa-āśrita-bhuja-ghāta-aikyena 4095 bhaktam labdham 3136/ asya mūlam 56 %eka-karṇas/ tathā %dvitīya-karṇa-artham %prathama-karṇa-āśrita-bhuja-ghāta-aikyam 4095 bhuja-pratibhuja-vadha-yoga-3528-guṇitam jātam 14447160/ anya-karṇa-āśrita-ghāta-aikyena 3640 bhaktam labdham 3969/ asya mūlam 63 %dvitīyas karṇas// asmin viṣaye kṣetra-karṇa-sādhanam/ asya karṇa-ānayanasya prakriyā-gauravam laghu-prakriyā-darśana-dvāreṇa āha/
body.translated_text: Setting down: By 'products of sides sharing a diagonal,' the first time, the product of 25 and 39 is 975; likewise the product of 52 and 60 is 3120; the sum of the two products is 4095. Similarly, the second time, the product of 25 and 52 is 1300; and the product of 39 and 60 is 2340; the sum of the two products is 3640. The product of opposite sides 52 and 39 is 2028; then the product of 25 and 60 is 1500; their sum is 3528. By this sum, 3640 multiplied gives the first product 12841920; divided by the first sum of products of sides sharing a diagonal, 4095, the quotient is 3136; its square root, 56, is the first diagonal. Similarly, for the second diagonal, the first sum of products of sides sharing a diagonal, 4095, multiplied by the sum of products of opposite sides, 3528, gives 14447160; divided by the other sum of products, 3640, the quotient is 3969; its square root, 63, is the second diagonal. In this topic, [this is] the determination of diagonals of figures. Having [noted] the complexity of this procedure, he states it through showing a simpler method:

children.text: abhīṣṭa-jātya-%dvaya-bāhu-koṭayas parasparam karṇa-hatās bhujās iti/
children.translated_text: The sides and altitudes of two chosen right triangles, mutually multiplied by [the other's] hypotenuse, become the sides;

children.text: %catur-bhujam yat viṣamam prakalpitam śrutī tu tatra %tri-bhuja-%dvayāt tatas//
children.translated_text: the scalene quadrilateral thus constructed—its diagonals [are found] from the two [component] triangles.

children.text: bāhvos vadhas koṭi-vadhena yuk @syāt ekā śrutis koṭi-bhujā-vadha-aikyam/
children.translated_text: The product of the [two] sides, combined with the product of the altitudes, gives one diagonal; the sum of the altitude-side cross-products [gives]

children.text: anyā laghau sati api sādhane asmin pūrvais kṛtam yat guru tat na @vidmas//
children.translated_text: the other. Even though this method of determination is simple, we do not understand why the ancients made [it] laborious!

body.text: jātya-kṣetra-%dvayam/ nyāsas [fig.17][/] etayos itaretara-karṇa-hatās bhujās koṭayas itareta-karṇa-hatās koṭayas bhujās iti kṛte jātam 25/ 60/ 52/ 39/ teṣām mahatī bhūs laghu mukham itarau bāhū iti @prakalpya kṣetra-darśanam/ [fig. lost] imau karṇau mahatā āyāsena ānītau 63/ 56/ asya eva jātya-%dvayasya uttara-uttara-bhuja-koṭyos ghātau jātau 36/ 20/ anayos aikyam %ekas karṇas 56/ bāhvos 3/ 5/ koṭyos ca 4/ 12/ ghātau 15/ 48/ anayos aikyam anyas karṇas 63/ evam śrutī @syātām/ evam sukhena @jñāyate// atha yadi pārśva-bhuja-mukhayos vyatyayam @kṛtvā nyastam kṣetram/ nyāsas/ [fig.18] tadā jātya-%dvaya-karṇayos vadhas 65 %dvitīya-karṇas// atha sūcī-kṣetra-udāharaṇam/ [fig.19]
body.translated_text: Two right triangles. Setting down: [Fig. 17]. Of these, the sides multiplied by each other's hypotenuse and the altitudes multiplied by each other's hypotenuse—doing thus, the results are 25, 60, 52, 39; of these, the greatest is the base, the smallest is the face, the other two are the sides—thus constructing the figure. [Fig. lost] These diagonals, 63 and 56, were obtained with great effort. From these same two right triangles, the successive products of sides and altitudes are 36 and 20; their sum is one diagonal, 56. Of the sides 3, 5, and the altitudes 4, 12, the products are 15 and 48; their sum is the other diagonal, 63. Thus the diagonals are [found]; thus [it] is known easily. Now, if the figure is set down with the lateral sides and the face interchanged: Setting down: [Fig. 18] Then the product of the hypotenuses of the two right triangles, 65, is the second diagonal. Now, an example of a needle-shaped figure (<s>sūcī-kṣetra</s>): [Fig. 19]

children.text: kṣetre yatra %śata-%trayam 300 kṣiti-mitis #tattva-#indu-125-tulyam mukham/
children.translated_text: In a figure where the base measures three hundred, the face equals 125,

children.text: bāhū #kha-#utkṛtibhis 260 #śara-#atidhṛtibhis 195 tulyau ca tatra śrutī/
children.translated_text: the sides equal 260 and 195, and the diagonals there—

children.text: %ekā #kha-%aṣṭa-#yamais 280 samā #tithi-#guṇais 315 anyā atha tad-lambakau[/]
children.translated_text: one equals 280, the other 315; and its two altitudes

children.text: tulyau #go-#dhṛtibhis 189 tathā #jina-#yamais 224 yogāt śravas-lambayos//
children.translated_text: equal 189 and 224; from the sum of the diagonals and altitudes—

children.text: tad-khaṇḍe @kathaya adhare śravaṇayos yogāt ca lamba-abadhe[/]
children.translated_text: state the lower segments of the two diagonals, and from the sum [of diagonals], the altitude and base-segments;

children.text: tad-sūcī nija-mārga-vṛddha-bhujayos yogāt yathā @syāt tatas/
children.translated_text: the needle[-figure], from the sides extended along their own paths such that [they meet]—

children.text: sa-ābādham @vada lambakam ca bhujayos sūcyās pramāṇe ca ke[/]
children.translated_text: state the altitude with perpendicular segments, and what are the measures of the sides of the needle[-figure]?

children.text: sarvam gāṇitika @pracakṣva nitarām kṣetre atra dakṣas @asi ced//
children.translated_text: Declare all this completely, O calculator, if you are skilled in this figure!

body.text: atha saṃdhi-ādi-ānayanāya karaṇa-sūtram vṛtta-%dvayam/
body.translated_text: Now, for finding the junction (<s>saṃdhi</s>) and other [quantities], the rule of operation in two verses:

children.text: lamba-tad-āśrita-bāhvos madhyam saṃdhi-ākhyam asya lambasya/
children.translated_text: The mean of the altitude and the side resting on it is called the junction (<s>saṃdhi</s>); the base diminished by this junction

children.text: saṃdhi-ūnā bhūs pīṭham sādhyam yasya adharam khaṇḍam//
children.translated_text: of its altitude is the pedestal (<s>pīṭha</s>); its lower segment is to be determined.

children.text: saṃdhis dviṣṭhas para-lamba-śravaṇa-hatas parasya pīṭhena/
children.translated_text: The junction, doubled, multiplied by the product of the other [triangle's] altitude and diagonal, divided by the other's pedestal—

children.text: bhaktas lamba-śrutyos yogāt @syātām adhas-khaṇḍe//
children.translated_text: [the results] from the sum of altitude and diagonal give the lower segments.

body.text: lambas 189/ tad-āśrita-bhujas 195/ anayos madhye yat lamba-lamba-āśrita-bāhu-varga-iti-ādinā āgatā ābādhā saṃdhi-saṃjñā 48/ tad-ūnita-bhūs iti %dvitīyā ābādhā sā pīṭha-saṃjñā 252/ evam %dvitīya-lambas 224/ tad-āśrita-bhujas 260[/] pūrva-vat saṃdhis 132/ pīṭham 168// atha ādya-lambasya 189 adhas-khaṇḍam sādhyam/ asya saṃdhis 48/ %dvi-sthas 48/ para-lambena 224/ śravaṇena ca 280/ pṛthak guṇitas 10752/ 13440/ parasya pīṭhena 168 bhaktas labdham lamba-adhas-khaṇḍam 64/ śravaṇa-adhas-khaṇḍam ca 80/ evam %dvitīya-lambasya 224/ saṃdhis 132/ para-lambena 189/ karṇena ca 315/ pṛthak guṇitas parasya pīṭhena 252 bhaktas labdham lamba-adhas-khaṇḍam 99/ śravaṇa-adhas-khaṇḍam ca 165// atha karṇayos yogāt adhas-lamba-jñāna-artham sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Altitude 189; the side resting on it 195; the mean of these, the perpendicular segment obtained by 'the square root of the sum of squares of the altitude and altitude-side' etc., is the junction, 48; the base diminished by that gives the second perpendicular segment, the pedestal, 252. Similarly, the second altitude 224; the side resting on it 260; as before, the junction is 132; the pedestal is 168. Now, to determine the lower segment of the first altitude 189: its junction 48, doubled [gives] 48; multiplied by the other altitude 224 and the diagonal 280 separately, [gives] 10752 and 13440; divided by the other's pedestal 168, the lower segment of the altitude is 64 and the lower segment of the diagonal is 80. Similarly, for the second altitude 224: the junction 132, multiplied by the other altitude 189 and the diagonal 315 separately, divided by the other's pedestal 252, the lower segment of the altitude is 99 and the lower segment of the diagonal is 165. Now, for finding the lower altitude from the sum of the diagonals, the rule in a verse:

children.text: lambau bhū-ghnau nija-nija-pīṭha-vibhaktau ca vaṃśau @stas/
children.translated_text: The altitudes multiplied by the base, divided by their respective pedestals, give the poles (<s>vaṃśa</s>);

children.text: tābhyām prāk-vat śrutyos yogāt lambas ku-khaṇḍe ca//
children.translated_text: from those, as before, from the sum of the diagonals, the altitude and base-segments [are found].

body.text: lambau 189/ 224/ bhū-300-ghnau jātau 56700/ 67200/ sva-sva-pīṭhābhyām 252/ 168 bhaktau/ evam atra labdhau vaṃśau 225/ 400/ ābhyām anyonya-mūla-agra-ga-sūtra-yogāt iti-ādi-karaṇena labdhas karṇa-yogāt adhas-lambas 144/ bhū-khaṇḍe ca 108/ 192// atha sūcī-ābādhā-lamba-bhuja-jñāna-artham sūtram vṛtta-%trayam/
body.translated_text: Altitudes 189 and 224, multiplied by the base 300, give 56700 and 67200; divided by their respective pedestals 252 and 168, the poles obtained are 225 and 400; from these, by the method of 'the cord going from the base to the top of each other' etc., the altitude obtained from the sum of diagonals is 144; the base-segments are 108 and 192. Now, for finding the needle-point perpendicular segments, altitude, and sides, the rule of operation in three verses:

children.text: lamba-hṛtas nija-saṃdhis para-lamba-guṇas sama-āhvayas jñeyas/
children.translated_text: One's own junction divided by one's altitude, multiplied by the other altitude, is known as the 'equal' (<s>sama</s>);

children.text: sama-para-saṃdhyos aikyam hāras tena uddhṛtau tau ca//
children.translated_text: the sum of the 'equal' and the other junction is the divisor; dividing the two by it—

children.text: sama-para-saṃdhī bhū-ghnau sūcī-ābādhe pṛthak @syātām/
children.translated_text: the 'equal' and the other junction, multiplied by the base, give the needle-segments (<s>sūcī-ābādhā</s>) separately;

children.text: hāra-hṛtas para-lambas sūcī-lambas @bhavet bhū-ghnas//
children.translated_text: the other altitude, divided by the divisor, multiplied by the base, gives the needle-altitude (<s>sūcī-lamba</s>).

children.text: sūcī-lamba-ghna-bhujau nija-nija-lamba-uddhṛtau bhujau sūcyās/
children.translated_text: The sides multiplied by the needle-altitude, divided by their respective altitudes, give the sides of the needle[-figure].

children.text: evam kṣetra-kṣodas prājñais trairāśikāt @kriyate//
children.translated_text: Thus the subdivision of figures is performed by the wise through the Rule of Three.

body.text: atra kila ayam lambas 224/ asya saṃdhis 132/ ayam para-lambena 189 guṇitas 224 anena bhaktas jātas sama-āhvayas 891_8/ asya para-saṃdhes ca 48/ yogas hāras 1275_8/ anena bhū-ghnas 300 samas 267300_8 para-saṃdhis ca 14400_1/ bhaktas jāte sūcī-ābādhe 3564_17/ 1536_17/ evam %dvitīya-sama-āhvayas 512_9/ %dvitīyas hāras 1700_9/ anena bhū-ghnas svīyas samas 153600_9/ para-saṃdhis ca 39600_1/ bhaktas jāte sūcī-ābādhe 1536_17/ 3564_17/ [āpaṭe: jāta < jāte] para-lambas 224/ bhūmi-300-guṇas hāreṇa 1700_9 bhaktas jātas sūcī-lambas 6048_17/ sūcī-lambena bhujau 195/ 260 guṇitau sva-sva-lambābhyām 189/ 224 yathā-kramam bhaktau jātau sva-mārga-vṛddhau sūcī-bhujau 6240_17[/] 7020_17/ evam atra sarvatra bhāga-hāra-rāśi-pramāṇam/ guṇya-guṇakau tu yathā-yogyam phala-icche @prakalpya sudhiyā trairāśikam ūhyam// atha vṛtta-kṣetre karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Here, this altitude is 224; its junction is 132; this multiplied by the other altitude 189 and divided by 224 gives the 'equal,' 891/8; the sum of this and the other junction 48 is the divisor 1275/8. By this, the 'equal' multiplied by the base 300 gives 267300/8, and the other junction gives 14400; divided [by the divisor], the needle-segments obtained are 3564/17 and 1536/17. Similarly, the second 'equal' is 512/9; the second divisor is 1700/9; by this, one's own [value] multiplied by the base 153600/9, and the other junction 39600, divided, the needle-segments obtained are 1536/17 and 3564/17. The other altitude 224, multiplied by the base 300, divided by the divisor 1700/9, gives the needle-altitude 6048/17. The sides 195 and 260, multiplied by the needle-altitude and divided by their respective altitudes 189 and 224 in order, give the sides of the needle[-figure] extended along their own paths: 6240/17 and 7020/17. Thus everywhere here [the computation follows from] the divisor-quantity-measure; the multiplicand and multiplier should be suitably assigned as the fruit and desire, and the Rule of Three should be inferred by the intelligent. Now, for circular figures, the rule of operation in a verse:

children.text: vyāse #bha-#nanda-#agni-3927-hate vibhakte #kha-#bāṇa-#sūryais 1250 paridhis sas sūkṣmas/ [śarma: susūkṣmas < sas sūkṣmas]
children.translated_text: When the diameter is multiplied by 3927 and divided by 1250, [one obtains] the precise circumference;

children.text: %dvāviṃśati-22-ghne vihṛte atha #śailais 7 sthūlas atha vā @syāt vyavahāra-yogyas//
children.translated_text: when multiplied by 22 and divided by 7, the approximate [circumference results], suitable for practical use.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: viṣkambha-mānam kila %sapta 7 yatra tatra pramāṇam paridhes @pracakṣva/
children.translated_text: Where the measure of the diameter is seven, declare the measure of the circumference!

children.text: %dvāviṃśatis 22 yad-paridhi-pramāṇam tad-vyāsa-saṃkhyām ca sakhe @vicintya//
children.translated_text: And that whose circumference measures twenty-two—consider its diameter-count, O friend!

body.text: nyāsas/ vyāsa-mānam 7/ labdham paridhi-mānam 21_1239_1250/ [fig.20] sthūlas vā paridhis labdhas 22// atha vā paridhi-tas vyāsa-ānayanāya nyāsas/ [paridhi-mānam 22/] guṇa-hāra-viparyayeṇa vyāsa-mānam sūkṣmam 7_11_3927[/] sthūlam vā 7// vṛtta-golayos phala-ānayane karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: diameter measure 7; the circumference obtained is 21 1239/1250. [Fig. 20] Or the approximate circumference obtained is 22. Alternatively, for finding the diameter from the circumference, setting down: [circumference measure 22;] by reversing the multiplier and divisor, the precise diameter measure is 7 11/3927; or the approximate is 7. For finding the area and volume of circles and spheres, the rule of operation in a verse:

children.text: vṛtta-kṣetre paridhi-guṇita-vyāsa-pādas phalam yat kṣuṇṇam vedais upari paritas kandukasya iva jālam/ [āpaṭe: -kṣetra < -kṣetre]
children.translated_text: In a circular figure, one-quarter of the diameter multiplied by the circumference is the area; that, multiplied by four, [covers the surface] like a net around a ball—

children.text: golasya evam tat api ca phalam pṛṣṭha-jam vyāsa-nighnam %ṣaḍbhis bhaktam @bhavati niyatam gola-garbhe ghana-ākhyam//
children.translated_text: such is the surface area of the sphere; that, multiplied by the diameter and divided by six, invariably gives the volume (<s>ghana</s>) inside the sphere.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: yad-vyāsas #turagais mitas kila phalam kṣetre same tatra kim vyāsas %sapta-mitas ca yasya sumate golasya tasya api kim/
children.translated_text: The area of the flat circle whose diameter is measured by seven—what is that? And of the sphere whose diameter is seven, O wise one, what also [is its surface]?

children.text: pṛṣṭhe kanduka-jāla-saṃnibha-phalam golasya tasya api kim madhye @brūhi ghanam phalam ca vimalām ced @vetsi līlāvatīm//
children.translated_text: What is the surface area of the sphere, resembling the net of a ball? And what is the solid volume inside it? Tell me, if you know the clear <s>Līlāvatī</s>!

body.text: vṛtta-kṣetra-phala-darśanāya nyāsas/ [fig.22] vyāsas 7/ paridhis 21_1239_1250/ [āpaṭe: 1250 < 1239] kṣetra-phalam 38_2423_5000/ gola-pṛṣṭha-phala-darśanāya nyāsas/ [fig.23] vyāsas 7/ gola-pṛṣṭha-phalam 153_1173_1250/ gola-antar-gata-ghana-phala-darśanāya nyāsas/ [fig.24] vyāsas 7/ golasya antar-gatam ghana-phalam 179_1487_2500// atha prakāra-antareṇa tad-phala-ānayane karaṇa-sūtram sa-%ardha-vṛttam/
body.translated_text: For showing the area of the circular figure, setting down: [Fig. 22] Diameter 7; circumference 21 1239/1250; area of the figure 38 2423/5000. For showing the surface area of the sphere, setting down: [Fig. 23] Diameter 7; surface area of the sphere 153 1173/1250. For showing the volume inside the sphere, setting down: [Fig. 24] Diameter 7; volume inside the sphere 179 1487/2500. Now, for finding that area by another method, the rule of operation in a verse and a half:

children.text: vyāsasya varge #bha-%nava-#agni-nighne sūkṣmam phalam %pañca-%sahasra-bhakte/
children.translated_text: When the square of the diameter is multiplied by 3927, the precise area [is obtained] when divided by 5000;

children.text: #rudra-āhate #śakra-hṛte atha vā @syāt sthūlam phalam tat vyavahāra-yogyam//
children.translated_text: or when multiplied by 11 and divided by 14, the approximate area results, suitable for practical use.

children.text: ghanī-kṛta-vyāsa-#dalam nija-%ekaviṃśa-aṃśa-yuk gola-ghanam phalam @syāt//
children.translated_text: The cube of half the diameter, increased by one twenty-first of itself, gives the solid volume of the sphere.

body.text: śara-jīva-ānayanāya karaṇa-sūtram sa-%ardha-vṛttam/
body.translated_text: For finding the arrow (versine) and the chord, the rule of operation in a verse and a half:

children.text: jyā-vyāsa-yoga-antara-ghāta-mūlam vyāsas tad-ūnas dalitas śaras @syāt/
children.translated_text: The square root of the product of the sum and difference of the chord and diameter—the diameter minus that, halved, is the arrow (versine).

children.text: vyāsāt śara-ūnāt śara-saṃguṇāt ca mūlam %dvi-nighnam @bhavati iha jīvā/
children.translated_text: From the diameter minus the arrow, multiplied by the arrow, the square root multiplied by two is the chord (<s>jīvā</s>).

children.text: jīvā-%ardha-varge śara-bhakta-yukte vyāsa-pramāṇam @pravadanti vṛtte//
children.translated_text: The square of half the chord, divided by the arrow and added [to the arrow]—that is declared to be the measure of the diameter in a circle.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: %daśa-vistṛti-vṛtta-antar yatra jyā %ṣaṣ-mitā sakhe/
children.translated_text: In a circle of breadth ten, where the chord measures six, O friend—

children.text: tatra iṣum @vada bāṇāt jyām jyā-bāṇābhyām ca vistṛtim//
children.translated_text: there tell the arrow from the chord, the chord from the arrow, and the diameter from the chord and arrow.

body.text: nyāsas/ [fig.25] vyāsas 10/ jyā 6/ yogas 16/ antaram 4/ ghātas 64/ mūlam 8/ etad-ūnas vyāsas 2/ dalitas 1/ jātas śaras 1/ vyāsāt 10/ śara-ūnāt 9/ śara-1-saṃguṇāt 9/ mūlam 3 %dvi-nighnam jātā jīvā 6// evam jñātābhyām jyā-bāṇābhyām vyāsa-ānayanam yathā/ jīvā-%ardha-3-varge 9 śara-1-bhakte 9/ śara-1-yukte jātas vyāsas 10// atha vṛtta-antar-%tri-asra-ādi-%nava-asra-anta-kṣetrāṇām bhuja-māna-ānayanāya karaṇa-sūtram vṛtta-%trayam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: [fig. 25] diameter 10/ chord 6/ sum 16/ difference 4/ product 64/ root 8/ diameter less this: 2/ halved: 1/ the obtained arrow (<s>śara</s>) is 1/ From the diameter 10, less the arrow 9, multiplied by the arrow 1, giving 9/ root 3, doubled, the obtained chord (<s>jīvā</s>) is 6// Similarly, from the known chord and arrow, the derivation of the diameter is as follows: the square of half the chord (3) is 9, divided by the arrow (1) gives 9, plus the arrow (1), the obtained diameter is 10// Now for deriving the side-measures of triangular and other figures up to nonagons inscribed in a circle, the rule of operation in three verses:

children.text: %tri-%dvi-#aṅka-#agni-#nabhas-#candrais 103923 %tri-#bāṇa-%aṣṭa-#yuga-%aṣṭabhis 84853/ [śarma: %dvi-%dvi- < tri-dvi-]
children.translated_text: By [the constants] 103923 for three, 84853 for [four],

children.text: #veda-#agni-#bāṇa-#kha-#aśvais 70534 ca #kha-#kha-#abhra-#abhra-#rasais 60000 kramāt//
children.translated_text: 70534 for [five], and 60000 for [six], in order;

children.text: #bāṇa-#iṣu-#nakha-#bāṇais 52055 ca %dvi-%dvi-#nanda-#iṣu-#sāgarais 45922/ [śarma: #śaila-#ṛtu- < bāṇa-iṣu-]
children.translated_text: and 52055 for [seven], 45922 for [eight],

children.text: #ku-#rāma-%daśa-#vedais 41031 ca vṛtta-vyāse samāhate// [śarma: %tri-#veda- < ku-rāma-]
children.translated_text: and 41031 for [nine]—when the circle's diameter is multiplied [by these]

children.text: #kha-#kha-#kha-#abhra-#arka-120000-saṃbhakte @labhyante kramaśas bhujās/
children.translated_text: and divided by 120000, the sides are obtained successively

children.text: vṛtta-antar-%tri-asra-pūrvāṇām %nava-asra-antam pṛthak pṛthak// [śarma: vṛtta-tad- < vṛtta-antar-, nava-antānām < nava-asra-antam]
children.translated_text: of the inscribed figures from the triangle onward up to the nonagon, each separately.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: %sahasra-%dvitaya-vyāsam yat vṛttam tasya madhyatas/
children.translated_text: In a circle whose diameter is two thousand, tell me from its center

children.text: sama-%tri-asra-ādikānām me bhujān @vada pṛthak pṛthak//
children.translated_text: the sides of the equilateral triangle and other [inscribed regular polygons] separately!

body.text: atha vṛtta-antar-%tri-bhuje bhuja-māna-ānayanāya nyāsas/ [fig.26] vyāsas 2000/ %tri-%dvi-#aṅka-#agni-#nabhas-#candrais 103923 guṇitas 207846000 %kha-%kha-%kha-%abhra-%arkais 120000 bhakte labdham %tri-asre bhuja-mānam 1732_1_20// vṛtta-antar-%catur-bhuje bhuja-māna-ānayanāya nyāsas/ [fig.27] vyāsas 2000/ %tri-#bāṇa-%aṣṭa-#yuga-%aṣṭabhis 84853 guṇitas 169706000 #kha-#kha-#kha-#abhra-#arkais 120000 bhakte labdham %catur-asre bhuja-mānam 1414_13_60// vṛtta-antar-%pañca-bhuje bhuja-māna-ānayanāya nyāsas/ [fig.28] vyāsas 2000/ #veda-#agni-#bāṇa-#kha-#aśvais 70534 guṇitas 141068000 #kha-#kha-#kha-#abhra-#arkais 120000 bhakte labdham %pañca-asre bhuja-mānam 1175_17_30// vṛtta-antar-%ṣaṣ-bhuje bhuja-māna-ānayanāya nyāsas/ [fig.29] vyāsas 2000/ #kha-#kha-#abhra-#abhra-#rasais 60000 guṇitas 120000000 #kha-#kha-#kha-#abhra-#arkais 120000 bhaktas labdham %ṣaṣ-asre bhuja-mānam 1000// vṛtta-antar-%sapta-bhuje bhuja-māna-ānayanāya nyāsas/ [fig. 30] vyāsas 2000/ #bāṇa-#iṣu-#nakha-#bāṇais 52055 guṇitas 104110000 #kha-#kha-#kha-#abhra-#arkais 120000 bhakte labdham #sapta-asre bhuja-mānam 867_7_12// vṛtta-antar-%aṣṭa-bhuje bhuja-māna-ānayanāya nyāsas/ [fig.30a, lost] vyāsas 2000/ %dvi-%dvi-#nanda-#iṣu-sāgarais 45922 guṇitas 91844000 #kha-#kha-#kha-#abhra-#arkais 120000 bhakte labdham #aṣṭa-asre bhuja-mānam 765_11_30// vṛtta-antar-%nava-bhuje bhuja-māna-ānayanāya nyāsas/ [fig.31] vyāsas 2000/ #ku-#rāma-%daśa-#vedais 41031 guṇitas 82062000 #kha-#kha-#kha-#abhra-#arkais 120000 bhaktas labdham %nava-asre bhuja-mānam 683_17_20// evam iṣṭa-vyāsa-ādibhyas anyās api jīvās @sidhyanti iti tās tu gole jyā-utpattau @vakṣye// atha sthūla-jīvā-jñāna-artham laghu-kriyayā karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Now for deriving the side-measure of the inscribed triangle, setting down: [fig. 26] diameter 2000/ multiplied by 103923, giving 207846000, divided by 120000, the obtained side-measure of the triangle is 1732 1/20// For deriving the side-measure of the inscribed square, setting down: [fig. 27] diameter 2000/ multiplied by 84853, giving 169706000, divided by 120000, the obtained side-measure of the square is 1414 13/60// For deriving the side-measure of the inscribed pentagon, setting down: [fig. 28] diameter 2000/ multiplied by 70534, giving 141068000, divided by 120000, the obtained side-measure of the pentagon is 1175 17/30// For deriving the side-measure of the inscribed hexagon, setting down: [fig. 29] diameter 2000/ multiplied by 60000, giving 120000000, divided by 120000, the obtained side-measure of the hexagon is 1000// For deriving the side-measure of the inscribed heptagon, setting down: [fig. 30] diameter 2000/ multiplied by 52055, giving 104110000, divided by 120000, the obtained side-measure of the heptagon is 867 7/12// For deriving the side-measure of the inscribed octagon, setting down: [fig. 30a, lost] diameter 2000/ multiplied by 45922, giving 91844000, divided by 120000, the obtained side-measure of the octagon is 765 11/30// For deriving the side-measure of the inscribed nonagon, setting down: [fig. 31] diameter 2000/ multiplied by 41031, giving 82062000, divided by 120000, the obtained side-measure of the nonagon is 683 17/20// Thus from a desired diameter and so forth, other chords also can be determined; but those I shall state in the [section on the] sphere, in the generation of sines// Now for knowing approximate chords by an easy method, the rule of operation in a verse:

children.text: cāpa-ūna-nighna-paridhis %prathama-āhvayas @syāt %pañca-āhatas paridhi-varga-%caturtha-bhāgas/
children.translated_text: The circumference multiplied by [itself] diminished by the arc is called the first [quantity]; the quarter of the square of the circumference multiplied by five [is the second].

children.text: ādya-ūnitena khalu tena @bhajet %catur-ghna-vyāsa-āhatam %prathamam āptam iha jyakā @syāt//
children.translated_text: Dividing the first [quantity] multiplied by four times the diameter by the second diminished by the first, the result here will be the chord.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: %aṣṭādaśa-aṃśena vṛtes samānam %eka-ādi-nighnena ca yatra cāpam/
children.translated_text: Where the arc equals one-eighteenth of the circumference, and [also] multiplied by one, two, and so on,

children.text: pṛthak pṛthak tatra @vada āśu jīvām #kha-#arkais mitam vyāsa-#dalam ca yatra//
children.translated_text: tell quickly the chord in each case separately, where the half-diameter measures one hundred and twenty!

body.text: nyāsas/ [fig.32] vyāsas 240/ atra kila aṅka-lāghavāya %viṃśates sa-%ardha-#arka-%śata-aṃśa-militas sūkṣma-paridhis 754/ asya %aṣṭādaśa-aṃśas 42/ atra api aṅka-lāghavāya %dvayos %aṣṭādaśa-aṃśa-yutas gṛhītas/ anena pṛthak pṛthak %eka-ādi-guṇitena tulye dhanuṣi kalpite jyās sādhyās// atha vā atra sukha-artham paridhes %aṣṭādaśa-aṃśena paridhim dhanūṃṣi ca @apavartya jyās sādhyās tathā api tās eva @bhavanti/ apavartite nyāsas/ paridhis 18/ cāpāni ca 1/ 2/ 3/ 4/ 5/ 6/ 7/ 8/ 9/ yathā-ukta-karaṇena labdhās jīvās 42/ 82/ 120/ 154/ 184/ 208/ 226/ 236/ 240// atha cāpa-ānayanāya karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: [fig. 32] diameter 240/ Here, for convenience of computation, the precise circumference including the fractional part in twelve-hundredths of twenty is 754/ Its eighteenth part is 42/ Here also, for convenience, two-eighteenth parts have been taken. With this [unit], multiplied separately by one and so on, equal arcs being assumed, the chords are to be determined// Or here, for ease, dividing the circumference and arcs by the eighteenth part of the circumference, the chords are to be determined—they turn out the same. Setting down after reduction: circumference 18/ arcs 1/ 2/ 3/ 4/ 5/ 6/ 7/ 8/ 9/ By the stated operation, the obtained chords are 42/ 82/ 120/ 154/ 184/ 208/ 226/ 236/ 240// Now for finding the arc, the rule of operation in a verse:

children.text: vyāsa-#abdhi-ghāta-yuta-maurvikayā vibhaktas jīvā-#aṅghri-%pañca-guṇitas paridhes tu vargas/
children.translated_text: The square of the circumference multiplied by five times the quarter of the chord, divided by the chord plus the product of the diameter and four,

children.text: labdha-ūnitāt paridhi-varga-%caturtha-bhāgāt āpte pade vṛti-#dalāt patite dhanus @syāt//
children.translated_text: subtracted from a quarter of the square of the circumference—the square root of the result, subtracted from half the circumference, gives the arc.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: viditās iha ye guṇās tatas @vada teṣām adhunā dhanus-mitīs/ [śarma: svatas < tatas, atha me < adhunā, -mitim < -mitīs]
children.translated_text: The chords being known here, now tell their arc-measures;

children.text: yadi te @asti dhanus-guṇa-kriyā-gaṇite gāṇitika atinaipuṇam// [śarma: atinaipuṇī]
children.translated_text: if you have supreme skill in the computation of arcs and chords, O mathematician!

body.text: nyāsas/ jyās 42/ 82/ 120/ 154/ 184/ 208/ 226/ 236/ 240[/] sas eva apavartita-paridhis 18/ jīvā-#aṅghriṇā 21_2 %pañcabhis 5 ca paridhes 18 vargas 324 guṇitas 17010/ vyāsa-240-#abdhi-4-ghāta-960-yuta-maurvikayā 1002 anayā vibhaktas labdhas 17/ atra aṅka-lāghavāya %caturviṃśates %dvi-adhika-%sahasra-aṃśa-yutas gṛhītas/ anena ūnitāt paridhi-18-varga-324-%caturtha-81-bhāgāt 64 pade prāpte 8 vṛti-18-#dalāt 9 patite 1 jātam dhanus/ evam jātāni dhanūṃṣi 1/ 2/ 3/ 4/ 5/ 6/ 7/ 8/ 9[/] etāni paridhi-%aṣṭādaśa-aṃśena guṇitāni @syus// iti bhāskara-ācārya-viracitāyām līlāvatyām kṣetra-vyavahāras samāptas//
body.translated_text: Setting down: chords 42/ 82/ 120/ 154/ 184/ 208/ 226/ 236/ 240/ the same reduced circumference 18/ The chord-quarter 21/2, multiplied by five (5), and the circumference-18 square 324, [giving] 17010/ divided by the chord plus the product of diameter-240 and four (960), that is, the chord plus 960 = 1002, giving 17/ Here for computational convenience, twenty-four with the fractional part in thousandths of two has been taken. Subtracting this from the quarter of the circumference-18 square (324) quarter (81), giving 64, the root obtained is 8, subtracted from half the circumference (18) half (9), giving 1—the obtained arc/ Similarly the obtained arcs are 1/ 2/ 3/ 4/ 5/ 6/ 7/ 8/ 9/ These, multiplied by one-eighteenth of the circumference, give [the actual arcs]// Thus ends the section on field-computation (<s>kṣetra-vyavahāra</s>) in the <s>Līlāvatī</s> composed by <s>Bhāskara-ācārya</s>//

body.text: khāta-vyavahāra
body.translated_text: Section on Excavation

body.text: atha khāta-vyavahāras/ karaṇa-sūtram sa-%ardhā āryā/
body.translated_text: Now the section on excavation (<s>khāta-vyavahāra</s>)/ The rule of operation in one and a half <s>āryā</s> verses:

children.text: @gaṇayitvā vistāram bahuṣu sthāneṣu tad-yutis bhājyā/
children.translated_text: Having measured the width at many places, their sum should be divided

children.text: sthānaka-mityā sama-mitis evam dairghyam ca vedhe ca//
children.translated_text: by the number of places—[this gives] the uniform measure. Similarly for the length and for the depth.

children.text: kṣetra-phalam vedha-guṇam khāte ghana-hasta-saṃkhyā @syāt// [śarma: ghāte < khāte]
children.translated_text: The field-area multiplied by the depth gives the number of cubic cubits in the excavation.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: bhuja-vakratayā dairghyam %daśa-#īśa-#arka-karais mitam/
children.translated_text: An excavation whose length, due to the crookedness of the sides, measures ten, eleven, and twelve cubits,

children.text: %triṣu sthāneṣu %ṣaṣ-%pañca-%sapta-hastā ca vistṛtis// [śarma: -hastā atra < -hastā ca]
children.translated_text: and whose width at three places measures six, five, and seven cubits,

children.text: yasya khātasya vedhas api %dvi-%catur-%tri-karas sakhe/ [śarma: -tri-mitas < -tri-karas]
children.translated_text: and whose depth also measures two, four, and three cubits, O friend—

children.text: tatra khāte kiyantas @syus ghana-hastās @pracakṣva me//
children.translated_text: how many cubic cubits are there in that excavation? Tell me!

body.text: nyāsas/ [fig.33] atra sama-miti-karaṇena vistāre hastās 6/ dairghye 11 vedhe ca 3/ tathā kṛte kṣetra-darśanam/ nyāsas/ [fig.34] yathā-ukta-karaṇena labdhā ghana-hasta-saṃkhyā 198// [āpaṭe: -raṇena < -karaṇena] khāta-antare karaṇa-sūtram sa-ardha-vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: [fig. 33] Here, by the averaging method, the width in cubits is 6/ the length 11/ and the depth 3/ When so determined, the field shown is: setting down [fig. 34]. By the stated method, the obtained number of cubic cubits is 198// For a different [type of] excavation, the rule of operation in one and a half verses:

children.text: mukha-ja-tala-ja-tad-yuti-ja-kṣetra-phala-aikyam hṛtam %ṣaḍbhis/
children.translated_text: The sum of the field-areas generated from the top, from the bottom, and from their combination, divided by six,

children.text: kṣetra-phalam samam evam vedha-hatam ghana-phalam spaṣṭam// [śarma: -guṇam < -hatam]
children.translated_text: is the uniform field-area. This, multiplied by the depth, gives the exact cubic volume.

children.text: sama-khāta-phala-%tri-aṃśas sūcī-khāte phalam @bhavati//
children.translated_text: One-third of the volume of a uniform excavation is the volume of a needle-shaped (<s>sūcī</s>) excavation.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: mukhe %daśa-%dvādaśa-hasta-tulyam vistāra-dairghyam tu tale tad-%ardham/ [śarma: -tulye < -tulyam, -dairghye < -dairghyam]
children.translated_text: An [excavation] whose width and length at the top measure ten and twelve cubits, and at the bottom half of that,

children.text: yasyās sakhe %sapta-karas ca vedhas kā khāta-saṃkhyā @vada tatra vāpyām//
children.translated_text: and whose depth is seven cubits, O friend—what is the excavation-volume? Tell me, in that cistern!

body.text: nyāsas/ [fig.35] mukha-jam kṣetra-phalam 120/ tala-jam 30/ tad-yuti-jam 270/ eṣām aikyam 420/ %ṣaḍbhis 6 hṛtam jātam sama-phalam 70 vedha-7-hatam jātam khāta-phalam ghana-hastās 490// %dvitīya-udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: [fig. 35] The field-area from the top is 120/ from the bottom 30/ from their combination 270/ Their sum is 420/ divided by six (6), the obtained uniform area is 70, multiplied by the depth (7), the obtained excavation-volume in cubic cubits is 490// Second example:

children.text: khāte atha #tigmakara-tulya-%catur-bhuje ca kim @syāt phalam %nava-mitas kila yatra vedhas/ [śarma: khalu < kila]
children.translated_text: In an excavation that is a square with side twelve, what will be the volume where the depth is nine?

children.text: vṛtte tathā eva %daśa-vistṛti-%pañca-vedhe sūcī-phalam @vada tayos ca pṛthak pṛthak me//
children.translated_text: And in a circular [excavation] of diameter ten and depth five, tell me the needle-volume of each separately!

body.text: nyāsas/ [fig.36] bhujas 12/ vedhas 9/ jātam yathā-ukta-karaṇena khāta-phalam ghana-hastās 1296/ sūcī-phalam 432// vṛtta-khāta-darśanāya nyāsas/ [fig.37] vyāsas 10/ vedhas 5/ atra sūkṣma-paridhis 3927_125/ sūkṣma-kṣetra-phalam 3927_50/ vedha-guṇam jātam khāta-phalam 3927_10/ sūkṣma-sūcī-phalam 1309_10/ yat vā sthūla-khāta-phalam 2750_7/ sūcī-phalam sthūlam 2750_21// iti khāta-vyavahāras samāptas//
body.translated_text: Setting down: [fig. 36] side 12/ depth 9/ By the stated method, the obtained excavation-volume in cubic cubits is 1296/ the needle-volume is 432// For showing the circular excavation, setting down: [fig. 37] diameter 10/ depth 5/ Here the precise circumference is 3927/125/ the precise field-area is 3927/50/ multiplied by the depth, the obtained excavation-volume is 3927/10/ the precise needle-volume is 1309/10/ Or alternatively, the approximate excavation-volume is 2750/7/ and the approximate needle-volume is 2750/21// Thus ends the section on excavation//

body.text: citi-vyavahāra
body.translated_text: Section on Stacking

body.text: citau karaṇa-sūtram sa-%ardha-vṛttam/
body.translated_text: For stacking, the rule of operation in one and a half verses:

children.text: ucchrayeṇa guṇitam cites kila kṣetra-saṃbhava-phalam ghanam @bhavet/ [śarma: api < kila]
children.translated_text: The field-area arising from the [base of the] stack, multiplied by the height, becomes the cubic [volume].

children.text: iṣṭakā-ghana-hṛte ghane cites iṣṭakā-parimitis ca @labhyate// [śarma: tu < ca]
children.translated_text: The cubic [volume] divided by the cubic [measure] of a brick gives the count of bricks in the stack.

children.text: iṣṭakā-ucchraya-hṛt-ucchritis cites @syus starās ca dṛṣadām cites api//
children.translated_text: The height of the stack divided by the height of a brick gives the number of layers; and similarly for a stone stack.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: %aṣṭādaśa-aṅgulam dairghyam vistāras %dvādaśa-aṅgulas/
children.translated_text: Bricks whose length is eighteen <s>aṅgula</s>s (finger-widths), width twelve <s>aṅgula</s>s,

children.text: ucchritis %tri-aṅgulā yāsām iṣṭakās tās citau kila//
children.translated_text: and height three <s>aṅgula</s>s—those bricks are used in a stack

children.text: yad-vistṛtis %pañca-karā %aṣṭa-hastam dairghyam ca yasyām %tri-kara-ucchritis ca/ [śarma: yasyās < yasyām]
children.translated_text: whose width is five cubits, length eight cubits, and height three cubits.

children.text: tasyām citau kim phalam iṣṭakānām saṃkhyā ca kā @brūhi kati starās ca// [śarma: kim < kā]
children.translated_text: In that stack, what is the volume, what is the count of bricks, and how many layers are there? Tell me!

children.text: nyāsas/ [fig.38] iṣṭakā-citis/ iṣṭakāyās ghana-hasta-mānam 3_64/ cites kṣetra-phalam 40/ ucchrayeṇa guṇitam cites ghana-phalam 120/ labdhā iṣṭakā-saṃkhyā 2560/ stara-saṃkhyā 24/ evam pāṣāṇa-citau api// iti citi-vyavahāras//
children.translated_text: Setting down: [fig. 38] Brick stack/ The cubic-cubit measure of a brick is 3/64/ The field-area of the stack is 40/ multiplied by the height, the cubic volume of the stack is 120/ The obtained brick-count is 2560/ The layer-count is 24/ Similarly for a stone stack also// Thus [ends] the section on stacking//

body.text: krakaca-vyavahāra
body.translated_text: Section on Sawing

body.text: atha krakaca-vyavahāre karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Now in the section on sawing (<s>krakaca-vyavahāra</s>), the rule of operation in a verse:

children.text: piṇḍa-yoga-#dalam agra-mūlayos dairghya-saṃguṇitam aṅgula-ātmakam/
children.translated_text: Half the sum of the girths at the tip and base, multiplied by the length, in <s>aṅgula</s>s (finger-widths),

children.text: dāru-dāraṇa-pathais samāhatam %ṣaṣ-#svara-#iṣu-vihṛtam kara-ātmakam// [āpaṭe: ṣaṣ-stareṣu vihṛtam]
children.translated_text: multiplied by the number of cuts through the timber, and divided by 576, gives the result in cubits.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: mūle #nakha-aṅgula-mitas atha #nṛpa-aṅgulas agre piṇḍas %śata-aṅgula-mitam kila yasya dairghyam/
children.translated_text: A timber whose girth at the base measures twenty <s>aṅgula</s>s and at the tip sixteen <s>aṅgula</s>s, and whose length measures one hundred <s>aṅgula</s>s,

children.text: tad-dāru-dāraṇa-patheṣu %caturṣu kim @syāt hasta-ātmakam @vada sakhe gaṇitam drutam me//
children.translated_text: in four cuts through that timber, what will be the result in cubits? Tell me quickly, O friend!

body.text: nyāsas/ [fig.39] piṇḍa-yoga-#dalam 18[/] dairghyeṇa 100 saṃguṇitam 1800/ dāru-dāraṇa-pathais 4 guṇitam 7200/ %ṣaṣ-#svara-#iṣu-576-vihṛtam jātam kara-ātmakam gaṇitam 25_2// krakaca-antare karaṇa-sūtram sa-%ardha-vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: [fig. 39] Half the sum of the girths: 18/ multiplied by the length 100, giving 1800/ multiplied by the number of cuts 4, giving 7200/ divided by 576, the obtained result in cubits is 25/2// For a different [type of] sawing, the rule of operation in one and a half verses:

children.text: @chidyate tu yadi tiryak ukta-vat piṇḍa-vistṛti-hates phalam tadā/ [śarma:-hṛtes < -hates]
children.translated_text: But if the cutting is transverse, then the result is as stated, from the product of the girth and the width.

children.text: iṣṭakā-citi-dṛṣad-citi-khāta-krākaca-vyavahṛtau khalu mūlyam/
children.translated_text: In the operations of brick-stacking, stone-stacking, excavation, and sawing, the cost indeed

children.text: karma-kāra-jana-saṃpratipattyā tad-mṛdutva-kaṭhinatva-vaśena//
children.translated_text: [depends] on the agreement with the workers, and on the softness or hardness [of the material].

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: yad-vistṛtis #danta-mitā aṅgulāni piṇḍas tathā %ṣoḍaśa yatra kāṣṭhe/
children.translated_text: A timber whose width measures thirty-two <s>aṅgula</s>s and whose girth is likewise sixteen,

children.text: chedeṣu tiryak %navasu @pracakṣva kim @syāt phalam tatra kara-ātmakam me//
children.translated_text: in nine transverse cuts, tell me what the result in cubits would be there!

children.text: nyāsas/ [fig.40] vistāras 32/ piṇḍas 16/ piṇḍa-vistṛti-hatis 512/ dāru-dāraṇa-mārga-9-ghnī 4608/ %ṣaṣ-#svara-#iṣu-576-vihṛtā jātam phalam hastās 8// iti krakaca-vyavahāras//
children.translated_text: Setting down: [fig. 40] width 32/ girth 16/ the product of girth and width 512/ multiplied by the number of cuts 9, giving 4608/ divided by 576, the obtained result in cubits is 8// Thus [ends] the section on sawing//

body.text: rāśi-vyavahāra
body.translated_text: Section on Heaps

body.text: atha rāśi-vyavahāre karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Now in the section on heaps (<s>rāśi-vyavahāra</s>), the rule of operation in a verse:

children.text: anaṇuṣu %daśama-aṃśas aṇuṣu atha %ekādaśa-aṃśas paridhi-%navama-bhāgas śūki-dhānyeṣu vedhas/ [śarma: śūka- < śūki-]
children.translated_text: For non-fine grains, one-tenth [of the circumference is the height]; for fine grains, one-eleventh; for husked grains, one-ninth of the circumference is the height. [śarma: śūka- < śūki-]

children.text: @bhavati paridhi-%ṣaṣṭhe vargite vedha-nighne ghana-gaṇita-karās @syus māgadhās tās ca khāryas//
children.translated_text: When one-sixth of the circumference is squared and multiplied by the height, the result gives the cubic <s>hastas</s> (cubits) in <s>Māgadha</s> measure; and those are the <s>khārīs</s> (grain-measures).

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: sama-bhuvi kila rāśis yas sthitas sthūla-dhānya-paridhi-parimitis @syāt hasta-%ṣaṣṭis yadīyā/ [śarma:-dhānyas < -dhānya-, vai < syāt]
children.translated_text: If a heap of coarse grain standing on level ground has a circumference measuring sixty <s>hastas</s> (cubits), [śarma: -dhānyas < -dhānya-, vai < syāt]

children.text: @pravada gaṇaka khāryas kim-mitās @santi tasmin atha pṛthak aṇu-dhānyais śūka-dhānyais ca śīghram// [śarma: aṇu-dhānye śūki-dhānye ca]
children.translated_text: tell me, O mathematician, how many <s>khārīs</s> are there in it? And separately for fine grains and husked grains, quickly! [śarma: aṇu-dhānye śūki-dhānye ca]

body.text: atha sthūla-dhānya-rāśi-māna-avabodhanāya nyāsas/ [fig.41] paridhis 60/ vedhas 6/ paridhes %ṣaṣṭha-aṃśas 10/ vargitas 100/ vedha-6-nighnas/ labdhās khāryas 600// atha aṇu-dhānya-rāśi-māna-ānayanāya nyāsas/ [fig.42] paridhis 60/ vedhas 60_11/ jātam phalam 545_5_11// atha śūka-dhānya-rāśi-māna-ānayanāya nyāsas/ [fig.43] paridhis 60/ vedhas 20_3/ khāryas 666_2_3// atha bhitti-antar-bāhya-koṇa-saṃlagna-rāśi-pramāṇa-ānayana-karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Now, for understanding the measure of the coarse-grain heap, the setting-out: [fig.41] circumference 60; height 6; one-sixth of the circumference is 10; squared, 100; multiplied by height 6; the <s>khārīs</s> obtained are 600. Now, for determining the measure of the fine-grain heap, the setting-out: [fig.42] circumference 60; height 60/11; the result obtained is 545 5/11. Now, for determining the measure of the husked-grain heap, the setting-out: [fig.43] circumference 60; height 20/3; <s>khārīs</s> 666 2/3. Now, the verse-rule for determining the measure of a heap resting against a wall, in a corner, or on an outer corner:

children.text: %dvi-#veda-sa-%tri-bhāga-%eka-nighnāt tu paridhes phalam/
children.translated_text: From the circumference multiplied by two, or with one-third added, or by one,

children.text: bhitti-antar-bāhya-koṇa-stha-rāśes sva-guṇa-bhājitam// [śarma: -antar-koṇa-bāhya-stha-]
children.translated_text: the result for a heap against a wall, in an inner corner, or on an outer corner is obtained by dividing by its own multiplier. [śarma: -antar-koṇa-bāhya-stha-]

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: paridhis bhitti-lagnasya rāśes %triṃśat-karas kila/
children.translated_text: The circumference of a heap resting against a wall is thirty <s>hastas</s> (cubits),

children.text: antar-koṇa-sthitasya api #tithi-tulya-karas sakhe//
children.translated_text: and that of one standing in an inner corner is equal to fifteen, O friend,

children.text: bahir-koṇa-sthitasya api %pañca-ghna-%nava-saṃmitas/
children.translated_text: and that of one standing on an outer corner measures five times nine (i.e., forty-five);

children.text: teṣām @ācakṣva me kṣipram ghana-hastān pṛthak pṛthak//
children.translated_text: tell me quickly the cubic <s>hastas</s> of each of them separately.

body.text: atra api sthūla-ādi-dhānyānām rāśi-māna-avabodhanāya spaṣṭam kṣetra-%trayam/ tatra ādau anaṇu-dhānya-rāśi-māna-bodhakam kṣetram/ nyāsas/ [fig.44] atra ādyasya paridhis 30 %dvi-nighnas 60/ anyas 15 %catur-ghnas 60/ aparas 45 sa-%tri-bhāga-%eka-4_3-nighnas 60/ eṣām vedhas 6 ebhyas phalam tulyam etāvantyas eva khāryas 600/ etat sva-sva-guṇena bhaktam jātam pṛthak pṛthak phalam 300/ 150/ 450// atha aṇu-dhānya-rāśi-māna-ānayanāya nyāsas/ [fig.45] pūrva-vat kṣetra-%trayāṇām sva-guṇa-guṇita-paridhis 60/ vedhas 60_11/ phalāni 272_8_11/ 136_4_1/ 409_1_11// atha śūki-dhānya-rāśi-māna-ānayanāya nyāsas/ [fig.46] atra api pūrva-vat kṣetra-%trayāṇām sva-guṇa-guṇitas paridhis 60/ vedhas 20_3/ phalāni 333_1_3/ 166_2_3/ 500// iti rāśi-vyavahāras samāptas//
body.translated_text: Here too, for understanding the measure of heaps of coarse and other grains, three diagrams are given clearly. Among them, first the diagram illustrating the measure of a coarse-grain heap. Setting-out: [fig.44] Here, the circumference of the first is 30, multiplied by two gives 60; of the second, 15 multiplied by four gives 60; of the third, 45 multiplied by one-and-one-third (4/3) gives 60. Their height is 6; from these the result is the same, namely 600 <s>khārīs</s>. This, divided by the respective multiplier, gives the separate results: 300, 150, 450. Now, for determining the measure of a fine-grain heap, the setting-out: [fig.45] As before, for the three diagrams the circumference multiplied by the respective multiplier is 60; height 60/11; the results are 272 8/11, 136 4/11, 409 1/11. Now, for determining the measure of a husked-grain heap, the setting-out: [fig.46] Here too, as before, for the three diagrams the circumference multiplied by the respective multiplier is 60; height 20/3; the results are 333 1/3, 166 2/3, 500. Thus the section on heap-measurement (<s>rāśi-vyavahāra</s>) is concluded.

body.text: chāyā-vyavahāra
body.translated_text: Shadow Problems (<s>chāyā-vyavahāra</s>)

body.text: atha chāyā-vyavahāre karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Now, the verse-rule in shadow problems:

children.text: chāyayos karṇayos antare ye tayos varga-viśleṣa-bhaktās #rasa-#adri-#iṣavas/
children.translated_text: The differences of the two shadows and the two hypotenuses -- 576 divided by the difference of their squares,

children.text: sa-%eka-labdhes pada-ghnam tu karṇa-antaram bhā-antareṇa ūna-yuktam #dale @stas prabhe// [śarma: stambha-bhe < stas prabhe]
children.translated_text: the square root of the quotient plus one, multiplied by the difference of the hypotenuses, increased or decreased by the difference of the shadows, halved, gives the two shadows. [śarma: stambha-bhe < stas prabhe]

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: #nanda-#candrais mitam chāyayos antaram karṇayos antaram #viśva-tulyam yayos/
children.translated_text: The difference of the two shadows measures 19, and the difference of the two hypotenuses equals 13;

children.text: te prabhe @vakti yas yuktimān @vetti asau vyaktam avyakta-yuktam hi @manye akhilam// [śarma: yukti-mārgeṇa me < yuktimān vetti asau, avyaktam uktam < avyakta-yuktam]
children.translated_text: he who states those two shadows and knows them through reasoning, he truly understands all that is known through the unknown (algebra). [śarma: yukti-mārgeṇa me < yuktimān vetti asau, avyaktam uktam < avyakta-yuktam]

body.text: chāyā-antaram 19/ karṇa-antaram 13/ anayos varga-antareṇa 192 bhaktās #rasa-#adri-#iṣavas 576 labdham 3/ sa-%ekasya asya 4 mūlam 2/ anena karṇa-antaram 13 guṇitam 26 %dvi-stham 26/ 26 bhā-antareṇa 19 ūna-yute 7/ 45/ tad-%ardhe labdhe chāye 7_2/ 45_2/ tad-kṛtyos yoga-padam iti-ādinā jātau karṇau 25_2/ 51_2[//] chāyā-antare karaṇa-sūtram vṛtta-%ardham/
body.translated_text: Difference of shadows 19; difference of hypotenuses 13; 576 divided by the difference of their squares 192 gives quotient 3; the square root of this plus one, i.e. of 4, is 2; multiplied by the difference of hypotenuses 13 gives 26, halved gives 26; 26 increased and decreased by the shadow-difference 19 gives 7 and 45; halved, the two shadows obtained are 7/2 and 45/2; the square root of the sum of their squares, etc., gives the two hypotenuses 25/2 and 51/2. Half a verse as the rule for the shadow-difference:

children.text: śaṅkus pradīpa-tala-śaṅku-tala-antara-ghnas chāyā @bhavet vi-nara-dīpa-śikha-auccya-bhaktas// [śarma: -aucca-]
children.translated_text: The <s>śaṅku</s> (gnomon) multiplied by the distance between the base of the lamp and the base of the gnomon, divided by the height of the lamp-flame minus the man (gnomon), gives the shadow. [śarma: -aucca-]

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: śaṅku-pradīpa-antara-bhūs %tri-hastā dīpa-ucchritis sa-%ardha-kara-%trayā ced/
children.translated_text: If the ground-distance between the gnomon and the lamp is three <s>hastas</s> (cubits), and the height of the lamp is three and a half cubits,

children.text: śaṅkos tadā #arka-aṅgula-saṃmitasya tasya prabhā @syāt kiyatī @vada āśu//
children.translated_text: then what would be the shadow of the gnomon measuring twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> (finger-breadths)? Tell me quickly.

body.text: nyāsas/ [fig.48] śaṅkus 1_2/ pradīpa-śaṅku-tala-antaram 3/ anayos ghātas 3_2/ vi-nara-dīpa-śikha-aucyena 3 bhaktas labdhāni chāyā-aṅgulāni 12// atha dīpa-ucchriti-ānayanāya karaṇa-sūtram vṛtta-%ardham/
body.translated_text: Setting-out: [fig.48] gnomon 1/2 [hasta]; distance between lamp-base and gnomon-base 3; their product 3/2; divided by the height of the lamp-flame minus the man, i.e., 3, the shadow-<s>aṅgulas</s> (finger-breadths) obtained are 12. Now, half a verse as the rule for finding the height of the lamp:

body.text: chāyā-hṛte tu nara-dīpa-tala-antara-ghne śaṅkau @bhavet nara-yute khalu dīpaka-aucyam// [śarma: -uddhṛte < hṛte, -auccam < -aucyam]
body.translated_text: The gnomon multiplied by the distance between the man (gnomon) and the lamp-base, divided by the shadow, increased by the man (gnomon), gives the height of the lamp. [śarma: -uddhṛte < hṛte, -auccam < -aucyam]

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: pradīpa-śaṅku-antara-bhūs %tri-hastā chāyā-aṅgulais %ṣoḍaśabhis samā ced/
children.translated_text: If the ground-distance between the lamp and the gnomon is three <s>hastas</s> (cubits), and the shadow equals sixteen <s>aṅgulas</s> (finger-breadths),

children.text: dīpa-ucchritis @syāt kiyatī @vada āśu pradīpa-śaṅku-antaram @ucyatām me// [śarma: tathā ābhyām < vada āśu]
children.translated_text: what would be the height of the lamp? Tell me quickly, and also state the distance between the lamp and the gnomon. [śarma: tathā ābhyām < vada āśu]

body.text: nyāsas/ [fig.49] śaṅkus 12/ chāyā-aṅgulāni 16/ śaṅku-pradīpa-antara-hastās 3/ labdham dīpaka-auccyam hastās 11_4// pradīpa-śaṅku-antara-bhū-māna-ānayanāya karaṇa-sūtram vṛtta-%ardham/
body.translated_text: Setting-out: [fig.49] gnomon 12; shadow-<s>aṅgulas</s> 16; distance between gnomon and lamp in <s>hastas</s> 3; the height of the lamp obtained is 11/4 <s>hastas</s>. Half a verse as the rule for finding the ground-distance between lamp and gnomon:

body.text: vi-śaṅku-dīpa-ucchraya-saṃguṇā bhā śaṅku-uddhṛtā dīpa-nara-antaram @syāt//
body.translated_text: The shadow multiplied by the height of the lamp minus the gnomon, divided by the gnomon, gives the distance between the lamp and the man (gnomon).

body.text: udāharaṇam/ pūrva-uktas eva dīpa-ucchrāyas 11_4/ [śarma: pūrva-uktam eva/] śaṅku-aṅgulāni 12 chāyā 16/ labdhās śaṅku-pradīpa-antara-hastās 3// chāyā-pradīpa-antara-dīpa-auccya-ānayanāya karaṇa-sūtram sa-%ardha-vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Example: the height of the lamp as stated before is 11/4. [śarma: pūrva-uktam eva/] Gnomon-<s>aṅgulas</s> 12; shadow 16; the distance between gnomon and lamp in <s>hastas</s> obtained is 3. The rule in one and a half verses for finding the shadow, the distance to the lamp, and the height of the lamp:

children.text: chāyā-agrayos antara-saṃguṇā bhā chāyā-pramāṇa-antara-hṛt @bhavet bhūs/
children.translated_text: The shadow multiplied by the distance between the tips of the two shadows, divided by the difference of the shadow-lengths, gives the ground-distance;

children.text: bhū-śaṅku-ghātas prabhayā vibhaktas @prajāyate dīpa-śikha-auccyam evam/
children.translated_text: the ground-distance multiplied by the gnomon, divided by the shadow, gives the height of the lamp-flame; thus,

children.text: trairāśikena eva yat etat uktam vyāptam sva-bhedais hariṇā iva viśvam//
children.translated_text: what has been stated here through the Rule of Three alone pervades all its varieties, just as <s>Hari</s> (Viṣṇu) pervades the universe through His own manifestations.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: śaṅkos bhā #arka-mita-aṅgulasya su-mate dṛṣṭā kila %aṣṭa-aṅgulā chāyā-agra-abhimukhe kara-%dvaya-mite nyastasya deśe punar/
children.translated_text: The shadow of a gnomon measuring twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> (finger-breadths) is observed to be eight <s>aṅgulas</s>; when it is placed again in a spot two cubits closer toward the tip of the shadow,

children.text: tasya eva #arka-mita-aṅgulā yadi tadā chāyā-pradīpa-antaram dīpa-auccyam ca kiyat @vada vyavahṛtim chāyā-abhidhām @vetsi cet//
children.translated_text: if its shadow is twelve <s>aṅgulas</s>, then what is the distance to the lamp and what is the height of the lamp? Tell me, if you know the procedure called shadow-problems.

body.text: nyāsas/ [fig.50] atra chāyā-agrayos antaram aṅgula-ātmakam 52/ chāye ca 8/ 12/ anayos ādyā 8/ iyam anena 52 guṇitā 416 chāyā-pramāṇa-antareṇa 4 bhaktā labdham bhū-mānam 104/ idam %prathama-chāyā-agra-dīpa-talayos antaram iti arthas/ evam %dvitīya-chāyā-agra-bhū-mānam 156/ bhū-śaṅku-ghātas prabhayā vibhaktas iti jātam ubhaya-tas api dīpa-auccyam samam eva hastās 6_1_2/ evam iti atra chāyā-vyavahāre trairāśika-kalpanayā ānayanam @vartate tat yathā/ %prathama-chāyātas 8 %dvitīya-chāyā 12 yāvatā adhikā tāvatā chāyā-avayavena yadi chāyā-agra-antara-tulyā bhūs @labhyate tadā %prathama-chāyayā kim iti/ evam pṛthak pṛthak chāyā-pradīpa-tala-antara-pramāṇam @labhyate/ tatas %dvitīyam trairāśikam/ yadi chāyā-tulye bhuje śaṅkus koṭis tadā bhū-tulye bhuje kim iti/ labdham dīpaka-auccyam ubhayatas api tulyam eva/ evam pañcarāśika-ādikam akhilam trairāśika-kalpanayā eva siddham/ yathā bhagavatā śrī-nārāyaṇena janana-maraṇa-kleśa-apahāriṇā nikhila-jagat-janana-%eka-bījena sakala-bhuvana-bhāvanena giri-sarit-sura-nara-asura-ādibhis sva-bhedais idam jagat vyāptam tathā idam akhilam gaṇita-jātam trairāśikena vyāptam// yadi evam tad-bahubhis kim iti āśaṅkyā āha/
body.translated_text: Setting-out: [fig.50] Here the distance between the tips of the two shadows in <s>aṅgulas</s> is 52; and the two shadows are 8 and 12; of these, the first 8, multiplied by 52 gives 416, divided by the difference of shadow-lengths 4, gives the ground-distance 104; this means the distance between the tip of the first shadow and the base of the lamp. Similarly the ground-distance from the second shadow-tip is 156. The ground-distance multiplied by the gnomon, divided by the shadow -- thus the height of the lamp obtained from both is the same, namely 6 1/2 <s>hastas</s>. 'Thus' here means that in shadow-problems the derivation proceeds by the Rule of Three reasoning, as follows: by how much the second shadow 12 exceeds the first shadow 8, if by that shadow-increment the ground equal to the distance between the shadow-tips is obtained, then what is obtained from the first shadow? Thus the distance from each shadow to the lamp-base is obtained separately. Then the second Rule of Three: if the shadow-length is the base and the gnomon is the perpendicular, then what is the perpendicular when the base equals the ground-distance? The height of the lamp obtained from both is the same. Thus the Rule of Five and all others are established through the Rule of Three reasoning alone. Just as the blessed <s>Śrī Nārāyaṇa</s>, the remover of the afflictions of birth and death, the sole seed of the creation of the entire world, the sustainer of all realms, pervades this universe through His own manifestations as mountains, rivers, gods, men, demons, and so forth, so too this entire science of computation is pervaded by the Rule of Three.

children.text: yat kiṃcit guṇa-bhāga-hāra-vidhinā bīje atra vā @gaṇyate tat trairāśikam eva nirmala-dhiyām eva avagamyam vidām/ [śarma: avagamyā bhidā]
children.translated_text: Whatever is computed here by the method of multiplication, division, and reduction, or in algebra (<s>bīja</s>), is all just the Rule of Three, comprehensible only to those of clear intellect among the learned. [śarma: avagamyā bhidā]

children.text: etat yat bahudhā asmad-ādi-jaḍa-dhī-dhī-vṛddhi-buddhyā budhais tad-bhedān su-gamān @vidhāya racitam prājñais prakīrṇa-ādikam// [śarma: -buddhi-pravṛddhyai < -vṛddhi-buddhyā, -bheda-anugamān < -bhedān sugamān]
children.translated_text: That which the wise have composed in many forms -- such as miscellaneous problems (<s>prakīrṇa</s>) and the rest -- arranging its varieties in accessible manner, is done to nurture the intellect of dull minds such as ours. [śarma: -buddhi-pravṛddhyai < -vṛddhi-buddhyā, -bheda-anugamān < -bhedān sugamān]

children.text: iti śrī-bhāskara-ācārya-viracitāyām līlāvatyām chāyā-adhikāras samāptim @agāt//
children.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Līlāvatī</s> composed by the illustrious teacher <s>Bhāskara</s>, the chapter on shadows (<s>chāyā-adhikāra</s>) is concluded.

body.text: kuṭṭaka
body.translated_text: The Pulverizer (<s>Kuṭṭaka</s>)

body.text: atha kuṭṭake karaṇa-sūtram vṛtta-%pañcakam/
body.translated_text: Now, the rule in five verses for the <s>kuṭṭaka</s> (pulverizer):

children.text: bhājyas hāras kṣepakas ca apavartyas kena api ādau saṃbhave kuṭṭaka-%artham/
children.translated_text: The dividend (<s>bhājya</s>), the divisor (<s>hāra</s>), and the addend (<s>kṣepaka</s>) should first be reduced by whatever common factor is possible, for the purpose of the <s>kuṭṭaka</s>;

children.text: yena chinnau bhājya-hārau na tena kṣepas ca etat duṣṭam uddiṣṭam eva//
children.translated_text: if the factor by which the dividend and divisor are divided does not also divide the addend, then the problem as stated is ill-posed.

children.text: parasparam bhājitayos yayos yas śeṣas tayos @syāt apavartanam sas/
children.translated_text: The remainder that results from mutually dividing the two (dividend and divisor) is their greatest common divisor (<s>apavartana</s>);

children.text: tena apavartena vibhājitau yau tau bhājya-hārau dṛḍha-saṃjñitau @stas//
children.translated_text: the dividend and divisor divided by that common factor are called 'reduced' (<s>dṛḍha</s>).

children.text: mithas @bhajet tau dṛḍha-bhājya-hārau yāvat vibhājye @bhavati iha #rūpam/
children.translated_text: One should mutually divide the reduced dividend and divisor until the remainder in the dividend becomes unity;

children.text: phalāni adhas adhas tad-adhas niveśyas kṣepas tatas śūnyam upāntimena//
children.translated_text: the quotients are placed one below the other, below them the addend, and then zero; then by the penultimate,

children.text: sva-ūrdhve hate antyena yute tad-antyam @tyajet muhus @syāt iti rāśi-#yugmam/
children.translated_text: each upper term is multiplied by the one below and increased by the last -- one should discard that last term repeatedly until a pair of quantities remains;

children.text: ūrdhvas vibhājyena dṛḍhena taṣṭas phalam guṇas @syāt adharas hareṇa//
children.translated_text: the upper one, reduced modulo the reduced dividend, gives the quotient (<s>labdhi</s>); the lower one, reduced modulo the divisor, gives the multiplier (<s>guṇa</s>).

children.text: evam tadā eva atra yadā samās tās @syus labdhayas ced viṣamās tadānīm/
children.translated_text: This is the case when the number of quotients is even; but if they are odd, then

children.text: yathā āgatau labdhi-guṇau viśodhyau sva-takṣaṇāt śeṣa-mitau tu tau @stas//
children.translated_text: the quotient and multiplier as obtained should be subtracted from their respective reduced values; the remainders are then the true values.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: %ekaviṃśati-yutam %śata-%dvayam yad-guṇam gaṇaka %pañcaṣaṣṭi-yuk/
children.translated_text: Two hundred and twenty-one multiplied by some number and increased by sixty-five,

children.text: %pañca-varjita-%śata-%dvaya-uddhṛtam śuddhim @eti guṇakam @vada āśu tam//
children.translated_text: when divided by one hundred and ninety-five, leaves no remainder -- tell me that multiplier quickly.

body.text: nyāsas/ bhājyas 221/ hāras 195/ kṣepas 65/ atra paraspara-bhājitayos bhājya-221-bhājakayos 195 śeṣam 13/ anena bhājya-hāra-kṣepās apavartitās jātas bhājyas 17/ [āpaṭe: apavarttitās] hāras 15/ kṣepas 5/ anayos dṛḍha-bhājya-hārayos paraspara-bhaktayos labdhāni adhas adhas tad-adhas kṣepas tad-adhas #śūnyam niveśyam iti nyaste jātā vallī {btabular} 1 \\ 7 \\ 5 \\ 0 {etabular} upāntimena sva-ūrdhve hate iti-ādi-karaṇena jātam rāśi-%dvayam {btabular} 40 \\ 35 {etabular} etau dṛḍha-bhājya-hārābhyām {btabular} 17 \\ 15 {etabular} taṣṭau labdhi-guṇau jātau 6/ 5/ iṣṭa-āhata-sva-sva-hareṇa yukte iti vakṣyamāṇa-vidhinā etau iṣṭa-guṇita-sva-takṣaṇa-yuktau vā labdhi-guṇau 23/ 20/ %dvikena iṣṭena vā 40/ 35/ iti-ādi// kuṭṭaka-antare karana-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Setting-out: dividend 221; divisor 195; addend 65. Here the remainder from mutually dividing the dividend 221 and divisor 195 is 13; by this, the dividend, divisor, and addend are reduced, giving: dividend 17, [āpaṭe: apavarttitās] divisor 15, addend 5. Mutually dividing these reduced dividend and divisor, the quotients are placed one below the other, below them the addend, and below that zero, giving the column: {btabular} 1 \\ 7 \\ 5 \\ 0 {etabular}. By the procedure 'the penultimate multiplied by the one above it' etc., the pair of quantities obtained is {btabular} 40 \\ 35 {etabular}. These, reduced modulo the reduced dividend and divisor {btabular} 17 \\ 15 {etabular}, give the quotient and multiplier: 6 and 5. By the rule to be stated 'increased by the product of an arbitrary number and its own divisor,' these, with an optional multiple of their respective moduli added, give quotient and multiplier 23 and 20; or with optional multiplier two, 40 and 35; and so on. The verse-rule for another form of the <s>kuṭṭaka</s>:

children.text: @bhavati kuṭṭa-vidher yuti-bhājyayos samapavartitayos api vā guṇas/
children.translated_text: The multiplier that arises from the <s>kuṭṭaka</s> procedure applied to the sum and the dividend after they have been reduced by a common factor,

children.text: @bhavati yas yuti-bhājakayos punar sas ca @bhavet apavartana-saṃguṇas//
children.translated_text: that same multiplier, when applied to the sum and the divisor, becomes the multiplier times the common factor.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: %śatam hatam yena yutam %navatyā vivarjitam vā vihṛtam %triṣaṣṭyā/
children.translated_text: A hundred multiplied by some number, when increased by ninety or decreased [by it], and divided by sixty-three,

children.text: nis-agrakam @syāt @vada me guṇam tam spaṣṭam paṭīyān yadi kuṭṭake @asi//
children.translated_text: leaves no remainder -- tell me that multiplier clearly, if you are skilled in the <s>kuṭṭaka</s> (pulverizer).

body.text: nyāsas/ bhājyas 100/ hāras 63/ kṣepas 90/ jātā pūrva-vat labdhi-kṣepāṇām vallī {btabular} 1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 2 \\ 2 \\ 1 \\ 90 \\ 0 {etabular} upāntimena sva-ūrdhve hate antyena yute iti-ādi-karaṇena jātam rāśi-%dvayam {btabular} 2430 \\ 1530 {etabular} jātau pūrva-vat labdhi-guṇau 30/ 18/ atha vā bhājya-kṣepau %daśabhis @apavartya bhājyas 10/ kṣepas 9/ paraspara-bhajanāt labdhāni phalāni kṣepam #śūnyam ca adhas adhas @niveśya jātā vallī {btabular} 0 \\ 6 \\ 3 \\ 9 \\ 0 {etabular} pūrva-vat labdhas guṇas 45/ atra labdhis na grāhyā/ yatas labdhayas viṣamās jātās/ atas guṇe 45 sva-takṣaṇāt asmāt 63 viśodhite jātas guṇas sas eva 18/ guṇa-ghna-bhājye kṣepa-90-yute hara-63-taṣṭe labdhis ca 30// atha vā hāra-kṣepau 63/ 90/ %navabhis apavartitau jātau hāra-kṣepau 7/ 10/ atra labdhi-kṣepāṇām vallī {btabular} 14 \\ 3 \\ 10 \\ 0 {etabular} labdhas guṇas 2/ kṣepa-hāra-apavartana-9-guṇitas jātas sas eva guṇas 18/ bhājya-100-bhājaka-63-kṣepebhyas 90 labdhis ca 30// atha vā bhājya-kṣepau punar hāra-kṣepau ca apavartitau jātau bhājya-hārau 10/ 7/ kṣepas 1/ atra pūrva-vat jātā vallī {btabular} 1 \\ 2 \\ 1 \\ 0 {etabular} guṇas ca 2/ hāra-kṣepa-apavartanena guṇitas jātas sas eva guṇas 18/ pūrva-vat labdhis ca 30/ iṣṭa-āhata-sva-sva-hareṇa yukte iti-ādinā atha vā guṇa-labdhī 81/ 130/ iti-ādi// kuṭṭaka-antare karaṇa-sūtram vṛtta-%ardham/
body.translated_text: Setting down: dividend 100, divisor 63, addend 90. As before, the <s>vallī</s> (chain) of quotients and addends is obtained: {1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 1, 90, 0}. By the procedure 'the penultimate multiplied by the one above it and increased by the last' and so on, the pair of quantities obtained is {2430, 1530}. The quotient and multiplier obtained as before are 30 and 18. Alternatively, reducing the dividend and addend by ten, the dividend becomes 10 and the addend 9. By mutual division, the quotients obtained, with the addend and zero placed below, give the chain: {0, 6, 3, 9, 0}. As before, the multiplier obtained is 45. Here the quotient should not be taken, since the quotients are odd [in number]. Therefore, subtracting the multiplier 45 from its own divisor 63, the multiplier is that same 18. When the dividend is multiplied by the multiplier and increased by the addend 90 and divided by the divisor 63, the quotient is also 30. Alternatively, reducing the divisor and addend 63 and 90 by nine, the reduced divisor and addend are 7 and 10. Here the chain of quotients and addends is: {14, 3, 10, 0}. The multiplier obtained is 2; multiplied by the divisor-addend reduction factor 9, it becomes that same multiplier 18. From dividend 100, divisor 63, and addend 90, the quotient is also 30. Alternatively, reducing the dividend-addend and again the divisor-addend, the reduced dividend and divisor are 10 and 7, the addend is 1. Here the chain is obtained as before: {1, 2, 1, 0}. And the multiplier is 2; multiplied by the divisor-addend reduction, it becomes that same multiplier 18. As before, the quotient is also 30. By 'multiplied by the desired number and increased by its own divisor' and so on, alternatively the multiplier and quotient are 81 and 130, and so on. The rule of operation for another type of <s>kuṭṭaka</s> (pulverizer), in half a verse:

body.text: yoga-je takṣaṇāt śuddhe guṇa-āptī @stas viyoga-je//
body.translated_text: When [the addend] is produced by addition, [the results] subtracted from their own divisors [give] the multiplier and quotient; when produced by subtraction, [they stand as obtained].

body.text: atra pūrva-udāharaṇe %navati-kṣepe yau labdhi-guṇau jātau 30/ 18/ etau sva-takṣaṇābhyām ābhyām 100/ 63 śodhitau ye śeṣake tad-mitau labdhi-ṅuṇau %navati-śodhite jñātavyau 70/ 45/ etayos api iṣṭa-āhata-sva-sva-takṣaṇam kṣepas iti labdhi-guṇau 170/ 108/ atha vā 270/ 171 iti-ādi// %dvitīya-udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Here, in the previous example, when the addend is ninety, the quotient and multiplier obtained were 30 and 18. These, subtracted from their own divisors 100 and 63, give the quotient and multiplier for when ninety is subtracted, namely 70 and 45. For these too, by 'multiplied by the desired number and increased by its own divisor,' the quotient and multiplier are 170 and 108, or alternatively 270 and 171, and so on. Second example:

children.text: yad-guṇā gaṇaka %ṣaṣṭis anvitā varjitā ca %daśabhis %ṣaṣ-uttarais/
children.translated_text: That number which, when multiplied by sixty, increased or decreased by sixteen,

children.text: @syāt %trayodaśa-hṛtā nis-agrakā tat guṇam @kathaya me pṛthak pṛthak//
children.translated_text: Becomes exactly divisible by thirteen — tell me that multiplier separately in each case.

body.text: nyāsas/ bhājyas 60 hāras 13 kṣepas 16/ prāk-vat jātā vallī {btabular} 4 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 16 \\ 0 {etabular} tathā jāte guṇa-āptī 2/ 8/ atra api labdhayas viṣamās/ atas guṇa-āptī sva-takṣaṇābhyām 13/ 60 śodhite jāte 11/ 52/ evam %ṣoḍaśa-kṣepe etau eva labdhi-guṇau 52/ 11/ [āpaṭe: etās < etau] sva-sva-harābhyām śodhitau jātau %ṣoḍaśa-viśuddhau 2/ 8// kuṭṭaka-antare karaṇa-sūtram sa-%ardha-vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: dividend 60, divisor 13, addend 16. As before, the chain is obtained: {4, 1, 1, 1, 1, 16, 0}. Thus the multiplier and quotient obtained are 2 and 8. Here too the quotients are odd. Therefore, the multiplier and quotient subtracted from their own divisors 13 and 60 are 11 and 52. Thus, when the addend is sixteen, these are the quotient and multiplier: 52 and 11. Subtracted from their own divisors, the results when sixteen is subtracted are 2 and 8. The rule of operation for another type of <s>kuṭṭaka</s>, in one and a half verses:

children.text: guṇa-labdhyos samam grāhyam dhī-matā takṣaṇe phalam/
children.translated_text: Of the multiplier and quotient, the wise should take the equal result at the divisor,

children.text: hara-taṣṭe dhana-kṣepe guṇa-labdhī tu pūrva-vat/
children.translated_text: When divided by the divisor with a positive addend, the multiplier and quotient are as before;

children.text: kṣepa-takṣaṇa-lābha-āḍhyā labdhis śuddhau tu varjitā//
children.translated_text: The quotient increased by the addend-divisor product [applies] to the subtracted case, and diminished [from the divisor] when purified.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: yena saṃguṇitās %pañca %trayoviṃśati-saṃyutās/
children.translated_text: That [number] which, multiplied by five and increased by twenty-three,

children.text: varjitās vā %tribhis bhaktās nis-agrās @syus sa kas guṇas//
children.translated_text: Or decreased [by twenty-three], when divided by three, leaves no remainder — what is that multiplier?

body.text: nyāsas/ bhājyas 5/ hāras 3/ kṣepas 23/ atra vallī {btabular} 46 \\ 23 {etabular} pūrva-vat jātam rāśi-%dvayam {btabular} 14 \\ 3 \\ 10 \\ 0 {etabular} etau bhājya-hārābhyām taṣṭau/ atra adhas-rāśau 23 %tribhis taṣṭe %sapta @labhyante/ ūrdhva-rāśau 46 %pañcabhis taṣṭe %nava @labhyante/ tatra %nava na grāhyās/ guṇa-labdhyos samam grāhyam dhī-matā takṣaṇe phalam iti/ atas %sapta eva grāhyās/ evam jāte guṇa-āptī 2/ 11/ kṣepa-je takṣaṇāt śuddhe iti %trayoviṃśati-śuddhau jātā viparīta-śodhanāt avaśiṣṭā labdhis 6/ [āpaṭe: -śuddhas < -śuddhau] śuddhau jāte 1/ 6/ iṣṭa-āhata-sva-sva-hareṇa yukte iti vakṣyamāṇa-vidhinā dhana-ṛṇayos antaram eva yogas iti bīja-uktyā ca/ iṣṭa-guṇita-sva-hāra-kṣepaṇena yathā dhana-labdhis @syāt iti tathā kṛte jāte guṇa-āptī 7/ 4/ evam sarvatra// atha vā hara-taṣṭe dhana-kṣepe iti/ nyāsas/ bhājyas 5/ hāras 3/ kṣepas 2/ pūrva-vat jāte guṇa-āptī 2/ 4 ete sva-sva-hārābhyām śodhite viśuddhi-je jāte 1/ 1/ kṣepa-takṣaṇa-lābha-āḍhyā labdhis iti jātau kṣepa-jau labdhi-guṇau 11/ 2/ śuddhau tu varjitā iti śuddhi-jau @bhavatas/ kintu atra śuddhā na @bhavati tasmāt viparīta-śodhanena ṛṇa-labdhis 6/ guṇas 1/ dhana-labdhi-artham %dvi-guṇe sva-hāre kṣipte sati jāte 7/ 4// kuṭṭaka-antare karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: dividend 5, divisor 3, addend 23. Here the chain is: {46, 23}. As before, the pair of quantities obtained is: {14, 3, 10, 0}. These divided by the dividend and divisor: in the lower quantity 23, divided by three, one obtains 7. In the upper quantity 46, divided by five, one obtains 9. There, 9 should not be taken — 'of the multiplier and quotient, the wise should take the equal result at the divisor.' Therefore 7 alone should be taken. Thus the multiplier and quotient obtained are 2 and 11. By 'when [the addend] is produced by addition, subtracted from the divisor,' the quotient remaining after subtracting twenty-three by reverse subtraction is 6. The purified [results] are 1 and 6. By 'multiplied by the desired number and increased by its own divisor' and by the seed-statement 'the difference of positive and negative is indeed the sum,' by adding the desired-multiple of its own divisor to the addend so as to make the quotient positive, the multiplier and quotient become 7 and 4. Thus in all cases. Alternatively, by 'when divided by the divisor with a positive addend': setting down: dividend 5, divisor 3, addend 2. As before the multiplier and quotient obtained are 2 and 4. These subtracted from their own divisors give the purification-results: 1 and 1. 'The quotient increased by the addend-divisor product' gives the addend-produced quotient and multiplier: 11 and 2. 'Diminished when purified': the purification does not occur here; therefore by reverse subtraction, the negative quotient is 6, multiplier 1. For the positive quotient, adding twice the divisor to the addend, the results are 7 and 4. The rule of operation for another type of <s>kuṭṭaka</s>, in a verse:

children.text: kṣepa-abhāvas atha vā kṣepas śuddhas hara-uddhṛtas/
children.translated_text: When the addend is absent, or when the addend is exactly divisible by the divisor,

children.text: jñeyas #śūnyam guṇas tatra kṣepas hāra-hṛtas phalam//
children.translated_text: The multiplier should be known as zero; the addend divided by the divisor is the result.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: yena %pañca-guṇitās #kha-saṃyutās %pañcaṣaṣṭi-sahitās ca te atha vā/
children.translated_text: That [number] which, multiplied by five, increased by zero, or increased by sixty-five,

children.text: @syus %trayodaśa-hṛtās nis-agrakās tam guṇam gaṇaka kīrtaya āśu me//
children.translated_text: Becomes exactly divisible by thirteen — tell me that multiplier quickly, O calculator!

body.text: nyāsas/ bhājyas 5/ hāras 13/ kṣepas 0/ jñeyas #śūnyam guṇas tatra kṣepas hāra-hṛtas phalam iti/ kṣepa-abhāve guṇa-āptī 0/ 0 iṣṭa-āhatā iti/ atha vā 13/ 5/ vā 26/ 10// nyāsas/ bhājyas 5/ hāras 13/ kṣepas 65/ kṣepas śuddhas hara-uddhṛtas/ jñeyas #śūnyam guṇas tatra kṣepas hāra-hṛtas phalam iti jāte guṇa-āptī 0/ 5/ vā 13/ 10/ atha vā 26/ 15/ iti-ādi// atha sarvatra kuṭṭake guṇa-labdhyos anekadhā-darśana-artham karaṇa-sūtram vṛtta-%ardham/
body.translated_text: Setting down: dividend 5, divisor 13, addend 0. 'The multiplier should be known as zero; the addend divided by the divisor is the result.' When the addend is absent, the multiplier and quotient are 0 and 0. Multiplied by the desired [number]: alternatively 13 and 5, or 26 and 10. Setting down: dividend 5, divisor 13, addend 65. 'When the addend is exactly divisible by the divisor, the multiplier should be known as zero; the addend divided by the divisor is the result.' The multiplier and quotient obtained are 0 and 5, or 13 and 10, or alternatively 26 and 15, and so on. Now, for showing multiple solutions of the multiplier and quotient in all <s>kuṭṭaka</s> cases, the rule of operation in half a verse:

body.text: iṣṭa-āhata-sva-sva-hareṇa yukte te vā @bhavetām bahudhā guṇa-āptī//
body.translated_text: Multiplied by a desired [number] and increased by their own divisors, they may become manifold — the multiplier and quotient.

body.text: asya udāharaṇāni darśitāni pūrvam iti/ atha sthira-kuṭṭake karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Examples of this have been shown previously. Now the rule of operation for the fixed <s>kuṭṭaka</s> (<s>sthira-kuṭṭaka</s>), in a verse:

children.text: kṣepe tu #rūpe yadi vā viśuddhe @syātām kramāt ye guṇa-kāra-labdhī/
children.translated_text: When the addend is unity, or when the addend is the [result of] purification, the multiplier and quotient obtained in order

children.text: abhīpsita-kṣepa-viśuddhi-nighne sva-hāra-taṣṭe @bhavatas tayos te//
children.translated_text: Are those [same values]; multiplied by the desired addend or purification, and reduced by their own divisors, they become those [desired values].

body.text: %prathama-udāharaṇe dṛḍha-bhājya-hārayos #rūpa-kṣepayos nyāsas/ bhājyas 17 hāras 15 kṣepas 1/ atra guṇa-āptī 7/ 8 ete tu iṣṭa-kṣepeṇa %pañcakena guṇite sva-hāra-taṣṭe ca jāte 5/ 6// atha #rūpa-śuddhau guṇa-āptī 7/ 8 takṣaṇāt śuddhau jātau labdhi-gunau 9/ 8/ ete %pañca-guṇe sva-hāra-taṣṭe ca jāte 10/ 11 evam sarvatra// asya graha-gaṇite upayogas tad-artham kim cit @ucyate/
body.translated_text: In the first example, for the fixed dividend and divisor with unity as addend, setting down: dividend 17, divisor 15, addend 1. Here the multiplier and quotient are 7 and 8. These, multiplied by the desired addend five and reduced by their own divisors, become 5 and 6. Now for the unity-purified [case], the multiplier and quotient 7 and 8, subtracted from the divisor, give the quotient and multiplier 9 and 8. These, multiplied by five and reduced by their own divisors, become 10 and 11. Thus in all cases. Its application in planetary computation — for that purpose, something is stated:

children.text: kalpyā atha śuddhis vikalā-avaśeṣas %ṣaṣṭis ca bhājyas ku-dināni hāras/
children.translated_text: One should assume the purification to be the remainder in arc-seconds; sixty is the dividend; the civil days are the divisor;

children.text: tad-jam phalam @syus vikalā guṇas tu liptā-agram asmāt ca kalā lava-agram/
children.translated_text: The result obtained will be the arc-seconds; and the multiplier is the arc-second remainder; from this, the arc-minutes [and] the degree remainder.

children.text: evam tad-ūrdhvam ca tathā adhimāsa-avama-agrakābhyām divasās ravi-indvos//
