children.translated_text: Similarly upward; and thus from the intercalary-month and omitted-day remainders, the days of the sun and moon.

body.text: grahasya vikalā-avaśeṣāt graha-ahargaṇayos ānayanam tat yathā/ tatra %ṣaṣṭis bhājyas/ ku-dināni hāras vikalā-avaśeṣam śuddhis iti @prakalpya sādhye guṇa-āptī/ tatra labdhis vikalās @syus/ guṇas tu kalā-avaśeṣam// evam kalā-avaśeṣam śuddhis tatra %ṣaṣṭis bhājyas ku-dināni hāras labdhis kalā guṇas bhāga-śeṣam// bhāga-śeṣam śuddhis/ %triṃśat bhājyas ku-dināni hāras phalam bhāgās/ [āpaṭe: bhāgā < bhāgās] guṇas rāśi-śeṣam// evam rāśi-śeṣam śuddhis %dvādaśa bhājyas ku-dināni hāras phalam gata-rāśayas guṇas bha-gaṇa-śeṣam// kalpa-bha-gaṇas bhājyas ku-dināni hāras bha-gaṇa-śeṣam śuddhis phalam gata-bha-gaṇas guṇas ahar-gaṇas @syāt iti// asya udāharaṇāni %tri-praśna-adhyāye// evam kalpa-adhimāsās bhājyas ravi-dināni hāras adhimāsa-śeṣam śuddhis/ phalam gata-adhimāsās guṇas gata-ravi-divasās// evam kalpa-avamāni bhājyas candra-divasās hāras/ avama-śeṣam śuddhis/ phalam gata-avamāni guṇas gata-cāndra-divasās iti// saṃśliṣṭa-kuṭṭake karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: The derivation of the day-count from the arc-second remainder of a planet — that is as follows. There, sixty is the dividend, civil days are the divisor, the arc-second remainder is the purification — thus establishing [the problem], the multiplier and quotient are to be found. There, the quotient will be the arc-seconds, and the multiplier is the arc-minute remainder. Similarly, the arc-minute remainder is the purification, sixty is the dividend, civil days are the divisor; the quotient is the arc-minutes, the multiplier is the degree remainder. The degree remainder is the purification, thirty is the dividend, civil days are the divisor; the result is the degrees, the multiplier is the sign remainder. Similarly, the sign remainder is the purification, twelve is the dividend, civil days are the divisor; the result is the elapsed signs, the multiplier is the revolution remainder. The <s>kalpa</s>-revolutions are the dividend, civil days are the divisor, the revolution remainder is the purification; the result is the elapsed revolutions, the multiplier will be the day-count. Examples of this are in the chapter on the three questions. Similarly, the <s>kalpa</s> intercalary months are the dividend, solar days are the divisor, the intercalary-month remainder is the purification; the result is the elapsed intercalary months, the multiplier is the elapsed solar days. Similarly, the <s>kalpa</s> omitted days are the dividend, lunar days are the divisor, the omitted-day remainder is the purification; the result is the elapsed omitted days, the multiplier is the elapsed lunar days. The rule of operation for the combined <s>kuṭṭaka</s> (<s>saṃśliṣṭa-kuṭṭaka</s>), in a verse:

children.text: %ekas haras ced guṇakau vibhinnau tadā guṇa-aikyam @parikalpya bhājyam/
children.translated_text: If the divisor is one and the multipliers are different, then, combining the multipliers as the dividend,

children.text: agra-aikyam agram kṛtas ukta-vat yas saṃśliṣṭa-saṃjñas sphuṭa-kuṭṭakas asau//
children.translated_text: The sum of the remainders as the addend, and performing [the operation] as stated before — that is called the combined <s>kuṭṭaka</s>.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: kas %pañca-nighnas vihṛtas %triṣaṣṭyā %sapta avaśeṣas atha sas eva rāśis/
children.translated_text: What [number], multiplied by five and divided by sixty-three, leaves a remainder of seven; and that same number,

children.text: %daśa-āhatas @syāt vihṛtas %triṣaṣṭyā %caturdaśa agras @vada rāśim enam//
children.translated_text: Multiplied by ten, when divided by sixty-three, leaves a remainder of fourteen — tell me that number!

children.text: atra guṇa-aikyam bhājyas/ agra-aikyam śuddhis iti/ nyāsas/ bhājyas 15 hāras 63 śudhis 21/ pūrva-vat jātas śuddhas guṇas 14// iti līlāvatyām kuṭṭaka-adhyāyas//
children.translated_text: Here the sum of multipliers is the dividend, the sum of remainders is the purification. Setting down: dividend 15, divisor 63, purification 21. As before, the purified multiplier obtained is 14. Thus ends the chapter on <s>kuṭṭaka</s> in the <s>Līlāvatī</s>.

body.text: aṅka-pāśa
body.translated_text: Digit-Patterns (<s>Aṅka-pāśa</s>)

body.text: atha aṅka-pāśas/ atha gaṇita-pāśe nirdiṣṭa-aṅkais saṃkhyāyās vibhede karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Now digit-patterns (<s>aṅka-pāśa</s>). Now, in the mathematical puzzle, the rule of operation for determining the number of permutations of specified digits, in a verse:

children.text: sthāna-antam %eka-ādi-caya-aṅka-ghātas saṃkhyā-vibhedās niyatais @syus aṅkais/
children.translated_text: The product of [numbers] beginning with one, with increment one, up to the number of places, gives the number of permutations with fixed digits;

children.text: bhaktas aṅka-mityā aṅka-samāsa-nighnas sthāneṣu yuktas miti-saṃyutis @syāt//
children.translated_text: Divided by the digit-count and multiplied by the digit-sum, placed at [each] position — that will be the sum of all permutations.

body.text: atra uddeśakas/
body.translated_text: Here the problem:

children.text: %dvika-%aṣṭakābhyām %tri-%nava-%aṣṭakais vā nirantaram %dvi-ādi-%nava-avasānais/
children.translated_text: With [the digits] two and eight, or with three, nine, and eight, or continuously with [digits] from two to nine,

children.text: saṃkhyā-vibhedās kati @saṃbhavanti tad-saṃkhyaka-aikyāni pṛthak @vada āśu//
children.translated_text: How many permutations are possible? And tell me quickly the sums of those [permutations] separately!

body.text: nyāsas/ 2/ 8/ atra sthāne 2 sthāna-antam %eka-ādi-caya-aṅkayos 1/ 2 ghātas 2 evam jātau saṃkhyā-bhedau 2/ atha sas eva ghātas aṅka-samāsa-10-nighnas 20 aṅka-mityā anayā 2 bhaktas 10 sthāna-%dvaye yuktas jātam saṃkhyā-aikyam 110// %dvitīya-udāharaṇe nyāsas/ 3/ 9/ 8/ atra %eka-ādi-caya-aṅkānām 1/ 2/ 3 ghātas 6 etāvantas saṃkhyā-bhedās/ atha sas eva ghātas 6/ aṅka-samāsa-20-āhatas 120 aṅka-mityā 3 bhaktas 40/ sthāna-%traye yuktas jātam saṃkhyā-aikyam 4440// %tṛtīya-udāharaṇe nyāsas/ 2/ 3/ 4/ 5/ 6/ 7/ 8/ 9/ evam atra saṃkhyā-bhedās %catvāriṃśat %sahasrāṇi %śata-%trayam %viṃśatis ca 40320/ samkhyā-aikyam ca %caturviṃśati-%nikharvāṇi %triṣaṣṭi-%padmāni n%avanavati-%koṭayas %navanavati-%lakṣāṇi %pañcasaptati-%sahasrāṇi %śata-%trayam %ṣaṣṭis ca 2463999975360// udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: 2, 8. Here, with 2 places, the product of numbers beginning with one with increment one, 1 × 2, is 2. Thus the number of permutations is 2. Now that same product multiplied by the digit-sum 10 and divided by the digit-count 2 gives 10; placed at two positions, the sum of permutations is 110. In the second example, setting down: 3, 9, 8. Here the product of 1 × 2 × 3 is 6; this many are the permutations. Now that same product 6, multiplied by the digit-sum 20, gives 120; divided by the digit-count 3, gives 40; placed at three positions, the sum of permutations is 4440. In the third example, setting down: 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. Thus the number of permutations here is forty thousand three hundred and twenty: 40,320. And the sum of permutations is twenty-four <s>nikharvas</s>, sixty-three <s>padmas</s>, ninety-nine <s>koṭis</s>, ninety-nine <s>lakṣas</s>, seventy-five thousand, three hundred and sixty: 2,463,999,975,360. Example:

children.text: pāśa-aṅkuśa-ahi-ḍamarūka-kapāla-śūlais khaṭvā-aṅga-śakti-śara-cāpa-yutais @bhavanti/
children.translated_text: With noose, goad, serpent, <s>ḍamaruka</s> (drum), skull-cup, trident, bed-post, spear, arrow, and bow, held in various hands — how many different forms arise

children.text: anyonya-hasta-kalitais kati mūrti-bhedās śaṃbhos hares iva gadā-ari-saras-ja-śaṅkhais//
children.translated_text: Of <s>Śambhu</s> (<s>Śiva</s>)? And similarly of <s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) with mace, discus, lotus, and conch?

body.text: nyāsas/ sthānāni 10/ jātās mūrti-bhedās 3628800/ evam hares ca 24// viśeṣa-karaṇa-sūtram vṛttam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: places 10. The number of different forms obtained is 3,628,800. Similarly for <s>Hari</s>: 24. The rule of operation for the special case, in a verse:

children.text: yāvat-sthāneṣu tulya-aṅkās tad-bhedais tu pṛthak kṛtais/
children.translated_text: When there are equal digits in however many places, dividing by the [respective] permutations of those [equal digits] separately,

children.text: prāk-bhedās vihṛtās bhedās tad-saṃkhyā-aikyam ca pūrva-vat//
children.translated_text: The previous permutations divided [by those] give the [actual] permutations; and the sum of those permutations is as before.

body.text: atra uddeśakas/
body.translated_text: Here the problem:

children.text: %dvi-%dvi-%eka-#bhū-parimitais kati saṃkhyakās @syus tāsām yutis ca gaṇaka āśu mama @pracakṣva/
children.translated_text: With [digits] limited to two, two, one, and one — how many numbers are there? And what is their sum? O calculator, tell me quickly!

children.text: #ambhodhi-#kumbhi-#śara-#bhūta-#śarais tathā aṅkais ced aṅka-pāśam iti yukti-viśāradas @asi//
children.translated_text: And similarly with the digits four, four, five, five, five — if you are skilled in the art of digit-patterns, [tell me]!

body.text: nyāsas/ 2/ 2/ 1/ 1/ atra prāk-vat bhedās 24/ yāvat-sthāneṣu tulya-aṅkās iti atra %prathamam tāvat sthāna-%dvaye tulyau/ prāk-vat sthāna-%dvayāt jātau bhedau 2/ punar atra api sthāna-%dvaye tulyau/ tatra api evam bhedau 2/ bhedābhyām prāk-bhedās 24 bhaktās jātās bhedās 6/ tat yathā 2211/ 2121/ 2112/ 1212/ 1221/ 1122/ pūrva-vat saṃkhyā-aikyam ca 9999// %dvitīya-udāharaṇe nyāsas/ 4/ 8/ 5/ 5/ 5/ atra api pūrva-vat bhedās 120/ sthāna-%traya-uttha-bhedais 6 bhaktās jātās 20/ tat yathā 48555/ 84555/ 54855/ 58455/ 55485/ 55845/ 55548/ 55584/ 45855/ 45585/ 45558/ 85455/ 85545/ 85554/ 54585/ 58545/ 55458/ 55854/ 54558/ 58554/ evam viṃśatis/ atha saṃkhyā-aikyam ca 1199988// aniyata-aṅkais atulyais ca vibhede karaṇa-sūtram vṛtta-%ardham/
body.translated_text: Setting down: 2/ 2/ 1/ 1/ Here, as before, the permutations are 24. [Since there are] equal digits in certain places: here, first, there are equal digits in two places. As before, from the two places, the permutations generated are 2. Again here too, there are equal digits in two places. There too, likewise, the permutations are 2. The previous permutations 24, divided by the [products of] permutations [of equal digits], give the [distinct] permutations as 6. They are: 2211/ 2121/ 2112/ 1212/ 1221/ 1122/ As before, the sum of the numbers is also 9999.

body.text: sthāna-antam %eka-apacita-antima-aṅka-ghātas asama-aṅkais ca miti-prabhedās// [āpaṭe: -antimaṅka- < -antima-aṅka-]
body.translated_text: The rule of operation for permutations with unequal and unrestricted digits, in a half-verse: The product of [integers from] the last digit down to one, decreasing by one up to [the number of] places, gives the number of permutations with unequal digits.

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: sthāna-%ṣaṭka-sthitais aṅkais anyonyam #khena varjitais/
children.translated_text: With digits placed in six positions, each different from the others and excluding zero—

children.text: kati saṃkhyā-vibhedās @syus yadi @vetsi @nigadyatām//
children.translated_text: how many number-permutations would there be? If you know, tell me!

body.text: nyāsas 9/ 8/ 7/ 6/ 5/ 4/ eṣām ghāte jātās saṃkhyā-bhedās 60480// anyat karaṇa-sūtram vṛtta-%dvayam/
body.translated_text: Setting down: 9/ 8/ 7/ 6/ 5/ 4/ Their product gives the number-permutations as 60480. Another rule of operation in two verses:

children.text: nis-%ekam aṅka-aikyam idam nis-%eka-sthāna-antam %eka-apacitam vibhaktam/
children.translated_text: The sum of the digits less one, [placed in a row] ending with the number of places less one, decreasing by one, divided

children.text: #rūpa-ādibhis tad-nihatais samās @syus saṃkhyā-vibhedās niyate aṅka-yoge//
children.translated_text: by one, etc.—those [quotients], multiplied together, give the number-permutations when the sum of the digits is fixed.

children.text: %nava-anvita-sthānaka-saṃkhyakāyās ūne aṅka-yoge kathitam tu vedyam/
children.translated_text: When the sum of the digits is less [than the number of places plus nine], the stated [method] should be known with the number of places increased by nine.

body.text: l 269c/ saṃkṣiptam uktam pṛthutā-bhayena na antas @asti yasmāt gaṇita-arṇavasya//
body.translated_text: This has been stated briefly, out of fear of prolixity; for there is no end to the ocean of mathematics!

body.text: udāharaṇam/
body.translated_text: Example:

children.text: %pañca-sthāna-sthitais aṅkais yad-yad-yogas %trayodaśa/
children.translated_text: With digits placed in five positions, [such that] their sum is thirteen—

children.text: kati-bhedā @bhavet saṃkhyā yadi @vetsi @nigadyatām//
children.translated_text: how many permutations of numbers would there be? If you know, tell me!

body.text: atra aṅka-aikyam 13/ nis-%ekam 12 etat nis-%eka-sthāna-antam %eka-apacitam %eka-ādibhis ca bhaktam jātam 12_1/ 11_2/ 10_3/ 9_4/ eṣām ghātais samās jātās saṃkhyā-bhedās 495//
body.translated_text: Here the sum of digits is 13. Less one: 12. This, [forming a sequence] decreasing by one [ending at] the number of places less one, divided by one, etc., gives: 12/1, 11/2, 10/3, 9/4. The product of these gives the number-permutations as 495.

children.text: na guṇas na haras na kṛtis na ghanas pṛṣṭas tathā api duṣṭānām/
children.translated_text: Neither multiplication, nor division, nor squaring, nor cubing is asked; yet for the wicked,

children.text: garvita-gaṇaka-baṭūnām @syāt pātas avaśyam aṅka-pāśe asmin//
children.translated_text: arrogant young student-mathematicians, a fall will surely come in this net of digits (<s>aṅka-pāśa</s>)!

body.text: iti līlāvatyām aṅka-pāśas/
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the section on the Net of Digits (<s>aṅka-pāśa</s>) in the <s>Līlāvatī</s>.

body.text: grantha-samāpti
body.translated_text: Conclusion of the work

children.text: yeṣām su-jāti-guṇa-varga-vibhūṣita-aṅgī śuddhā akhila-vyavahṛtis khalu kaṇṭha-saktā/
children.translated_text: For those whose limbs are adorned by the noble class of virtues, whose entire computation is pure and held close to the heart—

children.text: līlāvatī iha sa-rasa-uktim udāharantī teṣām sadā eva sukha-saṃpad @upaiti vṛddhim//
children.translated_text: the <s>Līlāvatī</s>, presenting examples with delightful expressions, [ensures that] for them, the prosperity of happiness always increases!

body.text: iti śrī-bhāskara-ācārya-viracite siddhānta-śiromaṇau līlāvatī-saṃjñas pāṭī-adhyāyas saṃpūrṇas//
body.translated_text: Thus ends the chapter called <s>Līlāvatī</s>, [being] the chapter on arithmetic (<s>pāṭī</s>), in the <s>Siddhānta-śiromaṇi</s> composed by the illustrious teacher <s>Bhāskara</s>.

body.text: End of part two in Apate
body.translated_text: End of part two in <s>Āpaṭe</s>'s edition
